A UK-funded climate project in Bangladesh is being forced to close two years early after foreign aid cuts, leaving thousands of vulnerable people without support and threatening to undo work that has already been carried out, The Independent has learnt.

The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) is in the middle of a programme of cuts to the foreign aid budget, which is set to see the UK aid budget fall from 0.5 per cent to 0.3 per cent of Gross National Income. With a number of developing countries seeing their UK aid relationships all-but eliminated , the cuts have been labelled a “ moral catastrophe ”, with many observers particularly dismayed at the decision to cut UK aid for climate projects .

One organisation impacted is British development charity Practical Action. Since 2023, the charity has been managing part of a major development project in Bangladesh , which is aiming to transform the lives of tens of thousands of people through interventions including solar power systems , climate-resilient agriculture and aquaculture feedstocks and technologies, and weather information systems that can provide early warnings for extreme rainfall and cyclones .

Situated in Bangladesh’s Sundarbans – the world’s largest tidal mangrove forest, much of which is UNESCO World Heritage Site – Practical Action’s project launched in 2023, and was expected to run until 2028.

In April 2026, however, the charity was told it would have to end its project in June of this year, according to Tamanna Rahman, climate resilience lead for Practical Action Bangladesh. That deadline was later extended to September, after intense lobbying from the charity, she says.

Practical Action was supposed to have received £2.2m by 2026, but ended up receiving “far less than this”, says Rahma. The project was supposed to reach 57,000 people by the end of this year, but will in the end only reach 37,000 people.

“This abrupt cut has threatened our reputation in the community, which we have carefully built up over the past two and a half years,” Rahma says. “It has also impacted the long-term stability of the interventions that we have made, and limited our ability to plan for an effective exit.”

The cut to Practical Action’s project forms a fraction of overall cuts to the UK-Bangladesh bilateral aid programme, which, it was revealed in July , is set to fall in value from £66.7 million to £31m between 2025/6 and 2026/7.

The early exit has also been damaging due to the fact that the target communities need as much support as possible to adapt to the climate crisis, Rahma adds.

“Every year we are seeing more severe storms and cyclones, while the sea is rising and soil is becoming salinated,” she says. “There is huge demand for financing such as this, yet the ability to make these kinds of tangible programmatic interventions is declining.”

Commenting in response to Practical Action’s concerns, Labour MP and chair of the International Development Committee Sarah Champion said: “If projects such as this are being ended two years early with short notice, it begs serious questions about the UK's commitment to supporting low-income countries as they respond to climate change.

“What’s more, this kind of action is likely to represent poor value for money for the UK taxpayer and damage the UK’s reputation as a reliable partner in the response to climate change.”

3cm sea level rise per year

Situated on the Ganges Delta - where the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers converge before flowing into the Bay of Bengal - the Sundarbans is a vast 10,277km² mangrove forest. It is home to 42 mammal species, including endangered tigers and river dolphins, as well as nearly 300 species of birds.

The communities supported by Practical Action live on the fringes of this unique ecological area, and have traditionally depended on the forest for products including fish, firewood and honey. Many now also farm, but widespread illiteracy and their isolation from the wider Bangladeshi economy leave them among the country’s most marginalised communities.

Many also continue to suffer the after-effects of Cyclone Aila, which affected an estimated 100,000 people when it hit the Sundarbans in 2009, destroying local infrastructure and completely changing the landscape in parts.

The Sundarbans also faces a sea level rise of roughly 3cm per year - around double the global average - with the rapid rising displacing communities and ruining once-fertile soil.

open image in gallery Bina Mondal, a villager supported by Practical Action, who recalls how Cyclone Aila in 2009 washed away embankments and effectively ended villagers’ ability to farm ( Practical Action )

Bina Mondal recalls how her village, Kalabogi, once had wide roads, productive farms, and fruit trees. After Cyclone Aila, roads and embankments washed away, and fishing is now the only viable source of income for the family.

Fresh water is now hard to come by except through rainwater harvesting, while smaller and smaller catches from the delta mean the family’s income becomes ever-more stretched. The family often cooks only one meal per day, and healthcare is currently out of reach.

A small solar panel provided by Practical Action has provided massive support as she struggles to make ends meet. “I can continue working after dark, and this has helped me earn more,” she says. “Before the project started, we were earning around 2,000 to 3,000 taka (£12-18 per month) from fishing, but this year we are earning around 4,000 to 5,000 taka.”

Another villager supported by Practical Action over the past two and a half years is Bashonti Mondal, who received a new solar-powered rice-husking machine. Previously, she says, she travelled from farm to farm each day looking for work from local landowners. Now, she can earn a higher income from home, while having more time to support her children.

open image in gallery Bashonti Mondal, who Practical Action supported with a solar-powered rice-husking machine, before the closure of its project in the Sundarbans ( Practical Action )

Aid workers at the charity report how, when the early closure of the project was announced, some members of communities cried, while other people were confused as to why support was ending just as interventions were beginning to bear fruit.

Interventions that will essentially go to waste include a scheme to support a pool of 140 entrepreneurs, who have been given 50,000 taka each, and have received initial project coaching. Leaving them now will bring them back to “ground zero”, however, as they have been provided with a “bare minimum understanding of markets”, says Practical Action’s Rahma.

“Having two to three months' notice to wrap things up when it was very clear that the project was to continue until December 2028 has been very difficult,” says Rahma. “Practical always has a proper exit plan that involves community coaching and a hand-over of interventions to the local government - but this time we have not been able to fully do this.”

No time to find new funding

Rahma is clear-sighted that – in a country of 170m people – it is unrealistic to expect grants from foreign governments to lift everyone in need out of poverty. The current shift by donor countries like the UK to drive in capital through new kinds of partnerships with private investors is understandable in that sense, she says.

“At the same time, when we are talking about the most marginalised and vulnerable here in Bangladesh, it is very hard to see how private capital can come,” says Rahma. “People do not have any significant monetary income to speak of, and transportation and infrastructure remains virtually non-existent due to Cyclone Aila, which took place as long ago as 2009.”

Rahma’s concerns have been echoed by other NGOs. Last year, for example, the NGO Mercy Corps warned that only three per cent of adaptation finance needs in developing countries have so far been met by the private sector, with interventions like flood defences typically considered a “public good” that require government money to be built.

Romily Greenhill, CEO of UK development charity network Bond, commented: "The cancellation of UK-funded humanitarian and climate adaptation programmes lays bare the harsh reality of Labour's short-sighted UK aid cuts, and represents a lifeline lost to communities already suffering the worst impacts of conflict, poverty and climate crisis worldwide.”

She added that the new Labour leadership of prime minister Andy Burnham and foreign secretary Ed Miliband have an opportunity to “change course” and restore the country’s “shattered reputation on international development”.

“We urge the new prime minister and foreign secretary to definitively rule out further cuts to the UK aid budget, set out a roadmap for returning UK aid to 0.7 per cent of GNI, and ensure that high-quality international climate finance is protected,” she said.

open image in gallery An aerial photograph of a river winding through the Sundarbans in Bangladesh ( AFP/Getty )

Rahma suggests that signals from FCDO in its new development strategy show that there is a desire to move away from giving money to NGOs like Practical Action, to provide more support directly to the governments of developing countries. “But I have concerns here, as the government has not traditionally had the manpower, the capacity, and skills to access hard-to-reach communities like those living in the forests of the Sundarbans,” she says.

Practical Action has been looking to find grant-funding from foundations to fill the gap left by FCDO, however, the short notice on the closure of the project has hindered such efforts.

“As Practical Action, we do not wish to talk negatively about FCDO, and we continue to work with them across Asia, Africa and Latin America,” says Rahma. “We continue to need sustainable, long-term grant finance to be able to reach the most vulnerable communities who we are trying to support.”

In response to concerns raised in this article, an FCDO spokesperson said: "Climate is an urgent national security threat, and the Foreign Secretary will be bringing his international leadership on this topic to FCDO.

“We are transitioning away from spending high levels of grant ODA [Official development assistance], but our ambition and effort will remain high - our bilateral programmes will focus on partnerships with governments to strengthen systems, leverage finance and move away from reliance on aid.”

Police in India’s western state of Maharashtra filed a case against Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the viral Indian youth protest movement Cockroach Janta Party, after he carried out a surprise inspection of a government-run school.

Officials said an initial legal complaint was filed at the Ausa police station in Maharashtra by a teacher, Sayyed Shamshadbano Khairatali, of the local Zilla Parishad Urdu school.

The complainant stated that the prominent youth leader entered a government school without permission, disrupted official work, and threatened the teachers.

Mr Dipke, 30, had been pressing the Indian government at the federal and state level to fix run-down, state-run educational institutions that provide free or subsidised education to millions of Indian students from all economic backgrounds.

open image in gallery Abhijeet Dipke announces the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan while addressing supporters at Jantar Mantar in Delhi ( Getty )

He led a rare successful campaign against the federal education minister Dharmendra Pradhan in June this year, after 21 students died by suicide over question paper leak of a prestigious medical competitive exam. The charged Gen-Z-led campaign resulted in the resignation – a primary demand from Mr Dipke’s movement – of the federal minister in July.

Mr Dipke has since then been visiting government-run schools in his home state Maharashtra to highlight the deficiencies faced by the students.

The complainant claimed that Mr Dipke and his team entered the school without permission, sat among students, enquired about the problems they were facing, which he said caused obstruction to educational and government work.

He added that the CJP founder filmed his interaction with the students and shared it on his social media accounts.

One of the videos purportedly shows students at the school accidentally revealing they were brought in from another school nearby to show that the school the CJP leader was visiting had an active classroom. Mr Dipke is seen expressing shock. Officials from the school are yet to respond to this allegation.

The complainant claimed the school was defamed by Mr Dipke over the incident. He said Mr Dipke called for the suspension of teachers behind the incident.

open image in gallery Police stand guard outside the home of Abhijeet Dipke, head of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, India, August 4, 2026. REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas ( Reuters )

Police officials have filed charges of assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty, trespassing, criminal intimidation and criminal defamation under the Indian penal code.

However, Mr Dipke has continued his campaign and on Monday asked education ministers across Indian states to present data on government school infrastructure, teacher vacancies, and funding.

“It has been 80 years since India gained independence, yet children in many government schools still do not have access to safe drinking water, functional washrooms, proper classrooms, or even something as basic as benches to sit on. No child should be forced to study in such conditions,” the Boston University graduate said in a letter shared on his social media accounts.

“They are being treated worse than animals,” he said, adding that his campaign was “not about politics or any one government", but focused on the “future of our children.”

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

Sports.title: ‘Hope he clears his head’ – Man Utd target Alejandro Balde axed as Barcelona boss speaks out on £25million transfer exit
Sports.content:
BARCELONA boss Hansi Flick has opened the door for Alejandro Balde to leave the club after dropping the Manchester United target from his squad for their La Liga opener.

The Spanish left-back was left out of Barcelona‘s matchday squad for the 5-0 win over Elche, with Flick admitting Balde is not currently “100 per cent” and needs to “clear his head”.



However, Balde has not been axed from first-team training and remains with the Barcelona squad as the club considers his future.

The 22-year-old is understood to be available for around £25million, with Premier League interest in his services.



Flick has options at left-back following the arrival of Joao Cancelo, while Gerard Martin can also operate in the position.

That has left Balde facing an uncertain future at the Nou Camp, with Barcelona prepared to listen to offers before the transfer window closes.



Flick said before the Elche game: “I spoke with him this morning, to be honest. I think he’s not at 100%, that he’s not here, and that’s why I’ve decided to leave him in Barcelona.

“I hope he clears his head, and we’ll see what happens on Monday.”

Balde’s omission was significant given he has already found himself slipping down the pecking order under Flick.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Barcelona boss has made it clear that Cancelo is currently his preferred option at left-back, while Martin provides further competition.



Barcelona are also facing a crucial final week of the transfer window, with departures expected to dictate whether they can make further additions.

Balde is one of several players whose futures are being assessed, alongside Marc Casado and Hector Fort, who were also left out of the squad to face Elche.

If Balde does depart, Barcelona could look to strengthen elsewhere, with a left-footed centre-back potentially on their shopping list.



Sporting defender Goncalo Inacio has emerged as a possible target.

The 24-year-old has already established himself at the highest level and was part of Portugal‘s squad for the 2026 World Cup.

Barcelona sporting director Deco has been in Lisbon in recent days, fuelling speculation that talks over Inacio could be progressing.

His arrival could allow Martin to return to his more natural left-back role and compete with Cancelo.

Manchester United have been monitoring the situation, although their interest in Balde comes alongside their continued admiration for Arsenal youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

United remain interested in Lewis-Skelly, but a move for the Arsenal star currently looks unlikely.

With the transfer window entering its final days, Balde’s future could now become one of the key stories to watch as Barcelona decide whether to cash in on the highly-rated defender.

Sports.title: Gary Neville fears Premier League manager could walk away after ONE GAME with ‘heart ripped out’ of club
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE has said that he is ‘nervous’ about Unai Emery walking away from his role as Aston Villa boss.

The Spanish tactician led Villa to their second Champions League campaign in three years last season, winning the Europa League on top of securing a fourth-place finish.



But his side came crashing down to earth after a number of his best stars were sold in the summer window.

Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Lucas Digne and Youri Tielemans were among the names that left the club, many of whom going to Premier League rivals.



Those departures told as they suffered a 4-0 opening day loss to Brighton, with their marquee signing Joao Gomes being sent off in the first half just minutes after giving the ball away for the fourth goal.

Fans were damning in their assessment of Villa’s barebones side, and now Manchester United legend Neville has expressed concerns about Emery’s state of mind.

He said on the Gary Neville podcast: “The goals that Villa conceded were horrific. But you looked at the Villa team as it was announced, and you looked at the Villa bench, and you were like, ‘they’ve had the heart ripped out of it.’

“You talk about who’s left – Tielemans, Rogers, Konsa. Talk about the heart being ripped out of Newcastle’s midfield. I mean, the experience that they’ve lost there. And there’s this peculiar thing going on at the moment with PSR, and sort of no one knows where the money is. It’s all over the shop, isn’t it?

“And so Villa will be sat there. Villa’s fans will be sat there. They’ve got an outstanding manager, and the big thing that I was thinking during that match at 4-0 was, ‘they’ve got to keep Unai Emery‘. Is Unai Emery going to think ‘Hang on a minute, I can’t be associated with this’?”

The manager was clearly fuming during the break and stormed down his tunnel after the match without shaking his opposite number’s hand.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Villa are primed to do some more transfer business, with goalkeeper signing Zion Suzuki ready to come into the fold and free agent Leon Goretzka nearing a deal.

But as Ollie Watkins looks increasingly likely to leave, and Emiliano Martinez clearly out of Emery’s plans, Villa seem a way off being able to compete in the Prem or Champions League.

Neville continued: “Hopefully (he stays), because I really want Villa to do well, and I want Unai Emery to stay there because I think I love the idea of different teams breaking into the Champions League places. Watching Villa in the last couple of seasons has been a joy.

“I just love Emery and the way he works, the way his teams play. It’s great to see them, from where they were 10 years ago when they were in the Championship.



“It’s a brilliant journey that they’ve been on, and sort of getting into this position. But this could go like that quite quickly. They’ve got to hold on to the manager. They’ve somehow got to get some players in this week.

“Villa are in a great position. They’re going to have a lot of good games this season. That was a shock seeing that. Well done to Brighton, but that was a big shock. And my immediate nervousness for Aston Villa is keeping their manager.”

Sports.title: Out-of-position gift Maxim De Cuyper dominates Dream Team on opening weekend
Sports.content:
MAXIM DE CUYPER (£3.5m) earned more points than any other Dream Team player over the first weekend of the new Premier League season.

The Belgium international banked 18 points as Brighton blitzed Aston Villa at the Amex on Sunday.

De Cuyper’s mega haul emphatically illustrates what is possible when players are deployed out of position.



The 25-year-old is a full-back by trade, hence why he’s categorised as a defender in Dream Team, but Fabian Hurzeler selected him as a left winger for the Seagulls’ opener, a decision that yielded tremendous results.



Key players Kaoru Mitoma (£4m) and Yankuba Minteh (£4m) are sidelined with injury at present and so most expected De Cuyper to be pushed forward against the Villains — he fulfilled the same role a few times last season.

The hosts’ No29 could hardly have been higher up the pitch for Brighton’s first goal.

He anticipated a wayward pass from Paul Torres (£3.5m) and forced Victor Lindelof (£3m) into an own goal to register a fantasy assist in just the eighth minute.



10 ten minutes later, De Cuyper got the goal he deserved when he popped up in the six-yard box like a seasoned poacher to convert Georginio Rutter’s (£3.5m) low cross.

Jack Hinshelwood (£3.5m) scored a quickfire brace soon after as Unai Emery’s side fell apart in a disastrous first half for the visitors.

The adaptable 21-year-old notched 17 points for his efforts and is currently second in the overall rankings at this embryonic stage of the campaign.



De Cuyper leads the way because he’s classified as a defender and therefore claimed his share of the clean sheet points from the 4-0 victory.

If the former Club Brugge man is going to continue as Brighton’s starting left winger – and why not after this impressive performance – then Dream Team managers would be wise to consider whether they are able to accommodate him.

At the time of writing De Cuyper features in just 0.9% of teams — very few gaffers benefited from his 18-point masterclass.

Mats Wieffer (£3.5m) also cashed in with a double-digit return of 12 points courtesy of three bonus points and four tackles (two points) on top of his clean sheet.



As for Aston Villa, the red flags are impossible to ignore.

Lindelof, Torres, Matty Cash (£4m) and Joao Gomes (£3.5m) all registered minus points on the day — the latter was sent off for violent conduct and will now serve a three-game domestic ban.

Lucas Digne, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers have already exited this summer with Ollie Watkins (£5m) and Emi Martinez (£4m) expected to follow suit in the coming days.

Gameweek 2 is unlikely to bring reprieve as champions Arsenal are due at Villa Park next Monday.

Dream Team bosses would be advised to stay well clear of Villa until the outlook improves significantly.

Sports.title: Man Utd still hopeful Arsenal can be persuaded to sell Myles Lewis-Skelly as they seek left-back for Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED are still hopeful Arsenal could be persuaded to sell Myles Lewis-Skelly despite his recent starts.

Lewis-Skelly, 19, has generated interest from United and Chelsea but lined up in Arsenal’s 3-0 Community Shield and Premier League triumphs against Manchester City and Coventry.



Well-placed sources said Lewis-Skelly’s starting role is partly due to Martin Zubimendi’s struggles and the late return of Mikel Merino, who appeared in Spain’s World Cup final victory.

Arsenal value Lewis-Skelly north of £50million and the unlikeliness of a club meeting their asking price has fuelled Mikel Arteta’s confidence in keeping the academy graduate.



Arteta said he was “100 per cent” certain that Lewis-Skelly would stay.

Lewis-Skelly started in only two Premier League matches before the final month of last season amid Arteta’s reservations about his lack of maturity.



But he ended up starting in the Champions League semi-final second leg win against Atletico Madrid and the final loss to Paris Saint-Germain.

United want to bring in a left back before the 11pm transfer deadline on September 1 but feel Lewis-Skelly is overpriced.

The versatile Arsenal starlet can play left-back as well as central midfield, where he has started this season for the Gunners.

Newcastle left back Lewis Hall was United’s prime target but the Magpies took measures to dampen talk of a move.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Hall, 21, would be keen on making the switch but Newcastle have already sold Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes for nearly £250m.

United belatedly decided to move for a left back after Barcelona passed on their option to buy Marcus Rashford.

Luke Shaw is into his 13th season at United and has entered the final year of his contract, which does not include the option of an additional year.

United are prepared to sell 19-year-old left back Harry Amass, who was involved during pre-season but failed to make the bench for the 2-0 defeat at Hull City on Saturday.



Patrick Dorgu, initially signed as a left wing back, can play at left back while right backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have also both played on the opposite side.

United were breached by two set pieces in their opening Premier League loss to Hull. Hull manager Sergej Jakirović revealed that they had targeted United’s set-up at dead-ball kicks in their final pre-match training session on Friday.

Sports.title: Barcelona fans give immediate Anthony Gordon verdict after LaLiga debut cameo and even want him to bench Lamine Yamal
Sports.content:
ANTHONY GORDON wasted no time making his mark on Barcelona, and fans have already been left dreaming about what he can do this season.

The England winger came off the bench for his professional Barcelona debut and first La Liga appearance last night as the Catalan giants raced towards a huge 5-0 victory away at Elche.

Gordon was introduced in the 65th minute, replacing superstar Lamine Yamal with Barca already 2-0 ahead.



Raphinha had opened the scoring in the first half before Karim Adeyemi doubled the advantage on the stroke of half-time, with the German also making his own Barcelona debut after arriving from Borussia Dortmund.



But Gordon needed just two minutes to announce himself.

The £70million summer signing from Newcastle picked up possession and immediately showed his attacking instincts, sliding a clever pass through for Raphinha to race onto and fire home his second of the night.

But the 25-year-old was not finished there as just four minutes later, he latched onto a superb through ball from Pedri before using his searing pace to eat up the ground in behind.



Rather than go for glory himself, Gordon kept his head and squared for Fermín Lopez, who tapped home to put Barca 4-0 up.

Fermín then added another 11 minutes from time.

It represented a dream debut for the former Newcastle star, who had the perfect introduction to life at one of the biggest clubs in world football.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS



The reaction from supporters told the story.

One fan wrote: “Anthony Gordon really said ‘remember my name’ on his Barcelona debut. What a cameo.”

Another was full of praise for his involvement in Fermín’s goal, saying: “Anthony Gordon so unselfish as he gifts Fermin Lopez that’s goal to tap in.”

But one supporter went considerably further with their verdict.

They sensationally posted: “Might have to bench Yamal for Gordon until he can figure it out.”



That may be a tongue-in-cheek reaction, but it underlines just how quickly Gordon has captured the imagination of Barcelona supporters.

The winger arrived from Newcastle for £70m this summer, with Barca looking to add more depth and explosiveness in attack following the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and Marcus Rashford returning to parent club Manchester United.

They also brought in Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund for just £19m, with the German viewed as another option behind Yamal and Raphinha.

That depth was needed after Rashford filled a similar role last season and enjoyed an impressive campaign.



The England forward finished with 14 goals and 14 assists in all competitions, while also getting regular opportunities as Raphinha endured an injury-interrupted campaign.

But Barca’s record with and without their Brazilian winger was particularly revealing.

When Raphinha started last season, Barcelona won 24 of their 27 games, drawing two and losing just one.

Without him in the starting XI, their record dropped dramatically.

In the 30 matches Raphinha did not start, Barca won 20, drew one and lost NINE.



Teenage sensation Yamal, meanwhile, established himself as the club’s talisman – scoring 24 goals in all competitions last season and finishing as Barcelona’s top scorer.

That makes Gordon’s task of forcing his way into the starting XI even more difficult.

If Raphinha and Yamal remain fit, there is little doubt that starting regularly out wide will be an enormous challenge for Gordon.

But he has already shown exactly why Barcelona were willing to spend £70m on him.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Barca already have a winning feeling inside the squad having won the last two La Liga titles, toppling Real Madrid in doing so.

If Hansi Flick is to win a third in a row this season and in doing so match Pep Guardiola‘s feat between 2008/09 and 2010/11, Gordon has a big part to play.

Sports.title: Why Celtic, Rangers, Hearts, Hibs, Motherwell face a make-or-break week
Sports.content:
All five of Scotland's European representatives are still standing as we prepare for the second legs of the play-off rounds, but only Celtic are guaranteed UEFA league phase action.

They have the cushion of Europa League football if they throw away their commanding lead against LASK in their Champions League tie, but there is no such comfort for Hearts, Rangers, Hibs and Motherwell.

The Jambos have already failed in their bid to qualify for Europe's top two club competitions, and need to win away to Rapid Vienna to secure a place in the Conference League.

Rangers are in the same situation, having crashed out of Europa League qualifying, meaning a place in the third-tier competition is their only chance.

Both Hibs and Motherwell have already come through two Conference League qualifying rounds. The Easter Road side are in a far better position than the Steelmen ahead of this week's games...

Will Celtic secure Champions League return?

Image: Celtic take a commanding lead into the second leg of their Champions League play-off

Just 12 months ago, Celtic failed to score in 210 minutes against Kairat Almaty before crashing out at the play-off stage on penalties.

What followed was a season of turmoil before Martin O'Neill returned to win a league and cup double. Now he has the Hoops on the brink of a return to Europe's elite competition.

The Champions League is all about big players producing big moments. Benjamin Nygren and Camilo Duran served up goals of the highest quality at a packed Parkhead to give them a commanding 3-0 first-leg win against LASK.

Image: Camilo Duran scored a stunning double against LASK

Duran scored five goals in the competition last season for Qarabag, and he is already proving he was worth the £6m fee.

The Colombian striker has pace and skill, and looked at home on the big stage. Fellow summer signings Mika Baur and Kasper Hogh also shone, with early suggestions this might be the summer the Hoops got their signings right.

Let's not forget Nygren, Celtic's top scorer last season. He opened the scoring, taking his tally for the season to four goals in four games.

O'Neill did urge some caution ahead of Tuesday night's game, with LASK showing enough to suggest it is not done yet.

If Celtic impress in attack again while avoiding any defensive lapses, the famous Champions League anthem will be back in Glasgow until after Christmas.

Can Hearts take another step towards becoming European regulars?

Tony Bloom has made no secret of his high hopes for Hearts.

The minority shareholder has already managed to split the Old Firm, and he has the Champions League in his sights.

Firstly, they have to qualify for the league phase of European tournaments regularly, and the Conference League is in their sights.

Image: James Wilson celebrates his goal against Rapid Vienna in the Conference League play-off first leg

Having failed to get past Sturm Graz in Champions League qualifying and Benfica in the Europa, they can still secure a place in the third-tier competition.

The Jambos take a 2-2 draw to Austria for the second leg of their play-off against Rapid Vienna on Wednesday night. To get through, they need to find their balance between attack and defence.

They have conceded 15 goals in European competition this season while scoring just four times.

The reward for that will be participation in the main phase of the Conference League for the third time in five seasons and, with it, a financial boost of at least £4m.

Can Rangers take last European chance?

Image: Ryan Naderi scored Rangers only going against Jablonec at Ibrox

Rangers manager Derek McInnes admitted his side will need to "be better" after their narrow 1-0 win against Jablonec in the first leg of their play-off.

Failure to reach the Europa League means the best the Ibrox side can achieve in Europe this season is the Conference League, a competition they have never played in before.

The boos rang out after a frustrating first half at Ibrox, but they did turn to cheers with Ryan Naderi's goal giving them hope heading into the second leg in the Czech Republic.

They did not make it easy for themselves, especially after Cammy Devlin's straight red card minutes after coming on, but the visitors never really troubled them.

Rangers dominated possession and had 13 shots on target compared to the opposition's five.

The fans will be hoping their failure to take chances does not cost them in the return leg as they aim to secure a ninth straight season competing on the European stage.

Historic season for Hibs?

Image: Hibs secured a goalless draw away to Gent

Hibernian are on the brink of club history - a first European league phase qualification.

A goalless draw away to Gent in the first leg of their Conference League tie has left them on the brink of securing a place in the league phase of the competition.

After beating KF Malisheva, and then seeing off North Macedonian outfit Shkendija over two legs, David Gray's side face the final hurdle of qualifying for the second straight season. Last season, they lost out to Legia Warsaw after extra time.

Image: Owen Elding missed an early penalty for Hibs

Hibs dealt well with the pressure in the away leg against Gent but were left to rue Owen Elding's first-half penalty miss.

The Belgian side, who have started their Pro League season with back-to-back wins, failed to pose any great threat to the Hibees, who will return to Leith believing this is their season.

Too late for Motherwell?

Image: Regan Charles-Cook gave Motherwell a dream start against Freiburg

When Regan Charles-Cook fired Motherwell ahead just two minutes into their tie against Freiburg, the Fir Park faithful probably started to dream of their first appearance in the group stage of European competition.

They caught the Germans out. However, when their opponents finally found their feet, they showed their own version of the attractive, free-flowing football the 'Well fans have become accustomed to under boss Alfred Johansson and his predecessor Jens Berthel Askou.

Image: It was a tough night for Motherwell against Freiburg in the first-leg of their play-off

Having reached last year's Europa League final, Freiburg spent a reported £30m in the close season and are one of those backed to go far in the competition.

They kept Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen busy. He impressed, but they still fell to a 3-1 defeat.

Freiburg were certainly worthy winners in Lanarkshire and will be overwhelming favourites to complete the job at the Europa-Park Stadion on Thursday.

Sports.title: Alvarez booed by Atletico fans amid Arsenal interest - so will he leave?
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez was booed by Atletico Madrid supporters on Sunday after all the transfer window noise around him - does that mean a move to Barcelona or Arsenal is any closer?

The Argentine forward cut a disappointed figure when his own fans turned on him during Atleti's 2-2 draw with Villarreal.

And with Arsenal and Barcelona circling ahead of the September 1 deadline, what will happen now? Here is a state of play about the forward's future...

What happened with Alvarez on Sunday?

Alvarez played his first Atletico Madrid match on Sunday after revealing his desire to leave the club during the World Cup.

The Argentine striker wants to leave Diego Simeone's side to join Barcelona. However, Arsenal are also interested in bringing the former Man City striker back to the Premier League.

Barcelona want Alvarez but earlier this summer, Atletico accused the Catalan club of building a "relentless smear campaign" regarding the forward.

"Over the past few months, we've been subjected to a relentless smear campaign against one of our players," wrote Atleti on X.

"Calculated leaks, fake news, constant disrespect, the culé version of the propaganda machine inventing little stories, phone calls before head-to-head clashes.

"But of course, it would never occur to us either to have the vice president of referees on the payroll or to rely on political favours to register players. Respect and values."

With Alvarez wanting to join one of Atleti's closest rivals, the forward was greeted by whistles, boos and jeers from the Atletico Madrid fans on his return to action for the club.

His named was booed as the Atleti team was read out - and Alvarez was sat on the substitutes bench when the first jeers of the afternoon were made. They continued when Alvarez entered the pitch on the 66th minute.

After the game, the Argentina international left the field on his own after the 2-2 home league draw against Villarreal, while his team-mates stayed behind to applaud the fans.

Image: Alvarez was booed by his own supporters on Sunday - and walked off the pitch while his team-mates applauded the crowd

Asked about the situation, Simeone said in his post-match press conference: "People at the club told me that the club decided he shouldn't be near the stands and the fans.

"The decision was made by the club to keep him away and separate him from the rest of the team, so he would come to the locker room instead."

Does this raise Arsenal's chances of signing him?

Just because Alvarez was booed by his own Atletico supporters on Sunday, does not mean Arsenal fans should get excited yet.

Signing the Argentina striker - in what would arguably be the coup of the window - still looks very unlikely to happen before the deadline.

That is because of several obstacles still in their way; primarily the player's heart being set on a move to Barcelona and Atletico Madrid still refusing to sell him with just over a week to go.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking in April, Diego Simeone admitted that Arsenal are interested in Julian Alvarez.

Regardless of the feelings of Atletico fans, the club are digging their heels in, insisting they do not want to sell him to any club; certainly not to Barca and not the Premier League champions nor PSG either.

Arsenal will not completely give up - the door will always be open to a deal from their end right up until September 1 - but until they get an indication that Alvarez has shifted his thinking away from the Nou Camp, there is not much more Andrea Berta and Mikel Arteta can do.

Sky Sports News reported in July that Alvarez's family want to stay in Spain and that remains the case. They are happy and settled and the player's dream has long been to follow in the footsteps of compatriot Lionel Messi and star for Barca.

There is just over a week of the window remaining and anything can happen, but Barcelona will not give up either and it cannot be ruled out that they will not make another push to test Atletico's resolve - which has, until now, held firm.

Do Arsenal need Alvarez?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Friday Night Football panel discuss whether Arsenal are still shy of a world-class attacker that would see them get over the line to win their first UEFA Champions League title.

Arsenal are happy with their squad and showed in their resounding 3-0 opening day win over Coventry that they are in healthy place.

They clearly are now in a position in which signing only the very best will improve on what they have got. Alvarez is that and there are not many others on the market that come close.

However, Gary Neville feels Arsenal getting Alvarez would make them Champions League winners this season. Jamie Carragher feels the Gunners are one stardust signing away from becoming Kings of Europe.

"What a squad [Mikel Arteta] has built," said Neville. "If he puts another forward into that, if they could get Julian Alvarez somehow, that would light this place up as you'd have a world-class striker to go with all the world-class defenders and midfielders.

"They wouldn't just become Premier League title winners they'd go the next step and win a Champions League. It's a massive [few] days [in the transfer window]. He needs a bit of magic up front - someone that can win a game for you when you don't play well."

For the Premier League, Arsenal have shown they are already ahead of their rivals with an opening night victory, with summer signing Christos Tzolis and Martin Odegaard - who missed 30 matches last season - adding another dimension to Arsenal's attack.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry.

Meanwhile, Liverpool, Manchester United and Tottenham all dropped points over the course of the first weekend, while Enzo Maresca admitted his Man City team - who were unconvincing in their late comeback win over Bournemouth - are still a "work in progress."

Arsenal could also move for a left-sided forward - which Alvarez is not - before the transfer deadline, if Gabriel Martinelli moves on this summer.

The Brazilian has been left out of Arsenal's last two matchday squads and has one year left on his deal - plus there is interest from Galatasaray and Saudi Arabia.

Arsenal could also let Gabriel Jesus leave this summer - but will not do so unless a replacement, such as Alvarez, is lined up.

So if Alvarez is unattainable - do Arsenal move elsewhere, or perhaps even not move for a forward at all? Despite being ahead of their rivals, the Premier League champions still face a big final week in the transfer window.

Sports.title: Meet the Filipino tennis superstar-in-waiting with a punch to rival Pacquiao's
Sports.content:
"Once it grows, it cannot be stopped" - tennis superstar-in-the-making Alex Eala is quickly becoming the biggest thing to come out of the Philippines since legendary boxer Manny Pacquiao.

The 21-year-old is carrying the hopes of a nation, the volume of support when she plays calling to mind the days when world boxing champion 'Pac Man' put the country on the map as a sporting force.

Few young players on the WTA Tour have experienced the level of expectation and support Eala has received ‌since she earned a place on the circuit, and she showed what all the fuss is about ‌by winning the recent Washington Open.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Alex Eala against Jessica Pegula in Washington

After a run to the fourth round of Wimbledon, which included a victory over defending champion Iga Swiatek, Eala capped her breakthrough in the US capital by rallying to defeat top seed Jessica Pegula 4-6 ​6-4 6-0 in a rain-interrupted final, becoming the first woman from her country to claim a tour-level singles crown.

Along the way, ​she beat Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen, last year's winner Leylah ‌Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka.

Her remarkable run of victories mark her down out as a ​dangerous outsider for the US Open, starting August 30 - live on Sky Sports.

"It's an incredible milestone for me," said Eala, who moved to Spain to attend the Rafa Nadal Academy on a scholarship at the age of 13. "Coming into the tournament, I knew that the competition was super strong and my draw was quite tough. Every match was a ‌different set of obstacles. I'm really proud.

"I ended the tournament in better shape than I started. Each match I kept improving and kept learning things about myself. So it definitely gives me ‌a lot of confidence.

"It's really nice to see all the things I've been working on off court or during training being implemented in matches."

Rise of the Filipino superstar-in-waiting

Eala's progress has been closely watched since her US Open junior triumph in 2022, and she reached the Eastbourne final last year before making the fourth ⁠round at Wimbledon - signalling a steady improvement.

As Eala's reputation grew, so ​too did her following, with large groups of Filipino fans packing ​the stands at tournaments around the world to back a player many see ​as a pioneer for tennis in their country.

Her popularity - like Pacquiao in his heyday - was evident in the final ⁠of the WTA 500 event in Washington. By the time the tournament ended, the phrase written across the Nike T-shirt she had worn earlier that week had become a reality: "Once it grows, it cannot be stopped."

Image: Eala has drawn huge support from the Filipino community at her matches

Philippines president Ferdinand Marcos released a message on social media congratulating Eala on "yet another historic achievement", adding: "You continue to redefine what is possible for Philippine tennis and inspire countless young Filipinos to dream without limits."

The Philippines' sporting interests have historically been all about basketball, billiards and boxing, but the nation is now being swept up in tennis fever.

Sky Sports analyst Annabel Croft believes Eala can be one of the "biggest stars" and is "just what the tour needs" following her success in Washington.

The former British No 1 said: "I've never seen anything like it. The stadium, you could not get a seat. The noise, the excitement levels, and she just takes it all in her stride. And you could see in Washington what she brings to the court and she plays with such grace.

"There's a certain class about her. I love her attitude. I love the way she goes after the ball. She's a very deceptive tennis player. Being a lefty, she's quite awkward, but that forehand it's not a huge strike, but it does damage."

Image: Eala has a similar serve to 2018 Wimbledon champion Angelique Kerber

Croft has likened Eala's serve to that of former Wimbledon champion Angelique Kerber who relied heavily on her left-handed spin, placement, and variation.

She said: "I would imagine that she has built up some kind of locker-room respect right now where you build a certain aura and then that counts for quite a lot on the tour as well because players don't want to face you because of the record that she's building up.

"There's something awkward about a lefty serve, a little bit like Kerber. I remember she didn't have a big serve, but it was so well placed into the court. But also when you put a lot of spin on it and it sometimes has less pace on it, you're forcing your opponents to generate pace and they start to get a bit jittery.

"She keeps notching up the big wins, but she's also backing up the pressure wins.

"She plays under a lot of pressure with all of that excitement from the Filipino community. They turn out in their droves to watch her. That for some people would be a pressure, but she embraces it. She loves it."

Is Eala a US Open contender?

Image: Is Eala a contender to win the US Open?

Asked whether Eala could be a contender at the US Open, Croft said: "She's obviously somebody who enjoys being on a big stage. There will be a lot of players that won't want to face her because she's very in form. And I think the hard courts really suit her game."

Eala partnered American tennis legend Venus Williams in the doubles in Toronto this month, resuming their pairing from the Bad Homburg Open in Germany earlier this year.

Williams had high praise for Eala, saying: "Alex is a world star. She's just incredible. Besides the fact of her tennis, she's an incredible person, well spoken, and just an impressive young lady."

Image: Eala has the potential to rival the popularity of legendary Filipino boxer Manny Pacquiao

Meanwhile, four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka has thanked Eala for bringing the Filipino community to tennis.

"I think it's great," said the Japanese star. "I finished my match and the little go-kart was taking me back. I looked at the practice court and it was completely full. I was like, 'who's practising right now?' She didn't even go on court yet and then I saw the Filipino flags and I was like, 'um-hum'.

"I think it's awesome. It's so cool that she's building a new community and obviously great for the tournament, because she sells a lot of tickets."

Sports.title: Yamashita equals LPGA Tour record in dominant CPKC Women's Open win
Sports.content:
Miyu Yamashita equaled the LPGA Tour's 72-hole scoring record in claiming a dominant, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open..

The Japanese star's closing birdie on Sunday signed off a four-under final round of 66 to take her total for the week to 23 under par and 257 strokes, securing a wire-to-wire win in Edmonton.

Sei Young Kim also shot 257 in the 2018 Thornberry Creek LPGA Classic in Wisconsin, finishing 31 under.

A stroke ahead after Thursday's opening round, thanks to a course-record 62, Yamashita posted a 64 on Friday to open a five-shot lead, before carding a 65 on Saturday.

That had her six strokes ahead entering the final round at Royal Mayfair, Yamashita pushed her winning margin to nine for a tournament record in the Canadian national championship, breaking Jin Young Ko's 262 set in 2019 at Magna in Aurora, Ontario.

Yamashita's four LPGA Tour titles have come in four different countries. She won the Meijer LPGA Classic in the USA in June, after claiming a first major success at the AIG Women's Open title in Wales along with taking the Maybank Championship title in Malaysia last year. She has 13 Japan LPGA victories.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights from Miyu Yamashita's maiden major victory at the AIG Women's Open in 2025 at Royal Porthcawl.

Fellow Japanese player Yuri Yoshida was second at 14 under after a closing 69. Kim was a further shot back after her final-round 67.

Seventeen-year-old Anna Huang was the top Canadian, signing off her week with an impressive 65 to tie for fourth at 12 under.

Aphrodite Deng, the 16-year-old amateur who won the 2025 US Girls' Junior, tied for seventh at 11 under after shooting 67 on Sunday.

Two-time winner Brooke Henderson finished seven under after a closing 70. World No 1 Nelly Korda shot 69 to get to five under.

Three spots on the US Solheim Cup were decided during the week, with Allisen Corpuz, Andrea Lee and Alison Lee securing their place at

US captain Angela Stanford is set to announce her final three picks on Monday, August 24.

Sports.title: Amorim’s Milan live up to billing as teenage star Cissè upstages signings | Nicky Bandini
Sports.content:
“I love Cissè. I love Cissè.” Ruben Amorim had not yet taken charge of his first competitive game as Milan manager but already he was furnishing journalists with soundbites and supporters with memes, clippable moments that you just knew we were destined to revisit.

Alphadjo Cissè is a 19-year-old attacking midfielder who signed for Milan from Verona in February but only joined up with them this summer, after completing the season-long loan he had already begun at Catanzaro in Serie B. He scored six goals in 22 games there, missing the second half of the campaign with a thigh injury. Previously he had played a combined 14 minutes for Verona across three substitute appearances in the top flight.

Yet Amorim spoke of Cissè like a man who knew something that the rest of the world doesn’t. More than his words, it was the body language: hands rubbing together in anticipation, lip curled at one corner into an emoji-like version of a smirk.

Cissè would start away to Torino the following evening. Within 75 seconds of kick-off, he had taken the first shot of the game: racing forward to hook a Ruben Loftus-Cheek cross into the side netting from an acute angle beyond the far post.

For an Italian teenager to make Milan’s first XI on the opening weekend was already a significant detail. The scarce opportunities afforded to young domestic talent in Serie A has been a national talking point ever since the Azzurri failed to qualify for a third consecutive men’s World Cup.

Data compiled by Football Benchmark found that Italians who qualified for the under-21 category accounted for only 3.9% of minutes played last season, while foreign players in that age group took 8.2%. “In other words, young foreign players receive more than twice as many opportunities as their Italian counterparts.”

There were signs of a possible shift this weekend. The season began with 21-year-old Pio Esposito delivering a man-of-the-match performance for the champions, Inter, in their 4-1 win over Monza, but he was the exception who stood apart already last year.

More surprising were the new faces popping up elsewhere. Cissè, born in Treviso to Guinean parents, was one of three Italian teenagers on the pitch at the Olympic stadium in Turin, with Diego Mascardi and Alessio Cacciamani, both 19, lining up at goalkeeper and left wing-back for the Granata.

View image in fullscreen Ruben Amorim won his first Serie A match in charge against Ignazio Abate’s Torino. Photograph: Daniele Mascolo/Reuters

The 18-year-olds Matteo Palma (an Italian-German dual national) and Simone Lontani started for Udinese and Parma respectively, and the 19-year-old Mathis Mout for Monza. Even Como, whose project has been criticised for relying almost exclusively on foreign talent, gave Mattia Liberali, 19, some minutes off the bench. It is far too soon to draw conclusions, but certainly a trend worth tracking.

In any case, putting your faith in untested young talent can feel like a greater gamble for a club with Milan’s expectations. After a disappointing fifth-place finish last season under Massimiliano Allegri, the Rossoneri have spent big – appointing Amorim and then dropping a club-record €74m to sign Gonçalo Ramos from Paris Saint-Germain, as well as another €50m on the midfielder Diego Moreira from Strasbourg and €30m on the defender Mario Gila from Lazio.

Amorim has not shied away from ambition, saying his goal is to win the Scudetto, even while acknowledging it may take time to bridge the gap to Inter. More than that, he has won over fans with the promise of a front-footed team who will seek to set the tempo and dictate how games are played – a welcome change from the caution and reactivity of Allegri.

There were promising performances in pre-season – not least the 4-2 win over Amorim’s last club, Manchester United, with Cissè on the scoresheet. But friendlies are not the real thing. Sunday’s visit to a Torino side undergoing a renewal of their own under a new manager, and former Milan player, Ignazio Abate, was always going to be a fascinating first challenge.

Ramos and Gila started, at centre-forward and on the right of defence. Moreira, who only completed his move on 19 August, stayed on the bench. Cissè was the other truly new face, playing to the left of Ramos in a 3-4-2-1, though Yunus Musah and the right wing-back Samuel Chukwueze were also returning after spending last season out on loan.

Amorim’s approach lived up to billing. From the start, Milan dominated the ball and the pitch – claiming more than 70% of first-half possession while outshooting their opponents by 11 to one. And yet, they struggled to break Torino down in the final third. Aside from one solo effort by Chukwueze, who dribbled in from the right and forced a save from Mascardi, they had rarely looked like scoring.

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Parma 0-1 Cagliari, Genoa 0-2 Napoli, Udinese 1-1 Como, Inter 4-1 Monza, Torino 1-2 Milan, Atalanta 2-1 Sassuolo, Venezia 0-2 Lecce, Frosinone 0-1 Juventus Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Cissè thought he had earned Milan a penalty after the interval, when his cross struck the arm of Nikola Vlasic. That the VAR booth did not call the referee, Luca Zufferli, to take a second look may be an early indicator – together with incidents from other games – of a shift in approach under the new refereeing designator, Daniele Orsato. He has stated a desire to “put referees back at the centre of the match” and return to the idea that technology should only be used for those elusive “clear and obvious” mistakes.

Torino were growing into the game. But that might also have been their undoing. In the 64th minute, Musah turned his man in midfield, surging into space left open by the home team’s press. He fed Adrien Rabiot, a second-half substitute, on the right. The Frenchman crossed to Cissè, who brought the ball down with his waist and curled a half volley into the far corner. The teenager slid to his knees as he celebrated in front of the away fans.

Within moments it was 2-0, Rabiot himself converting a Chukwueze delivery. Torino kept battling, and Scotland’s Ché Adams scored the best goal of the game in injury time, an outrageously nonchalant right-foot volley over his own left shoulder. But the three points went to Milan.

Cissè laughed when the interviewer from Dazn asked him at full time what he thought about Amorim’s professions of love. “It makes me happy,” he said. “But I didn’t hear the press conference. All my friends told me about it instead.”

View image in fullscreen Alphadjo Cissè’s half volley gives Milan the lead in Turin. Photograph: Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images

He was still recovering from injury when he first joined up with Milan this summer. Cissè said he had tried to watch training as closely as possible, getting to know what the manager wanted. Still, he acknowledged, it was “beyond a dream” to get to start, and score, in the season opener.

The numbers say he is the youngest Italian to score for Milan since Patrick Cutrone in 2017, as well as the first Italian to score for them on a debut Serie A start since Daniel Maldini in 2021. Those names should remind everyone not to get ahead of themselves. Cutrone, now 28, was a substitute for Monza this weekend and has only reached double figures for goals once in a top-flight season. Maldini, 24, has played for seven clubs since 2022, and begins this campaign with Cagliari.

But Amorim clearly thinks highly of Cissè, who has represented Italy at various age categories up to under-21, saying he looked at times in the first-half like the most experienced player on the pitch.

The manager, conducting his interviews mostly in English, said Milan have “a lot to improve”, acknowledging both their struggles to break Torino down early on and the way they faded at the end. “[But] the first thing is also win. That is the most important thing. We talk about ways of playing, but there is one goal in calcio. Vincere.”

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from opening weekend of the season
Sports.content:
1 Wright laments Martinelli treatment

Arsenal’s treatment of Gabriel Martinelli has been questioned by Ian Wright after the Brazil forward was left out of their squad for Friday’s opening game against Coventry. Martinelli turned down a move to Galatasaray last week after Arsenal had agreed a fee with the Turkish club and the former striker Wright revealed on Sky Sports after the Coventry game that no one at the club has spoken to the 25-year-old to discuss his future. “I know they might want him out, and a lot of people might say: ‘Yeah, it’s time for him to move him on.’ But there’s ways of doing that and it should suit him as well, how he wants to leave,” said Wright. “He’s done enough with this squad to be treated with a little bit more respect than he’s being treated with at the moment.” Ed Aarons

2 Has Watkins tarnished legacy?

It was only one game after 278 for Aston Villa, accumulated over the previous six seasons – a period in which Ollie Watkins has scored 108 goals and made himself one of the most popular players in the club’s Premier League history. But the rules are the rules. Nobody can refuse to play and emerge without a mark against their character. This is the charge against Watkins, brought in none-too-subtle fashion by Unai Emery after Villa’s 4-0 defeat at Brighton – a match that Watkins missed as he considers an approach from Al-Hilal. We do not yet have Watkins’s side of the story. Or that of his agent. But given Emery had no other available No 9, it feels pretty clear the manager did not choose to omit Watkins. Villa claim they are not close to any agreement with Al-Hilal, having rejected more than one offer from them. Perish the thought that this could drag on. Villa have one more game before the window shuts – against Arsenal at home next Monday night. David Hytner

View image in fullscreen Unai Emery did nothing to deny that Ollie Watkins had refused to play for Villa in their sobering defeat. Photograph: Glyn Kirk/AFP/Getty Images

3 United falter as No 9 options look thin

Michael Carrick was limited in his options during Manchester United’s opener because Benjamin Sesko was unable to feature at any point in pre-season but Matheus Cunha was completely ineffective as a false 9. Hull’s back three enjoyed a very quiet lunchtime as they returned to the Premier League. Cunha did not embrace the physical battle and went missing, leaving United with barely any presence in the final third as they failed to threaten their opponents. Sesko was brought on to change the dynamic but was equally ineffectual, while his fellow striker Joshua Zirkzee was left on the bench, implying how little trust the coaches have in him. Carrick needs to get Sesko up to speed and sell Zirkzee soon, freeing up funds to find a better alternative if United are to compete this season, especially with the false 9 tactic looking flawed. Will Unwin

4 Tigers delight in Tzolakis’s debut

Manchester United were impressively unthreatening in their approach to losing at Hull. There was the odd half-baked attempt at scoring or putting a cross into a dangerous area but nothing that made the highlights reel. This was unfortunate for the Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who had an impressive, if somewhat uncomplicated, debut between the sticks. United should have made a greater effort to test the £20m signing from Olympiakos. What duties the Greek international was forced to do were carried out with ease, instilling confidence in the defence in front of him. If he continues to look so calm and assured, Tzolakis could prove himself one of the smartest signings of the season. “We bought him and we spent some money there,” Sergej Jakirovic said. “He’s a national-team player of Greece, an Olympiakos player. If you’re following Greek football, Olympiakos, it’s a huge stress, huge pressure there, and he’s used to it. For him, I think this is like a cup of tea.” WU

5 Cherki’s crucial cameo after disquiet

Rayan Cherki wrested the three points in a cameo that consisted of the corner for Marc Guéhi’s equaliser and the cute pass for Josko Gvardiol’s winner. Enzo Maresca gave an insight into the Frenchman’s disquiet at not starting. “Rayan is quite a nice and clear boy, if he is not happy he wants to show it. If he’s next to me and he’s not happy, you all realise that he is not happy because he is doing anything just to show that he is not happy. I know that he was not happy today but at the end I had to take a decision,” said the manager. Jamie Jackson

6 Sangaré shines against big spenders

At a time when some Premier League are willing to spend more than £100m on midfielders there is unlikely to be a better bargain than Mamadou Sangaré. Brentford’s new signing was excellent for Lens last season and was outstanding on his debut against Tottenham. Sangaré dominated midfield, even with Spurs able to field upwards of £175m worth of talent in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, and his performance raised the question of why the league’s bigger clubs are not willing to look further afield for signings. Brentford, after all, paid only £39m for Sangaré. Yet it seems inevitable there will be clubs willing to pay double the price if he has a good first season in England. Jacob Steinberg
