7 Isak struggles on return to Newcastle

As gut-wrenching as it must have been for Newcastle fans to see their side concede a stoppage-time penalty to Liverpool, at least they can take comfort that it wasn’t Alexander Isak that scored the Reds’ dramatic equaliser from 12 yards. The former Newcastle striker had a torrid time on his return to St James’ Park – booed at every touch, crunched by Lewis Hall in the tackle and sending his only real chance of note into orbit – but he would surely have fancied taking his revenge with the last kick of the game before Dominik Szoboszlai converted the 99th-minute spot-kick. Worryingly, Isak is lacking the fluency that convinced Liverpool to spend £125m last summer and with Hugo Ekitiké still sidelined with a long-term injury, Andoni Iraola doesn’t have a natural replacement at No 9. If Liverpool are to be successful this season, Isak has to turn it on. Michael Butler

View image in fullscreen Alexander Isak watches the ball during his return to Tyneside. Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty Images

8 Ipswich combat set pieces with O’Shea

A defensive tactical shift from the Ipswich Town manager, Gary O’Neil, demonstrated the changing nature of the Premier League. O’Neil, an astute reader of the game, chose to play the tall centre-back Dara O’Shea at right-back to counter the threat of set pieces that have become so prevalent, in Ipswich’s surprise win against Sunderland. “Aerially the Premier League is such a test now, from long throws and set pieces,” O’Neil said. “To have three centre-half types in your back four helps us from set pieces, size-wise.” In the first season since Pep Guardiola departed, the top flight is already shifting away from his neat, passing football to a different beast. Sam Cunningham

9 Dewsbury-Hall on path to complete midfielder

David Moyes felt his young Everton team might have been uncomfortable chasing the game against Crystal Palace and were therefore indebted to Jordan Pickford’s save from Eddie Nketiah, plus Jean-Philippe Mateta’s finishing, for not having to do so. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall’s guidance was instrumental too. The performance of both teams altered once the midfielder imposed himself, while his superb strike beyond Dean Henderson underlined the quality of a player who will be crucial to Everton’s aspirations. “I want to be better than last season,” said Dewsbury-Hall, who delivered eight goals and four assists in his first Premier League campaign at Everton. “That’s not just goals and assists, it’s my overall play. A couple of years ago I probably wasn’t getting goals and assists but was influential in play. I want to mix that together and when you do that that’s when you become a complete midfielder. I know I have the ability to do it so fingers crossed I do.” Andy Hunter

10 Farke hopes Leeds can cement status

Optimism abounds at Leeds. An encouraging opening-day victory at Nottingham Forest gave credence to the idea that Daniel Farke’s side are capable of cementing their place in the league. Last season, survival was the aim but after investing about £80m to sign James Trafford, Tarik Muharemovic and Nico Elvedi, plus Harry Wilson on a free, they are seeking to build on a 14th-placed finish. Leeds and Forest, who meet again in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, have both been linked with a move for Chelsea’s Liam Delap; a striker to share the load with Dominic Calvert-Lewin would surely elevate Farke’s side. “If we want to establish ourselves and after a few years perhaps speak about something else, then we need to add individual quality,” Farke said. “The last time this club was able to have two solid seasons at this level, you will perhaps find it in black-and-white photos.” Ben Fisher

Sports.title: EFL and Scottish league pushing to stop illegal broadcast of matches in Russia
Sports.content:
The English Football League and Scottish Professional Football League have launched investigations and are considering legal action after discovering that television coverage of their matches has been broadcast in Russia this season.

Football TV, a Russian subscription and streaming service, has broadcast numerous games from the opening two rounds of the EFL, as well as Scottish Premiership matches featuring Celtic, Rangers and Hearts.

The EFL and SPFL stopped broadcasting in Russia in March 2022 after the previous month’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and have not sold rights packages in the country since, so the live footage of games appears to have been obtained and televised illegally.

Quick Guide How do I 

Until Russia’s full-scale invasion the EFL had a rights contract with Football TV, and the Scottish Premiership was broadcast on Match TV.

The Premier League suspended its broadcasts in Russia at the same time, with its rights held by Okko Sport.

The EFL contacted Football TV last week after being alerted that several games, including Cardiff’s 1-1 draw with Wrexham last Monday and Watford’s 2-1 win over Southampton the previous day, were shown in Russia, but despite this complaint the broadcaster also aired live coverage of West Ham v Charlton and West Brom v Burnley this past weekend.

Those matches were listed as test events, raising concerns that Football TV may also plan to show illegal content from the Premier League.

Several Scottish Premiership matches were shown over the past two weekends, with the broadcasts promoted on Football TV’s Telegram channel.

The EFL and the SPFL’s priority is to ensure the broadcasts stop, which is being pursued, and they are seeking to discover the source of the pirated content.

Both organisations are understood to reserve the right to take legal action against Football TV and whoever is supplying it with access to their matches.

An SPFL source said the league was investigating the matter in conjunction with its broadcasting distribution rights holder, Infront.

The EFL and SPFL declined to comment.

Sports.title: Ceferin brands Infantino’s failed World Cup plan as ‘even worse than the Super League’
Sports.content:
The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, has described Gianni Infantino’s doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup as “even worse than the Super League plan” and warned his embattled Fifa counterpart that he will face an opponent if he runs for re-election next March.

Ceferin has led Uefa’s firm collective stance against the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which was shelved amid widespread opposition at the start of August. Uefa are pushing for Infantino to quit, also drawing on support from Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, and are yet to drop a threat to boycott Fifa competitions while talks are under way with Concacaf to set up a combined Nations League tournament.

In an interview with the podcast The Rest is Politics: Leading, Ceferin denounced Infantino’s project as more damaging than the breakaway Super League that was shelved in 2021 after large-scale protests. “I think this plan is even worse than the Super League plan,” he said. “In the first case, super-important clubs wanted to do their own league, which is wrong and would destroy football. But in this case, football would be literally sold.

“I’m absolutely sure that the [FFE] plan is dead. For me, the most important thing is that we stopped another try to sell the sport. It’s hard to imagine what kind of people would sell the sport that belongs to everyone.”

Earlier this month it was reported that Infantino had held talks about running the Super League under Fifa branding. Ceferin is confident that any revival of that plan would be decades away. “It might happen in 20 years, you never know, but for now we cooperate with everyone in a great way. I’m sure it cannot happen in the next 10 years,” he said.

Infantino spent much of the weekend courting support from Concacaf members at a meeting in the Dominican Republic, infuriating many of those present. Ceferin, who revealed the pair had not been in contact since the FFE scandal broke, believes the Fifa president’s path to survival is narrowing.

“I didn’t speak with him, he didn’t contact me since this happened,” he said. “But there are two options. One option is that he realises that he doesn’t have the support, and that’s not only political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of the football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.

“And the second option [is] that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case, I think he will have a candidate against him. I don’t know yet who.” The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, has been tipped as a potential opponent for Infantino if he chooses to run in Rabat.

Ceferin has proponents of his own but ruled out making his own bid for the Fifa presidency. “My credibility is much, much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position,” he said. The Slovenian is expected to run unopposed for a fourth term at the helm of Uefa, with the election due next April.

Asked whether Infantino had become too close to Donald Trump, with whom he forged a close relationship before the recent World Cup, Ceferin said: “To be honest, I think you are naive if you think that a politician like that, or any politician, is your good friend. The moment you are a problem, you stop being a friend of a politician.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That friendship came under the spotlight last month when Trump said he had called Infantino to ask for a review of the red card given to the US striker Folarin Balogun, whose ban for the last-16 tie against Belgium was later suspended. “That was more than shocking,” Ceferin said. “We have rules and if you don’t respect your own rules, then the game doesn’t make any sense. That’s shocking and, trust me, almost everybody was shocked. Just not everybody dared to speak.”

Meanwhile, in a fresh show of European opposition to Infantino, the six Nordic football associations issued a statement saying they had “lost confidence in the Fifa president and have serious concerns about the governance and high-level decision making of the organisation”. They asked for binding assurances that Fifa will never again “open its governance or competitions to private ownership” and called for a full third-party review into the FFE scheme.

Earlier in August the Norwegian Football Federation was the first member association to call directly for Infantino to step down.

Infantino travelled straight from the Dominican Republic to Paris on Sunday, attending the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup. Television footage showed him exchanging greetings with the president of France, Emmanuel Macron.

Sports.title: Chelsea change course with Alonso primed to banish the chaos of youth
Sports.content:
It is a necessary reset. Although it would be pushing it to say that Chelsea have switched from development centre to retirement home, even after the signings of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, there has been a clear shift in strategy this summer. Some grownups are in the room at last and, for Xabi Alonso, the hope is that bringing in more experience will help a squad still packed with youngsters show more composure when adversity strikes.

Discipline was a problem for Chelsea last season: they had 11 red cards in all competitions and a lot of the wounds were self-inflicted. Chelsea were impetuous, on the receiving end of too many bookings for dissent and prone to collapsing at the first sign of trouble. No wonder Alonso, who was the epitome of calm during his playing career, has focused on maintaining “emotional control” before opening his tenure as manager with Monday’s trip to Fulham.

It will be a test of Chelsea’s mentality. Craven Cottage has been the setting for some spectacular implosions during the BlueCo era, the path to two 2-1 victories for Fulham over their neighbours smoothed by João Félix earning a red card on his Chelsea debut in 2023 and by Marc Cucurella getting himself sent off after 22 minutes last season.

Chelsea need to change, and hiring Alonso was a tacit admission that their approach required fine-tuning. Internally there was a recognition that the club had undervalued the importance of aura when it came to hiring coaches.

They blundered with Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior, neither of whom were capable of standing the heat. Alonso is a different breed. The 44-year-old burnished his reputation by leading Bayer Leverkusen to the Bundesliga title in 2024 and he wowed Chelsea during his discussions over the role, so much so that they broke with the past by naming him manager rather than head coach.

Now the players can look to the dugout and see an authority figure. Alonso has not seized absolute power – he is still part of a wider structure, collaborating with an extensive recruitment team – but there is no doubt that his arrival has lent credibility to a project that was in danger of falling apart when the Rosenior experiment ended.

View image in fullscreen Liam Rosenior struggled at Stamford Bridge, lasting less than four months. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock

Of course, it remains to be seen if success in Germany means Alonso can dominate in England. Leverkusen was special but Real Madrid left him with a scar. Then again, the Bernabéu is not exactly where managers go to develop. It makes Álvaro Arbeloa, who stepped in at Madrid after Alonso’s sacking last season, a similar unknown after replacing Marco Silva at Fulham.

Yet there is optimism around Chelsea. Can they mount a title challenge for the first time in a decade? There is a lot of ground to make up after finishing 10th last season. Weaknesses linger, particularly in goal, and a push for the top four looks likelier.

However, no European football could be a blessing, giving Alonso more time in training. He looks tactically flexible. Chelsea switched between a back four and a back three during pre-season. Cucurella has joined Madrid but Marco Palestra, signed from Atalanta for £43m, and Pep Chavarría, a £16.3m arrival from Rayo Vallecano, could play as wingbacks.

The recruitment looks purposeful. After years of buying promising youngsters Chelsea have targeted ready-made players. Maxence Lacroix, the 26-year-old France centre-back, is a sensible signing from Crystal Palace. Morgan Rogers, signed from Aston Villa for £117m, can play in a range of positions in attacking midfield and could form an exciting partnership with a rested Cole Palmer, who has a point to prove after missing out on England’s World Cup squad.

There is talent here. There always has been, though. The flaw has more been around mindset. It is a footballing norm to have wise heads around to protect young players. Chelsea went too far in the opposite direction and it is one of the first areas Alonso has addressed.

Perhaps he has heard the tale of one of his predecessors having to deal with a player prioritising a haircut over a team meeting. Either way it did not feel on brand when Chelsea made an unsuccessful attempt to sign the 33-year-old Granit Xhaka from Sunderland in June. Yet it underlined their desire for more leadership and the box was ticked when Welbeck, 35, joined from Brighton in a cut-price deal and Henderson, 36, was brought in on a free transfer from Brentford.

View image in fullscreen New signing Danny Welbeck offers experience, maturity and a reliable source of goals. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

They could be canny moves. Perhaps there is an element of overkill, a sense of Chelsea taking their new direction too far, but Welbeck and Henderson still have something to offer. Welbeck scored 13 league goals for Brighton last season and will provide cover for João Pedro up front, while Henderson did not look out of place for Brentford and, according to Jude Bellingham, is someone coaching staff will always go to when there are problems to resolve.

Alonso needs order. There are still rumblings of instability off the pitch, with Todd Boehly and Mark Walter looking to sell their stakes in the club to the majority shareholder, Clearlake Capital. Quiet is rare. Chelsea need to shift a host of players before the transfer window shuts and questions hover over Enzo Fernández, who favours a reunion with Enzo Maresca at Manchester City.

There has been a lot of noise around Fernández. The midfielder has made no secret of his desire to leave but speaking out so much when Chelsea were wounded underlined the decline in standards. Alonso needs leaders. He needs trust. He still has to prove the hype is justified but his attempts to change Chelsea’s mentality is an encouraging first step.

Sports.title: ‘Call his agent’: Emery feels Watkins should explain absence from Villa’s rout by Brighton
Sports.content:
Unai Emery did nothing to deny that Ollie Watkins had refused to play for Aston Villa in their sobering 4-0 defeat by Brighton at the Amex on Sunday. The head coach had a selection crisis up front with Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham injured. However, he did not include Watkins in the matchday squad as the England striker considers a move to Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia.

Emery was forced to rely on the attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía as an emergency striker and his team disappeared without trace on the south coast. They were 4-0 down after 31 minutes and had their new signing João Gomes sent off on his debut in the 40th minute. Gomes kicked up and out at the Brighton striker Georginio Rutter after being dispossessed by him.

Al-Hilal have made a number of bids for Watkins, all of which have been rejected. It is understood the 30-year-old is open to the move and Emery talked on Friday like a manager who was realistic about the sale happening. Villa would plainly like to replace Watkins should he depart as they approach the end of another difficult summer window. They have already sold Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Youri Tielemans, while they are expected to move on Emiliano Martínez.

Emery was asked why he had not picked Watkins against Brighton. “This question is for him,” he said. “I can answer only with my silence.” Emery was then asked if Watkins had refused to play, to which he said: “I think you can call him and you can call his agent and he can respond.”

The Guardian have contacted Watkins’s agent for comment.

“He [Watkins] can only explain his answer, I can’t,” Emery added, after being asked if he felt let down by Watkins.

Emery reported that Madjo would be out for “two weeks more … more or less” while attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi – who has been the club’s marquee summer signing – would “need maybe some days more [than that]”. He was unclear about a timeframe for Abraham’s return.

Quick Guide How do I 

Emery talked up the resistance of his players in the second half against Brighton and said he was optimistic about finding solutions for the season ahead. But he returned to the difficult preparations for the opening fixture, noting that: “Two strikers are injured and another striker gives his answer.”

The head coach added: “This problem [with the transfer market] … we had every season and every season we overcame it. It’s something we have to accept and always we reacted, especially the players. This is something hard for us every year but we are calm. With this result, it’s more difficult to explain but calm, work, be positive and find solutions for the next week and after the transfer window.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Alvarez set for Arsenal after being booed at Atlético?
Sports.content:
Booing Julián Alvarez during Atlético Madrid’s draw with Villarreal on Sunday has seemingly convinced the Argentina forward to consider joining Arsenal in the window. The former Manchester City man has been kept out of the reaches of Barcelona, who may not have the funds to complete the signing, whereas the Gunners have plenty of cash to splash.

Alejandro Balde was left out of the Barcelona squad as they roared past Elche, as the Catalan club open the door for a move to Manchester United. A new left-back should solve all of the problems at Old Trafford, that’s for sure.

Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to West Ham, despite them being relegated and starting the Championship season in desperate fashion. Despite all that, perhaps he will be tempted by a £50m bid from Crystal Palace after a welcome to the Championship to forget? The Eagles were blunt at Everton over the weekend and could be about to initiate panic stations by splashing out quite severely for the Hammers skipper.

Losing 4-0 at Brighton is not going to do much for morale but it will make a team take drastic action in the market. Aston Villa have lined up Joel Ordóñez to solve all of their problems for the remainder of the season, if Club Brugge are willing to sell the centre-back.

There is only one way to bounce back from losing at Ipswich and that is to chase a £34m Barcelona player. Sunderland have tracked Marc Casadó throughout the summer and could be about to pounce for the 22-year-old, who has also been linked with most of the Premier League in recent weeks.

It is difficult to decipher if Cruzeiro’s Jonathan Jesus would sign for Strasbourg or Chelsea, but the talk in Brazil is that ownership group BlueCo want the 22-year-old centre-back. Real Betis, Valencia and Benfica are equally keen, adding a bit of jeopardy to the chase.

With Chelsea always looking to move on a few players, they will be ecstatic to hear that Napoli are contemplating a move for the striker Marc Guiu. Whether the Italians are up for splurging £25m on the Spaniard remains to be seen because the Serie A club currently believe the Blues’ valuation is a touch on the high side.

As alluded to, it was a fantastic start to the season for Hull on Saturday when they gave Manchester United a bit of a shooing. To help build on that, they have agreed a £15.4m deal to sign forward Mohamed-Ali Cho from Nice.

And despite his goal against Liverpool, Joe Willock is being linked with a move to Besiktas, the Turkish club apparently casting flirtatious glances towards the Newcastle midfielder.

Sports.title: Newcastle and Liverpool crank up the entertainment for emotional send-off | Sam Dalling
Sports.content:
It’s 4.35pm on Tyneside. William Osula sets Anthony Elanga away, slightly right of centre and just short of 50,000 draw collective breaths. Pace is no issue; Elanga has no shortage of that, and Milos Kerkez won’t catch him.

But Newcastle fans have seen this clip before and remember the ending. Muscles tighten, cheeks clench, as they brace themselves for it to start again like it carried on before. (Yet) another memeable‑moment inbound. A tiny part of each of them, though, thinks: “Wait, hang on, this is a new season, a fresh start.” The slate is not just clean but has been entirely replaced and is now AI-operated.

Elanga takes a touch, a tad heavier ideal but it pushes the ball away from Alisson. A moment of composure follows and Newcastle lead. An entirely goalless league season passed after Elanga’s £55m transfer from Nottingham Forest and now, within five minutes of a new one, his drought is broken. Elanga missed a much easier opportunity against Aston Villa on the 2025-26 opening day, and his confidence never recovered. Can you walk back through a sliding door?

Nearly two hours later, there remain just a few precious seconds for Liverpool to salvage something. Victor Muñoz is brought down clumsily by Lewis Hall. Dominik Szoboszlai converts the resulting penalty. 2-2.

Muñoz apparently gave Newcastle positive noises about joining them during summer. Then, in a flexing of financial muscle, Liverpool met the Osasuna forward’s release clause and to Anfield he went. What was that about sliding doors?

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s Víctor Muñoz – a summer target for Newcastle – is brought down by Lewis Hall to hand the visitors a late penalty. Photograph: Ian Hodgson/AP

Those two goals bookended an afternoon that was, if you want to do go down that road, a fitting tribute to the recently departed Kevin Keegan. Entertaining but flawed.

As a term, legend is so chronically overused now that it is meaningless. But Keegan is a prime example of the word’s proper application. Shortly before kick-off everyone present paid an emotional tribute to him. Legend. Hero. King. All subjective labels essentially turned objective.

With Liverpool, Keegan’s seven trophies in six years – including three titles and the European Cup – set the club up to be the behemoth they now are. Across three spells at Newcastle, he jabbed syringes of hope into a flailing, helpless shell.

St James’ Park is not quite the house that Keegan built, but it is no stretch to say it is the house built because of him. Without his steering Newcastle to Second Division safety in 1992 as manager, the club in its current guise might not exist.

So, why does Keegan remain so adored? He is in effect a symbol of what football once was and should still be, can be even. Maybe. Forget spreadsheets, financial acronyms and PR-doused messaging. Ignore expected this and that, low blocks and cancelling each other out. Find the joy. Forget perfect; take a risk. Failure and fallibility? Both absolutely OK.

Those are sentiments Andoni Iraola and Matthias Jaissle would do well to remember as they look to settle themselves into new gigs. The former, with Liverpool being champions two seasons ago, will be under the greater pressure. A repeat of his start at Bournemouth, where he won only at the 10th time of asking, would be difficult to tolerate.

There were promising signs for Iraola, sure. Jérémy Jacquet grew into his debut. Cody Gakpo had only just whipped a strike narrowly off target before his fine equaliser just after half-time. Rio Ngumoha was quiet but that he has impressed sufficiently to start the season opener is itself a plus.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz (centre) and former Newcastle man Alexander Isak again both struggled to make an impact for Liverpool. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

But there were familiar failings, too. The full-backs looked shaky and Iraola needs more (much, much more) from both the sums and the whole of the £241m Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak combo.

Isak is about as popular in Newcastle as government-mandated balaclava wearing in a heatwave would be, but the stick-cum-abuse he received didn’t seem to bother him. However, what should keep Isak up at night is how he can and must refind the level that rightly saw him tagged one of the Premier League’s best forwards not so long ago. A skied left-footed effort was the closest he came to silencing the heckles.

Jaissle is likely to get more slack. Everyone is aware of what Newcastle have, where they are and, most pertinent, what they have lost. Something fresh was absolutely needed but that requires time and patience. There are, and will continue to be, warts, imperfections, things that Bruno Guimarães might have done.

A midfield pair sold for north of £180m were replaced on Sunday by a double pivot with a combined aged of 38 and less than 50 league starts. Lewis Miley and Sean Steur looked the part but made mistakes. That they did so seeking the positive option will only endear them to fans. As will more similar performances from Yoane Wissa. A player who last season looked sluggish and largely static, was suddenly full of everything in the No 10 role.

A decent start. Room for improvement. Apply that to both sides.

Sports.title: Chelsea rule out Premier League club for Mykhailo Mudryk after second offer
Sports.content:
Chelsea rule out Premier League club for Mykhailo Mudryk after second offer

Chelsea have rejected a second offer from Leeds to sign Mykhailo Mudryk, talkSPORT understands.

It is also understood the Blues are no longer considering Leeds as an option for Mudryk, having already turned down their first approach last Friday.

3 Leeds boss Daniel Farke will have to look elsewhere for a new winger Credit: Getty

Chelsea won't be short of suitors for Mudryk, though, with multiple clubs in the Premier League and elsewhere in Europe interested in the winger.

talkSPORT understands one of the clubs in the mix for Mudryk is Strasbourg, who are controlled by Chelsea's owners.

Brentford is another who has Mudryk on their radar.

It is understood Mudryk's preference is to remain in the Premier League.

Why did Mykhailo Mudryk's ban get overturned?

Mudryk is eligible to play competitive football once again after his FA doping ban was resolved in July.

The 25-year-old was slapped with a four-year ban in November 2024 after he returned an 'adverse finding' for Meldonium.

However, the ban was overturned due to changes in World Anti-Doping Agency's (WADA) procedures, which meant the Meldonium found in Mudryk's system 'would not have been reported'.

Mudryk made his return to action for Chelsea in a pre-season friendly against Juventus, which the Blues lost 1-0.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso's verdict on Mykhailo Mudryk's return

Before the contest, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso spoke of his delight at having Mudryk back in the squad and, more importantly, around his teammates after a lengthy period of isolation.

"We are thrilled that Misha could be with us," Alonso said.

3 Chelsea beat Arsenal to Mudryk's signature in January 2023 Credit: Getty

"You could see his smile, how great the feeling is for him to be part of the team because he has been training on his own for a long time."

Alonso, along with several of Chelsea's players, were impressed with Mudryk's fitness levels upon his return to the fold.

How did Mykhailo Mudryk stay fit during his ban?

The 25-year-old later explained he endured what was essentially a pre-season that lasted 18 months, ensuring he would be ready to go for whenever his ban ended.

"I've been training, I've been training hard," Mudryk said.

"I didn't give up and I just tried to work as hard as I could.

"I was working six days a week with proper recovery, with proper sleep schedule, food, everything. Everything was the same, just double sessions per day.

3 Mudryk's return has given Alonso plenty of food for thought when it comes to his squad this season Credit: Getty

"It was to come back and to show myself again in the football world. That was my mission and I knew what I had to do for that.

"Only through hard work can you reach something."

Sports.title: Insider reveals Frank Lampard’s immediate reaction after Coventry’s defeat to Arsenal
Sports.content:
Insider reveals Frank Lampard’s immediate reaction after Coventry’s defeat to Arsenal

Coventry City can take positives from their opening weekend defeat to Arsenal.

That is the view of Frank Lampard's former assistant Jody Morris after he spoke to the Sky Blues boss following their 3-0 loss on Friday.

3 Lampard's Coventry have been backed to take positives from their defeat to Arsenal Credit: Getty

The Gunners cruised to a comfortable home win at the Emirates Stadium as they began their Premier League title defence in style.

It came as Coventry made their return to the top-flight following a 25-year hiatus.

They were the only newly-promoted side not to win, though, as Ipswich Town and Hull City both claimed victories.

Despite their wins over Sunderland and Manchester United, respectively, Morris believes Coventry remain a better side.

Morris on Lampard reaction

The former Chelsea midfielder joined Jeff Stelling and Ally McCoist on Monday's talkSPORT Breakfast show.

When asked about Coventry's defeat, he revealed he had spoken to Lampard after the match.

Morris explained: "I spoke to him yesterday [Sunday], but I was like the first two goals that Coventry conceded were avoidable. They’re just mistakes that got punished early doors.

"Ok, Arsenal could have won by a lot more, but the first two goals were pivotal. Giving away a two-goal lead to the champions doesn’t get any easier.

"But I thought that there were positives for them and you’re right, when you’re looking at what Ipswich and Hull have done in week one of the new season, you’d have to say, they’re a better team than both of them.

"So let’s see, but I thought that there were positives for them, but you can’t ask for a harder start, playing against the champions."

3 Morris worked as Lampard's assistant manager at Derby and Chelsea Credit: Getty

Morris previously worked under Lampard as his assistant manager at both Derby County and Chelsea.

They also made 39 appearances together for the Blues between 2001 and 2003.

What's next for Coventry?

Lampard will be hoping his side can kickstart their season with a win this coming weekend.

The Sky Blues will play their first home match of the campaign on Saturday afternoon against Hull.

Their meeting at the CBS Arena last term ended in a goalless draw.

A victory would be the hosts' first in the Premier League since beating Sunderland in April 2001.

3 Coventry were beaten 3-0 by Arsenal in their return to the Premier League Credit: Getty

Following their relegation the following month, they have spent time in all three EFL divisions, including a season in League Two.

Ahead of the visit of Hull, Coventry face League One Plymouth Argyle in the Carabao Cup second round on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Fulham vs Chelsea prediction and betting tips – West London bragging rights on the line
Sports.content:
Fulham vs Chelsea prediction and betting tips – West London bragging rights on the line

Fulham and Chelsea renew rivalry at Craven Cottage tonight in the final fixture of the Premier League's opening weekend.

But pre-match talk will all be about the last two former Real Madrid managers in the respective dug outs. Xabi Alonso at Chelsea and Alvaro Arbeloa at Fulham.



Fulham vs Chelsea head to head overview

Date : Monday, 24th August 2026

Craven Cottage Where to watch: Sky Sports Main Event, Sky Sports Premier League, Sky Sports Ultra HD

Chelsea vs Fulham quick tips

Fulham vs Chelsea prediction

"...no friends and no past. We are fighting for 90 minutes.” That was Alonso's response to on his relationship with former Liverpool and Real Madrid team-mate Arbeloa ahead of tonight's West London derby.

Fulham and Chelsea finished level on 52 points last term, Chelsea a place above Fulham only on goal difference. But now it's a whole new era for both of the London rivals.

Arbeloa's two biggest signings have come from his connections at Los Blancos. Promising striker Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios have arrived at Craven Cottage this summer.

The new Fulham gaffer's build-up has been a mixed bag typical of a new regime bedding in fresh signings, and the head coach used a 2-1 friendly win over Stuttgart to test Calvin Bassey alongside Jorge Cuenca in central defence, a pairing that looks likely to open the season with Joachim Andersen banned for the opener.



Alonso's side won two, drew one and lost two of their final five friendlies, with a 3-0 win over AC Milan the highlight and defeats to Juventus and Tottenham Hotspur exposing work still to do.

A 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad last weekend was the last audition before Monday, though several of the club's World Cup players have had only a fortnight of full training.



Fulham vs Chelsea betting tips

Palmer back on form

Chelsea fans will hope the signing of Morgan Rogers will unlock his long-time friend and former Man City academy team-mate Cole Palmer's best form.

The England playmaker was off the boil last season and didn't make Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad. But with a new manager and some exciting signings through the door, it could all be set up for Palmer to shine once again.



Both Palmer and Rogers playing in a two-pronged attacking midfield behind Joao Pedro could see Palmer begin with a bang. Goals and assists his favourite currency. Chelsea's prime penalty taker too, we're backing him to be an anytime goalscorer tonight.

Fulham making a point

Both sides won their home game last season, with Fulham snaring a 2-1 win over The Blues back in January.

In the 2024/2025 season there were a pair of away wins, showcasing how unpredictable this rivalry has been, especially since 2023.

Chelsea's array of signings give an allure of grandeur - but could a home fixture under the lights, prove to be the making of Fulham on their opening night?



The Blues may have the better season, but Fulham have got points in two of their last four home meetings with Chelsea. And that's what we're backing again at Craven Cottage this evening.

Card games

Whether it's the most bitter or not. A derby game brings out an extra edge in both sets of fans and players alike.

And if history is anything to go by, referee Peter Bankes could be in for a busy night.

The last meeting between the two sides produced six yellow cards, with four in the fixture at Stamford Bridge.



Going over the 4.5 mark may be a good value play if things get heated.

Sports.title: Man United transfer target told to ‘stay at home’ by manager amid transfer links
Sports.content:
Man United transfer target told to ‘stay at home’ by manager amid transfer links

Alejandro Balde has seemingly made his mind on his Barcelona future after Hansi Flick left the defender out of his matchday squad on Sunday.

The Catalan giants travelled to Elche for their La Liga opener, with Anthony Gordon enjoying a dream debut after coming off the bench for Lamine Yamal.

3 Balde has been at the Catalan side's academy since 2011 Credit: Getty

The victory ensured Barcelona's title defence started strongly as they matched rivals Real Madrid in victory.

However, one obvious absentee was Balde, who stayed at home with his future at the club being speculated by fans.

Manchester United have made contact over a potential €40 million (£34m) deal for the 22-year-old as a cheaper alternative to Newcastle's Lewis Hall.

Barca are open to the move in order to raise funds for a new striker, while also bringing in Joao Cancelo as a replacement on the left flank.

Additionally, the emergence of young defender Xavi Espart has left Balde's place in the starting XI increasingly insecure.

Not in the head space

In Flick's pre-match press conference, the German manager hinted at the left-back's potential departure while revealing the player needed to resolve his focus:

He said: "We have to manage the minutes, I hope to have six players who can play 90 minutes.

"I spoke with Balde this morning and told him that I think he's not here at 100 per cent, clear your mind and then we'll talk.

He added: "He’s a player of immense quality, and it’s important to know if he’s confident he can compete in his position.

"That’s what I want to see from all my players. Every day I observe what they do, their level, whether they demonstrate that they’re at the level to play."

3 Flick never mentioned the move but said Balde was not 100 per cent focused Credit: Europa Press via Getty

Old Trafford dreams

Michael Carrick is keen to provide cover for Luke Shaw ahead of Man United's return to Champions League football.

After the Magpies have consistently made it clear that Hall is not for sale, they have turned their attention to Balde.

Although the full-back remains under contract with Barcelona for two more years with a nominal €1 billion (£855m) release clause, the Catalan hierarchy would prefer to cash in on the youngster, who is also pushing for a summer exit.

Balde previously expressed his desire to play for the Manchester-based side during a quick-fire Q&A on TikTok in 2020.

When asked to name 'a club other than Barcelona?', the defender immediately responded with 'United'.

The left-back has made seven appearances for Spain; however, he was left out of the World Cup squad this summer.

3 Balde continues to train with the Barca team Credit: Getty

In the Premier League, Carrick's side endured a disappointing start to their campaign with a 2-0 defeat to newly-promoted Hull City.

The Red Devils are not the only club interested in signing the 22-year-old, with Aston Villa and Benfica also keeping close tabs on the situation.

3 PSG won the Champions League last season with a penalty victory over Arsenal Credit: Getty

The 2025/26 final doesn't feel very long ago at all, but eyes are already moving on to the new season of action across Europe.

The new Champions League campaign actually started in early July with the qualifiers and they will conclude this week with the play-off round as the pots for the draw are confirmed.

Premier League champions Arsenal are going to be aiming to go one better this year, while Manchester City, Liverpool and Aston Villa will all be back in action in UEFA's elite competition again too.

Manchester United have also returned to the Champions League for the first time since the 2023/24 campaign.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle gives firm response to ex-Man United star’s cheeky jibe over club’s interest in Newcastle star
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle gives firm response to ex-Man United star’s cheeky jibe over club’s interest in Newcastle star

Add us as preferred source

Matthias Jaissle has shut down the prospect of another Newcastle United star leaving the club this summer.

The Magpies have already seen three key men leave St. James' Park during the current transfer window.

3 Jaissle has dismissed the suggestion Manchester United could sign one of his Newcastle stars Credit: Getty

Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon have all departed since the end of last season.

Despite the squad overhaul, Jaissle's side were moments away from claiming all three points against Liverpool in their season opener.

Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th minute penalty rescued a point for the Reds on Sunday.

Jaissle on Hall interest

Following the match, the Newcastle boss had an emphatic response when asked about potential transfer interest in another of his players.

Jaissle spoke to Viaplay during their post-match coverage of the opening weekend fixture.

Discussing the closing days of the transfer window, he admitted: "I think it will be a stressful period for the sporting director. We have some needs, definitely."

He added: "If you’re bringing players in, maybe there will also be some players out."

This prompted former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel to reference his old club's interest in Lewis Hall.

Schmeichel quipped: "We are looking at your left-back."

Jaissle immediately replied: "No chance, no chance."

3 There is 'no chance' Hall moves to United this summer, according to Jaissle Credit: Getty

Hall's future

The Red Devils have been long-term admirers of Hall as they look to strengthen at left-back.

However, Newcastle are keen to tie the 21-year-old down to a new contract.

Hall's current deal has three years remaining following his permanent move from Chelsea in 2024.

The England international played the full 90 minutes against Liverpool.

It was his challenge on Victor Munoz which handed the visitors their stoppage time penalty, though.

This summer's Premier League transfer window closes on Tuesday, September 1 at 11pm.

3 United have held a long-term interest in Hall, who Newcastle are keen to hand a new deal to Credit: Getty

Ahead of the deadline, Newcastle will return to action in the Carabao Cup this week.

The 2025 winners host West Brom on Wednesday night before visiting Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League on Saturday.

Sports.title: Unai Emery tipped to walk away from Aston Villa after shambles performance on opening day
Sports.content:
Unai Emery tipped to walk away from Aston Villa after shambles performance on opening day

Ally McCoist fears Unai Emery will be asking 'what's the point' after watching his Aston Villa side implode against Brighton.

The contest was wrapped up inside the opening half as the Seagulls slammed home four goals against a torrid 10-man Villa, with Joao Gomes sent for an early shower.

4 The start to the new season was not what Emery had in mind Credit: AFP

It could, and perhaps should, have been a higher scoreline, but a patched-up Villa squad managed to avoid further humiliation.

For Emery, Sunday's display was a grim reminder about the task that awaits him this season given he has lost four players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg.

Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa have all moved on this summer, while Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins - who is the subject of heavy interest from Al-Hilal - are also likely to leave.

Before the contest, Emery admitted change was coming to Villa Park but was 'definitely not expecting' just how severe the transition into a new era would be.

Why Ally McCoist believes Unai Emery could leave Aston Villa

And, worryingly, McCoist fears it may ultimately be too much for Emery to handle, especially on the back of Sunday's humiliation.

“You feel for them, it's an absolute shambles," McCoist said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"You think about the players they have lost: Tielemans, Digne, Rogers, and Konsa. It certainly looks as if Ollie Watkins has made his mind up. It looks as though he's going to take the buck and head over to Saudi.

“That squad has been absolutely decimated. I actually thought they did really well in the Super Cup final against PSG. (George) Hemmings and (Brian) Madjo did well, and I thought there was optimistic signs for them.

“But, having watched what unfolded at the weekend, I think the Villa fans have got to be really concerned about what's happening in front of them.

“I’d be really concerned with what's happening, potentially, with the manager because, surely at some point Unai Emery is going to say, what's the point?"

4 McGinn is one of the few members of Villa's core who has not left this summer Credit: Getty

Jeff Stelling's verdict on Unai Emery's future

Co-host Jeff Stelling echoed McCoist's verdict and questioned how long Emery would leave it before he 'wants to cash in his chips'.

“From the side that won the Europa League final, six of the starters are either not there or weren't playing for different reasons," Stelling said.

“When I look at the heart of that defence, and I'm sorry to pick out individuals, but if you're starting games with Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof you're going to lose more than you win.”

How Ollie Watkins contributed to Aston Villa's striker nightmare

Adding to Villa's woes on Sunday was the fact they could not field a recognised striker.

Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo, who scored in the Super Cup, were both out injured while Watkins was a no-show, with Emery hinting the England international refused to play in an effort to force through the Al-Hilal move.

As a result, midfielder Ross Barkley was forced to moonlight in the unfamiliar role of striker, although the experiment lasted until Gomes was sent off.

4 Watkins has less than two years remaining on his current Villa deal Credit: Getty

Watkins is nine goals shy of joining the Premier League's fabled 100 club, all of which have been scored for Villa.

Although McCoist acknowledged the lure of generational wealth, he felt Watkins was 'slightly young' to be making the move to Saudi Arabia.

But if this was Watkins' only chance at such a lucrative contract, McCoist recognised it was one he cannot let it pass.

Ally McCoist's thoughts on Ollie Watkins' mooted Saudi switch

"The easiest thing in the world for me is to say no," McCoist said.

"I'd be tempted to wait a couple of years and it's easy for me to sit here, but I don't know the full details.

“They might have made him an unbelievable offer, and he might be thinking it might not be there in two years.

4 Emery acknowledged previously that Villa 'have an issue' with Watkins Credit: AFP

“So he has to make a decision, and it is a financial decision. That's mainly what it is. He's obviously going to be uprooting his family and taking them to a place, which I don't know an awful lot about, but you just hear some stories.

“If you're in Bahrain, it's great. If you're not, it's not the best at all. It's a financial decision that will probably set him and generations of his family up.

“From that point of view I can understand it totally. It's easy for me to sit here and say 30's is too young.

“I think it is slightly young. In an ideal world, if you're a player like that, you don't want to go to maybe 33, 34 if you're lucky, but then he probably thinks I can't pick and choose.”

Sports.title: A scary Alexander Isak issue, the punditry duo who outshone struggling Wayne Rooney and who from Man United's 'spine' is still on the beach? IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend
Sports.content:
Without doubt the worst moment of Liverpool's dismal title defence season came when Hugo Ekitike ruptured his Achilles at Anfield against PSG last April. Not only did it rule a talented forward out until 2027, it left Liverpool relying on Alexander Isak this season and that already feels scary.

Watching Isak at St James' Park yesterday was painful. Where once – during his time at Newcastle - there was certainty and instinctive confidence, there is now only hesitancy and doubt.

Isak used to take penalties for his old club but when Liverpool won one in the 96th minute yesterday, I almost hoped he wouldn't take it. He didn't.

But Liverpool need him. They really need him and that already feels like a problem for Andoni Iraola as he tries to navigate the early weeks of his time as Liverpool manager.

As Liverpool laboured in the latter stages against Newcastle, Isak offered absolutely nothing but he stayed on the field simply because Iraola didn't really have any other option.

Alexander Isak must succeed for Liverpool - their early season prospects depend on it

Last summer – the summer of 2025 – saw a number of No 9s arrive at our big clubs. Isak to Liverpool, Benjamin Sesko to Manchester United, Liam Delap to Chelsea and Viktor Gyokeres to Arsenal. None have had it easy so Isak is not alone.

Indeed as the Premier League returned this weekend, none bar Isak started for their teams. Sesko and Gyokeres were on the bench and Delap has been frozen out entirely by new coach Xabi Alonso at Chelsea.

The difference is that United, Arsenal and Chelsea have alternatives. They can afford to start their season with big name strikers as impact players. Iraola and Liverpool do not have that option.

Cody Gakpo – criminally under-rated by some members of the Liverpool fanbase – delivered with a big goal for Liverpool yesterday and could – at a push – play through the middle. Florian Wirtz – who faces challenges of his own at Anfield – could feasibly operate as a false nine. But neither is a convincing alternative.

What Liverpool really need is for Isak to start playing like a £125m centre forward – or indeed any kind of centre forward at all. Currently he looks miles off.

It was never going to be easy returning to St James' Park where even Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle was whipping up the crowd's vitriol towards a player who once scored 54 Newcastle league goals at more than a goal every other game.

It will feel more straightforward for him when Liverpool host Nottingham Forest at Anfield next Saturday lunchtime.

But at the moment Isak looks like a player who doesn't trust either his body or his mind and that has to change very soon.

Iraola doesn't have the option of asking him to find his form gradually. That was last season's luxury.

It really has to happen now. Liverpool's early season prospects may depend upon it.

Jaissle must look in the mirror

Newcastle coach Jaissle looks as though he will be a lively and entertaining presence on the touchline. But the German was wrong to blame referee Stuart Attwell for the late penalty decision that denied his team victory. The contact from the otherwise excellent Lewis Hall on Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz was clear.

Indeed Jaissle may wish to examine his own part in what happened given that the foul came in time added on by Attwell for a totally unnecessary Newcastle substitution.

Jaissle's decision to replace Yoane Wissa with Fabian Schar in the last minute of added time was clearly designed to waste some precious moments. But all it did was prompt Attwell to add 30 seconds on and it was after 15 of those that Munoz ran at Hall to win the spot-kick.

New guidelines this season mean that players must leave the field within 10 seconds of their number being raised or risk a booking. This means that the classic 'time wasting' substitution is even more pointless than ever.

Is MOTD losing its identity?

It felt strange to see Mark Chapman at Newcastle for Sky the day after he had hosted the season's opening Match of the Day. It is something that chips away a little at the identity of the BBC's flagship show.

TNT, meanwhile, chose to use The Athletic's ace news breaker David Ornstein as one of their pre-match panellists at the Hull-Man Utd game which felt a little like a desperate attempt to jump on the back of his enormous social media following.

As for Wayne Rooney, he continues to struggle to look truly comfortable in the MOTD chair. Joe Hart and Danny Murphy were on this occasion a better combination on the Sunday show than Rooney and Alan Shearer had been 24 hours earlier.

Joe Hart and Danny Murphy were better than Wayne Rooney and Alan Shearer as pundits

A wake-up call for Carrick

Michael Carrick will now know that it really feels like to be a Manchester United manager after his team's lame defeat on Humberside.

Last season was a free hit for Carrick after he succeeded Ruben Amorim as an interim at Old Trafford. Now that he has the job, it is completely different. This is his team and therefore his responsibility.

It was on the one hand hard not to admire Carrick's frankness in his post-match interviews.

When, for example, it was suggested by former Middlesbrough striker Jan Age Fjortoft – now an excellent analyst for foreign rightsholder Viaplay – that his team had lacked 'passion'. Carrick almost bit his head off.

'That is ridiculous,' said Carrick. 'You played football. You [should] understand.'

On the other, Carrick will soon come to learn just how every single word he utters – especially after defeat – will be picked apart by a fanbase that grows ever more impatient for a league title.

For example, he spoke ahead of the Hull game about his team's spine offering him cause for comfort only to see one of the players he name-checked – centre half Harry Maguire – start the season as though he was still on the beach.

The sooner central defenders learn to concentrate on the ball at set pieces the better. When the first Hull goal went in, for example, Maguire was still so intent on holding his man that he actually had both arms wrapped round team-mate Noussair Mazraoui.

It was schoolboy stuff.

Harry Maguire started the season as though he was still on the beach for Man United

Who can be the new Sunderland?

Hull's victory may yet transpire to be a rare highlight in a hard season but it is impossible not to be pleased for a group of supporters who have been through so much since they last watched Premier League football a decade ago.

Indeed both Hull and fellow promoted club Ipswich have followed Sunderland's example of last summer by recruiting heavily to try and repurpose themselves for top-flight football.

Sunderland fielded almost a new team as they flew high last season and a year on Hull have arrived in the Premier League with seven new players – three were in the team that beat United - while Ipswich fielded seven newbies as they beat the Wearsiders at Portman Road.

Ipswich are among the biggest spenders in the Premier League, having shelled out more than £150m. As Sunderland prepare to play European football this season, it seems they may have started something.

Savinho deal doesn't add up

Tottenham have also spent heavily but after their thumping at Brentford it may be a while until we see what they will actually look like under Roberto de Zerbi.

De Zerbi is still without a number of his best players – guys like Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro were not fit to start on Saturday – while one of his anticipated new signings – the Egyptian wide player Omar Marmoush – was actually on the bench for Manchester City yesterday.

So there is much still to come for Spurs fans even if there will be pressure on Tottenham's new executive team for their signings to work out.

Paying Newcastle £100m for Sandro Tonali feels rather top heavy but that pales when compared to the £75m Tottenham have agreed to give City up front for the Brazilian winger Savinho.

The 22-year-old arrived at the Etihad for £30m two summers ago and has made only a modest impact with two Premier League goals and twelve assists.

So who at Tottenham has decided that a 150 per cent increase on value feels like a good deal?

It already feels like one of the strangest transfers in recent Premier League history and if it doesn't work Spurs fans will want answers.

Roberto de Zerbi has seen a number of expensive additions arrive at Tottenham

Arteta spot-on with Martinelli

Arsenal's squad depth is increasingly impressive – the likes of Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi were all on the bench as the champions beat Coventry – which is why Mikel Arteta feels comfortable in moving on Gabriel Martinelli.

Gunners legend Ian Wright claims Arteta's treatment of the Brazilian has been unnecessarily brutal. Martinelli was not involved at all on Friday or indeed at the Community Shield a week earlier.

But Arteta's track record at ruthlessly shipping players out when they have served their purpose is there for all to see.

The likes of Kieran Tierney, Granit Xhaka and Oleksandr Zinchenko all played significant roles in Arsenal's gradual return to eminence under the Spaniard. Indeed all three captained the club at some stage.

But all were invited to further their career elsewhere once their shelf life was reached. It can feel a little cold-hearted at times. But it has worked for Arsenal and that's what matters.

New hope for England

England assistant manager Anthony Barry – last seen struggling to hold back the tears at half-time of England's World Cup win over France – was on his native Merseyside to watch Everton down wasteful Crystal Palace and there was lots to take in.

A fabulous goal from the talented Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and an assured display from Adam Wharton will have reminded Barry and his boss Thomas Tuchel that it's possible to do something other than pack an England squad with wingers.

But Barry will also (hopefully) have noted a decent afternoon from talented Everton central defender Jarrad Branthwaite.

The Cumbrian is one of the most naturally gifted centre halves in England but has seen his progress stalled by injury. He is 24 now and it would help England enormously if he stepped up.

Ezri Konsa and new Manchester City 'midfielder' Marc Guehi (what on earth was all that about yesterday?) were very much 6/10 at the World Cup and could do with competition that isn't called Dan Burn.

Glasner needs history lesson

Former Palace manager Oliver Glasner is now at Nottingham Forest and that still feels like an odd swap, given Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis goes through managers like I go through tissues in hay fever season.

After an opening defeat to Leeds at the City Ground, Glasner suggested that it was impossible for him to suddenly make his team play like Real Madrid in the 1970s.

It was a strange thing to say, not least because Real were not winning big European trophies in that era.

A team who were? Forest, of course.

The club's two European Cup wins came in 1979 and 1980.

Oliver Glasner made strange comments about how Nottingham Forest could play

Still too many kid gloves

It was heartening to see a Premier League weekend pass without any notable VAR moments. Long may Howard Webb's 'high bar for intervention' continue. But he said this last season, too, and we know what happened.

Much of the responsibility for change continues to rest with the players, though, and that's particularly the case when it comes to all the messing about at corners and other set pieces.

As we watched Man City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma wrestle with a Bournemouth player at a corner on the TV in the Newcastle press room yesterday, a voice from the back piped up.

'It's like watching kids in a playground,' she said. It was perfectly put.

Farewell King Kev

Alan Shearer – said to be scaling back his TV schedule this season – was in Newcastle to witness a fabulous and moving tribute to the late Kevin Keegan by two of his former clubs at St James Park.

It really was a super effort by Newcastle and Liverpool and it was fitting that Keegan's family and grandchildren were in the stadium to witness it.

Sometimes football manages to get things very right indeed.

Sports.title: 'Come on, that's ridiculous!': Man United boss Michael Carrick snaps at ex-player interviewer as pressure hits on first question about his team's 'passion' after collapsing at promoted Hull City
Sports.content:
'Come on, that's ridiculous!': Man United boss Michael Carrick snaps at ex-player interviewer as pressure hits on first question about his team's 'passion' after collapsing at promoted Hull City

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Carrick snapped at a reporter's 'ridiculous' opening question after Manchester United's shock defeat by Hull City on Saturday.

The United manager was affronted when asked if his players had lost against the newly promoted club due to a lack of 'passion'.

United's Premier League season got off to a nightmare start as goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy – both stemming from set-pieces – put them to the sword in Yorkshire.

Carrick was interviewed afterwards by Viaplay broadcaster Jan Age Fjortoft, the Norwegian who played for Swindon, Middlesbrough, Sheffield United, and Barnsley in the 1990s.

'Would you accept that there was a lack of passion in the first half?' asked Fjortoft.

'Oh come on, that's ridiculous,' Carrick hit back.

Michael Carrick said it was 'ridiculous' to suggest his Manchester United team lacked passion in their 2-0 defeat by Hull City

He was vexed by the question posed by Viaplay reporter and former play Jan Age Fjortoft

“Come on, that’s ridiculous.”



Michael Carrick wasn’t happy when asked if there was a lack of passion from #mufc in their first half vs Hull.



via @ViaplayFotball pic.twitter.com/zyca5r5iSr — utdreport (@utdreport) August 23, 2026

'That's not how you would assess it?' asked Fjortoft.

Carrick replied: 'Come on, you played football, you understand, that's a ridiculous thing to say. Just because you got beat doesn't mean you don't care about it.'

Fjortoft said: 'I'm not saying that you didn't care about it. If you look at it, they came with passion, that's what I mean. I understand that you care about it, but would you accept that they took you on that front, so to say?'

'No, no. Their two goals came from set plays. Other than that, we had opportunities,' Carrick said. 'That was where the game was. I don't think it was passion or anything to do with that. I think it was just their moment that made the difference in the game.'

Fjortoft said: 'Is it these duels? Is that what you mean? That these two duels were the goals? Because they had chances. There were consequences there from the game that you could see that they would get at you.'

'It’s a game of football, it’s a Premier League game,' Carrick replied.

'It’s their first game at home, and we’ve seen it many times before. You know, I said it before the game because it was always going to be a tough game.

'And set-plays, yeah, that’s it. We’ve been decent over a period of time at dealing with them, and today we didn’t.

Any title talk for Manchester United was quickly dulled by their lacklustre performance

Semi Ajayi gave the hosts the lead after a kerfuffle in the box in the 17th minute

Nobel Mendy made matters worse for United when he added Hull's second after 38 minutes

Marcus Rashford came off the bench wearing the number nine shirt but was unable to change the match

'We can look into that, we can dissect it. We certainly won’t get carried away with the positives or the negatives. We never do. So I think we can stay calm and understand what we need to get better at.'

It was a humbling experience for Carrick, who lost just two of his 17 matches in interim charge of United.

They started with a new-look midfield in the form of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, but neither was overly convincing and the former even got nutmegged at one point.

Carrick did a fantastic job to lead United into the Champions League and the hope is that they will imitate that. Carlos Baleba is soon arriving from Brighton for £70million to further bolster their midfield.

Reporting on the match at the MKM Stadium, Daily Mail Sport's Manchester United reporter Chris Wheeler called any talk of a title challenge a 'joke'.

Wheeler wrote: 'Even in his worst nightmares, Carrick couldn't have foreseen this: an opening-day humiliation at the hands of a team that sneaked into the Premier League via the Championship play-offs in May, and have been prepped for their return to the top-flight with a summer spend of just £70million on 12 players – the same as it is costing United to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton.'

He added: 'After a summer of guarded optimism over the signing of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, the new midfield failed to launch.

'Both players were replaced midway through the second half on their Premier League debuts with United two goals down, having been eclipsed by Matt Crooks and Slater, a mere £50,000 signing from Sheffield United in 2022.

'Instead, it was the business that United haven't done that becomes the main talking point. The new striker that hasn't arrived. The missing defensive cover for Luke Shaw. Baleba, the third midfield signing, coming in too late to start the season.

Considering Carrick only lost two of his 17 games after taking over in January, this was a serious setback. He talked in the week about touting United as title contenders being 'a jump'. On this evidence, it's a joke.'

Sports.title: Harry Maguire is caught tackling his OWN TEAM-MATE in new angle of Man United's defensive horror show - as Luke Shaw's comments spark concern about weaknesses
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire's defending is again under scrutiny after the Manchester United star wrestled with his own team-mate before Hull's first goal at the weekend.

The centre-back had his arm around Noussair Mazraoui before the man he should have been marking, Semi Ajayi, bashed the ball into the net.

Had the grappling not have taken place, either Maguire or Mazraoui could have reacted and fought for the ball, which had bounced off the post into the danger area.

But perhaps the confusion makes sense after Luke Shaw raised the alarm over United's lack of preparation for set-pieces under Michael Carrick.

'Disappointing, I think we knew Hull’s strengths,' Shaw said. 'Set-plays and wide positions and crosses into the box.

'At times we did defend well, but the goals, set-plays, not good enough. We knew they were going to be good from set-plays and ultimately it’s cost us the three points today.

Harry Maguire held onto Noussair Mazraoui as Hull City scored their first goal on Saturday

Luke Shaw said afterwards that Manchester United had not prepared enough for set-pieces

Maguire has had similar moments before, such as when he brought down Shaw in 2020, leading to a Tottenham goal

'Really disappointing. It’s not us and we knew it was coming. I think as a whole, as a group, collectively, we could prepare better. Especially knowing how good they are at set-plays and what their dangers are.

'I think also going forward we were lacking that cutting edge today to score the goals and try to fight our way back into the game.'

United conceded a second goal stemming from a set-piece later in the first half when Nobel Mendy netted his first Premier League goal.

Football fans on social media were certainly confused by what they had seen.

'Maguire has done it again,' said one on X.

'Maguire please don't bring back the old version of yourself,' said another.

'He thought it was still pre-season training,' one joked.

Others stood up for the Englishman, with one saying: 'No Maguire slander would be tolerated. Man was our second best player today after Mbeumo.'

Semi Ajayi gave the hosts the lead after a kerfuffle in the box in the 17th minute

Nobel Mendy made matters worse for United when he added Hull's second after 38 minutes

Another shifted blame from Maguire, saying: 'All of them are standing like b***** statues and that's what p***** me off. Nobody charged. Nobody. Pathetic when it comes to passion.

This is not the first time Maguire has committed friendly fire and obstructed a team-mate.

He accidentally 'fouled' Shaw in 2020 against Tottenham, which resulted in a goal; once kicked Paul Pogba in the head, which forced him to leave the pitch bleeding; and appealed for a handball against team-mate Nemanja Matic in the box.

In high pressure moments, with the match moving at such speed, it is easy to become confused, but his repeated blunders in this department have left supporters befuddled.

The 33-year-old, who missed out on the World Cup, played for Hull between 2014 and 2017.

He joined United from Leicester in a record £80million deal in 2019 and, in April, signed a fresh one-year deal with the club. United also hold the option to extend it by a year.

His wages have dropped from around £180,000 per week to £120,000 in line with the club's new salary structure.
