Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: After a fortnight of fretting over floodlights on the fritz, Nelson's FA Cup journey ends at Witton Albion - where home fans toasted victory with pina coladas!
Sports.content:
Journey to Wembley: After a fortnight of fretting over floodlights on the fritz, Nelson's FA Cup journey ends at Witton Albion - where home fans toasted victory with pina coladas!

It’s the annual pina colada festival in the Witton area of Cheshire – the song about the drink, which topped the US charts in the late 1970s, was written by someone local to the place and they’ve spotted the commercial opportunity – so there are people walking around dressed as pineapples and wearing big yellow glasses on Saturday lunchtime. But life has not exactly been a cocktail party for Nelson, an East Lancashire ninth tier club, just lately.

They breeze through one of the challenges which faces them after arriving to face opponents one step above them in the pyramid. Their new yellow away kits for the season haven’t arrived and last season’s issue, which they’re still using, don’t have a No 18 jersey – needed today because you’re allowed seven subs in the FA Cup. Someone finds a white marker pen and inks the number on to a plain yellow away shirt. Wearing numbers on your back is mandatory in the tournament.

This is a minor obstacle compared with the floodlight problems which has been testing Nelson minds since we left them celebrating extra preliminary round victory at their ‘Little Wembley’ ground two weeks ago. That was the first part of our journey to Wembley told in 13 instalments, following a club as far as they go and then picking up with the team who knock them out, all the way to the final.

They’d signed off on a £30,000 contract, helped by FA grants, to replace the system of lights which had started to fail during evening games, only to find that the new ones still didn’t work.

The approved contractors didn’t seem to have mentioned that the cables and wiring supplying the lights also needed ripping out, and yet were sending the club legal letters demanding payment, as Nelson’s directors sought advice from the FA about the black hole they risked disappearing into.

Inside the home dressing room at the Bedspace Trust Community Stadium

Nelson captain Bill Priestley receives some treatment ahead of kick-off

A home steward - proudly sporting Witton Albion's colours - tucks into a pie at half-time

When we caught up with Nelson at their league away game at Charnock Richard in Lancashire, last Tuesday night, the floodlights were the prime topic of conversation as the players arrived in the car park. There had even been talk of a temporary ground move, which did not exactly delight the North West Counties League. Nelson’s proactive club sponsor Monks Contractors had offered supplying temporary structures.

In the end, they just went to work again. Volunteers helped dig two 100m trenches to lay the new cabling to the new lights and on Wednesday, they flicked the switch once more. ‘Let there be light?’ The look on Nelson director Rob Doherty’s face as the visiting contingent are welcomed into Witton’s snug little boardroom suggests so. ‘As of three days ago, they were working,’ he relates. The FA provided emergency funding.

Both these teams badly want to win this FA Cup Preliminary Round game. In his extremely modestly proportioned office Witton manager Benny Harrison, whose day job is a teacher at a special educational school, reflects at 2pm on the profound effects Marine experienced after playing Tottenham in the Third Round in 2021. The windfall helped win them two promotions in three years.

But as the rival teams’ executives gather in that boardroom, there’s a sense of mutual empathy about the existential threats which can be just around the corner for any non-league club.

‘There’s what goes on out on the pitch, and the fans and all that the lovely stuff,’ says Witton director Paul Sanderson, when Nelson relate their floodlight troubles. ‘And then there’s survivability stuff that fans don't know about. Trying to navigate things that can threaten your existence if you’re not prepared for anything.’

Nelson were on a precipice before new co-owners Stewart Fort and Chris Price arrived three years ago, invested and built up the team of volunteers who are their lifeblood. But Witton’s excellent little club museum, charting a 139-year history and signposted ‘Probably the best non-League football museum in the world’, shows that they’ve also ridden football’s rollercoaster.

The museum chronicles the club’s journey to the 1992 FA Trophy final at Wembley, where they lost to Colchester. That period, which included a brief stay in the Vauxhall Conference, saw them splashing the surplus earned after selling their old ground to Sainsburys and building a new one, on players. The rewards were painful temporary. Witton struggled when the money ran out and the new stadium required major repair sooner than anticipated.

The sun’s out, though, and the FA Cup is blowing everyone’s troubles away. ‘Welcome to the best football competition in the world by a long chalk,’ states the stadium announcer. The appropriately named Witton groundsman James Spruce is reversing his mower out onto the excellent playing surface, his partner Katy Hulse is nursing a pina colada and her friend Barbara Bazley is watching the warm-up.

Groundsman James Spruce applies the finishing touches to the playing surface

Katy Hulse (left) enjoys a pina colada with her friend Barbara Bazley

Albion statistician Phil Chadwick has helped to curate one of the best club museum's in non-League

Nelson's 87-year-old superfan Harry Manning’s immaculate handwritten notes will be converted into a match report for the local Nelson Leader

‘When you make s*** decisions, it goes pear-shaped, so if someone makes a s*** decision, back them up and help sort it out,’ shouts assistant coach Liam Lishman, as he puts the squad through their paces. Thursday’s training session focussed on not allowing Freddie Garbutt, Witton’s towering 22-year-old striker, the chance to control and shoot.

At Charnock Richard, Nelson won 2-0, led by their own dangerous target man Sefton Gonzalez, who scored and hurled himself through his trademark somersault. Today, goalkeeper Chris Thompson is back after a bout of sciatica. There’s optimism in the air.

Against the backdrop of the chemical plants in salt-mining territory, Nelson discover what they’re up against in Garbutt and Witton’s attacking pace. Nelson wing-back Darren Holden, outstanding in the previous round and at Charnock in midweek, is operating in his own half far more, protecting Nelson territory, yet removing one of the Lancashire team's attacking dimensions.

Jamie Edwards, Nelson’s force field, draws a sharp save and Gonzales has just headed a great opportunity into the ground when Witton’s Garbutt leaps to meet a corner and send his team ahead.

He’s one of only two players Witton have signed up to a contract, protecting his match fee if he’s injured and protecting the club if someone else tries to sign him, Witton chairman Graham Wood relates, back in the boardroom at half-time.

The winners today will collect £1,444 in prize money and that would be just as precious to Witton, a fan-owned club with 400 registered shareholders, none of them hugely wealthy, who are currently trying to make a community football facility.

Nelson players warm up at the side of the pitch before kick-off

Witton Albion play in the Northern Premier League Division One West, one divsion higher than Nelson

Visiting goalkeeper Chris Thompson keeps a Witton Albion player at bay

Freddy Garbutt's first-half goal settled the game and sent Witton through to the next round of the FA Cup

Home boss Ben Harrison addresses his players at full-time

‘That will bring us an income to put back into the club,’ says Wood, who has helped bring a commercial sponsorship deal with a locally based homelessness charity.

Nelson dominate a second half in which Holden is pushed forward more, encouraged by his wife Abi, who is live tweeting the match for the club’s website with another volunteer, Amy Holden, and taking photographs for next week’s match programme and the website.

In the main stand, 87-year-old superfan Harry Manning’s immaculate handwritten notes, which will be converted into a match report for the local Nelson Leader, reflect the growing frustration. The ‘18’ inked onto sub James Hooper’s jersey is impressive. But it’s raining in Nelson hearts when the whistle blows and they tumble out of the competition.

Manager Arron Ripley stands in the sun-dappled centre circle ten minutes later and reflects on the way his ambitious side are evolving. ‘Last year we’d have kept launching it in a situation like that but we’re looking after the ball. We look like we’re enjoying it. We just weren’t clinical enough.’

Nelson can return fortified to their league campaign, confident, in so many ways, that the lights will stay on.

Sports.title: England cricketer Brydon Carse handcuffed after nightclub incident - with former captain Ben Stokes spotted watching on
Sports.content:
English cricket is dealing with yet more embarrassing headlines after footage emerged of fast bowler Brydon Carse handcuffed by police outside a Derby nightclub late on Saturday.

Carse, who was part of England’s squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan and their leading wicket-taker during the Ashes defeat in Australia, was released without charge, having been out celebrating with Durham team-mates following their win over Derbyshire in the county championship.

A short video posted on social media showed Carse, 31, surrounded by four policemen outside the club, with fellow Durham stars Ben Stokes and Matthew Potts in the background. One of the policemen is heard to say: ‘Just get him over there.’

It is unclear why Carse was placed in handcuffs, and he is understood to have returned to the team hotel soon after.

The England and Wales Cricket Board said: ‘We are aware of an incident which is reported to have taken place in Derby [on Saturday] night, and are currently investigating. We will provide a further update when possible.’

No decision has yet been made over whether Carse will be removed from England’s 16-man squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s, starting on Thursday, while the ECB and the independent Cricket Regulator investigate the incident.

Brydon Carse was spotted in handcuffs surrounded by police outside a nightclub in Derby

The news comes not long after England’s new Test captain, Joe Root, abolished the team curfew that had been in place since the Ashes defeat in January, insisting his players should be trusted to behave like ‘grown adults’.

That followed a string of drink-related incidents over the past year that have sparked fresh debate about cricket’s relationship with alcohol.

In October, white-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a nightclub bouncer on the eve of a one-day international in Wellington, New Zealand – an incident the ECB hushed up until the story broke on the last day of the fifth Test against Australia at Sydney in January.

In the meantime, England’s Ashes squad spent four high-profile days between the second and third Tests in the Sunshine Coast resort of Noosa. Opening batsman Ben Duckett was filmed by a member of the public slurring his words during a late-night exchange, while observers likened the trip to a ‘stag-do’.

In June, Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test against New Zealand after they broke the team curfew at a west London nightclub celebrating England’s first-Test win at Lord’s. They both claimed they didn’t know the curfew still operated after the end of a home Test, and Stokes retired from international cricket soon after.

Carse, who has won 14 Test caps, has been in trouble with the authorities before, having been suspended for three months in 2024 for historic betting offences, which involved placing 303 bets on matches between 2017 and 2019.

Sports.title: 'No chance!': Peter Schmeichel is shot down live on TV by Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle on Man United's hopes of signing Lewis Hall
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle hilariously dismissed Man United's hopes of signing Lewis Hall live on TV.

Speaking in the aftermath of his side's 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St James' Park on Sunday, Jaissle was conducting a pitchside interview with Viaplay.

As the conversation turned to the transfer market, Jaissle was pressed on whether he hoped Newcastle would do any further business during what has been a turbulent summer for the club.

Key players Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon have already departed, and there has also been speculation over the futures of other stars including Joe Willock, Tino Livramento and Hall.

And when questioned on his aspirations to sign more players, Jaissle responded: 'I think it will be a stressful period for the sporting director, because we have some needs.

'But if we bring players in maybe there will also be some players who go out.'

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle shot down Man United's hopes of signing Lewis Hall

Hall has been linked to United this summer, but Jaissle insisted the left-back is going nowhere

Former Man United keeper Peter Schmeichel, who played 398 times for the club, then cheekily said: 'We are looking at your left back.'

That comment was in reference to Hall, with United having made enquiries for the defender this summer.

But to that, Jaissle said: 'No chance, no chance,' as he chuckled.

Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this month that Hall has been on United's radar as it is clear they need to strengthen that position, with Luke Shaw, now 31, in the final year of his contract while youngster Harry Amass has been told he may be best leaving for first team football.

Hall, 21, has three years left on his current deal, and would require a substantial fee, with the defender now seen as one of Newcastle's biggest assets after joining from Chelsea in 2023.

United, meanwhile, feel they are light in the position. Shaw started all 38 Premier League matches last season, though there is no obvious back-up, with Patrick Dorgu viewed as a winger by Michael Carrick.

Jaissle's comments came after an impressive opening day performance from Newcastle as they drew 2-2 with Liverpool.

They had looked set for all three points after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock had them 2-1 ahead, but Dominik Szoboszlai equalised with a penalty in the 99th minute.

'In the end, I am a bit disappointed,' the German said after the game. 'But there is also some brightness, definitely, because the guys were doing an amazing job for over 90 minutes.

'We are a young squad and they really left their heart on the pitch and this is something we can build on.

'I'm proud. We are proud to see a unit on the pitch. The guys were trying to do it the intense way that we wanted to play. Front-footed, vertical in our approach.

'This, after such a short amount of time, I'm really happy. I felt the goosebumps straight away. You get energy from the stands and you just want to deliver it on the pitch. This synergy will be something special.'

Sports.title: Mutiny-hit Match of the Day review: BBC try to go with same old, same old amid Alan Shearer backing out - and no sign of the 'modernisation'
Sports.content:
Before the action, we had that lovely old intro, old clips, old voices, old logos, old Kenneth Wolstenholme telling us from August 1964: 'Welcome to Match of the Day.'

Ah, familiarity, our old friend. Despite an addiction to trying to fix what is not broken, the BBC begin each and every MOTD by celebrating how long this staple of Saturday nights has been on our screens, since a time when Wolstenholme was being beamed to us in black and white.

It was at least with relief that the Beeb stuck with this theme of familiarity for their first broadcast of the 2026-27 season, if accompanied by some apprehension over whether that feeling would last.

They had advertised their new line-up this last week, after all, telling us to expect to see Thomas Frank, Toby Alderweireld, Robbie Keane and Ashley Young on our screens while simultaneously plugging their four new YouTube shows in a bid to tap into the young'uns.

Got to modernise. Go after the audience that apparently doesn't think terrestrially.

But this particular MOTD was more a case of same old, same old, and not only because it started with that vintage montage and theme tune which, if they tried to bin next in favour of some modern track, I'd be tempted to launch a petition of my own.

The BBC stuck with a sense of familiarity for the first Match of the Day of the season

I would launch a petition if they ever changed the show's opening, writes Kieran Gill

The Beeb did not want to suddenly beam fresh faces into our living rooms. They saved the new blood, and scrutiny, for another time. Instead we saw those we know and trust.

Mark Chapman was in the hot seat. We know Chappers. We like Chappers. He, along with Kelly Cates and Gabby Logan, were chosen well as Gary Lineker's successors.

After a week in which we learned there is discontent behind the scenes at MOTD at the direction of this crown jewel's travel, Chapman's tongue-in-cheek opener was: 'Happy new season. Match of the Day returns. We're all smiles here. Just look at Alan Shearer and Wayne Rooney.'

More familiarity. We like them, too. They add to the broadcast. We could watch the highlights online if we wanted, hours before MOTD. We tune in because it adds analysis in between the action, including the stylish statistical graphics they show, and that is what we want.

When we will next see Shearer in one of these seats, who knows. We are told he has scaled back his contractual commitments, and as well as giving him back his weekends by only doing one show a month if that, he supposedly has beef with those above him.

In his place, Frank should be a good addition. He has authority. Despite what happened with Tottenham Hotspur, he is a fine, modern, intelligent coach, and impressed during the 2026 World Cup, which the BBC predominantly covered from Salford as we know.

Also entering via the revolving door, Alderweireld and Keane can expect their takes on Spurs will end up being separate stories online, especially if they are controversial.

Rooney branding Manchester United's defending as 'schoolboy' on Saturday will have had the odd news editor tempted to ask for copy to be bashed up, I'm sure.

Alan Shearer and Wayne Rooney are good pundits, but we will see a heavily revolving cast

Yet it will be intriguing to see how they all click together and if there is chemistry, the type that Shearer, Richards and Lineker forged over time spent working together. Apparently that concern surrounding camaraderie forms part of the mutiny occurring within MOTD.

Millions still trust their Saturday nights in the hands of the BBC. Myself included, having watched this show since my parents let me stay up late enough to do so.

Those of us who love the company of MOTD never want it to go the same way as Football Focus, its sister show which ended in May after 52 years on air.

Changing it too much would be a risk. At least the Beeb saw enough sense to show us what we wanted to see on this occasion as we settled in for Hull's big win on their return to the Premier League and the other highlights thereafter. On to what next week brings.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs get transfer wake-up call as top-four hopefuls exposed
Sports.content:
The Premier League's opening weekend provided some telling signs as each club's summer business - the ins and the outs - were magnified.

Arsenal remain the club to catch but several of their rivals were dealt reality checks. Manchester United and Aston Villa were top-four finishers last season but both opened their campaigns with a defeat.

Michael Carrick's side were stunned at newly promoted Hull despite their midfield recruits being present. Unai Emery has seen his Europa League winners gutted amid talk of a need for transition, but Villa were ripped apart at Brighton with more exits on the cards.

Liverpool's midfield deficiencies were exposed at Newcastle, who themselves showed plenty of promise after summer that saw their top players leave, casting doubt over the project at St James' Park.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Chelsea and Fulham will round out the weekend on Monday night, they're yet to show their hand, but whilst there's no need to panic after one game the weekend's action certainly showed that some teams may have more work to do than they realised.

Mirror Football's writers takes a look at which club will need to have a massive week as the summer transfer window draws to a close.

Nathan Ridley - Aston Villa

It may seem obvious but it's impossible to ignore the scale of Villa's task in the final week of the window. Not only have they lost Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, there's a real possibility that Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez could follow them out the exit door.

‌



Although Sunday's drubbing at the hands of Brighton was probably a freak result, the warning signs were there. The biggest reason they need to make signings and do their best to retain both Watkins and Martinez is to keep Unai Emery happy.

View 5 Images Unai Emery could end up losing six of his Europa League-winning starting XI

Leaving the Spaniard with a threadbare squad on their return to the Champions League could cause him to lose faith in Villa's ambitions at a time when his stock is at an all-time high. There aren't many clubs in world football who'd turn Emery down, and he remains Villa's greatest asset.

John Cross - Liverpool

With just over a week to go of the transfer window, Liverpool are most in need of reinforcements. This is a crossroads moment for Andoni Iraola because they so obviously need new signings to be a club challenging for the title this season.

‌



Without major new recruits, Liverpool would be in serious danger of falling away with the season becoming all about a scrap for a Champions League place.

Liverpool boss Iraola was a really exciting appointment because he plays with intensity, pace and speed. It feels obvious that Liverpool need more in central midfield and the wide areas.

View 5 Images Liverpool have chased Bradley Barcola all summer (Image: Getty Images)

There is no surprise that they want Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh because they are fast, quick and dangerous wingers who would fit into the Iraola style.

‌



If they get one or both of those players then maybe Liverpool can step up into being genuine challengers but they do also lack something in midfield. Iraola is all about pressing, intensity and, at Newcastle, Liverpool lacked some of that energy to allow Florian Wirtz to really excel.

Sky pundit Gary Neville was spot on: Liverpool do need more from Wirtz and Alexander Isak this season. No-one can doubt Liverpool’s ambition or backing in the market.

Other clubs could do with the odd player. But not like Liverpool. For Liverpool, this is all about defining their season and immediate future. But they really need to invest again to stop the club flatlining this season. They are better than that.

James Whaling - Crystal Palace

Of all the results on the opening weekend, I think Crystal Palace's 2-0 defeat by Everton probably went under the radar.

‌



I fear for Palace. Their manager is untested in the Premier League, they have sold Maxime Lacroix to Chelsea and could yet lose Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta. The swap deal involving Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson is headscratching to say the least.

View 5 Images Jean-Philippe Mateta is looking to get out of Selhurst Park (Image: PA)

Everton fans will tell you they themselves need to do business before the window slams shut, so for them to swat aside Palace so easily should set alarm bells ringing. The Eagles have enjoyed probably the best couple of years in their history winning the FA Cup and UEFA Conference League. But with Europa League football to contend with as well as the grind of the top flight, their squad needs desperate reinforcements if they are to avoid a relegation scrap.

Sam Meade - Aston Villa

All this talk of a rebuild. It is only a rebuild if you bring in the type of quality you've let go, and the Europa League winners have simply not done that.

‌



Not only have they lost bucket loads of quality, but they've lost the continuity they'd enjoyed for so many years. Starting with Emi Buendia as your No 9 on the opening day of the season is just unforgivable, even if Ollie Watkins is seemingly taking matters into his own hands to force an exit.

Villa have punched above their weight to achieve what they have over the last three years or so, but they are now greatly under resourced. You cannot have your best manager in a generation and not give him the tools. It won't end well and they need to act with some serious conviction in the coming days.

Alex Richards - Brentford

There are a lot of teams that the opening day proved need to do some very good business in the coming week or so. Liverpool need another game-changer in attack, Spurs need all manner of help despite all the money they've spent already and Aston Villa, particularly if Ollie Watkins is becoming the latest out the exit door, pretty much need a new centre-back, No.10 and centre-forward.

View 5 Images Brentford could only be a signing away from securing a European spot

‌



But the one I'd really like to see make a move is Brentford. Go and get the kind of midfielder that will get you 10-15 goals this season. I don't care if you break your transfer record or find another uncut gem for a fraction of the cost. Just go and get someone that plugs straight into that midfield and will feast off the chaos that Kevin Schade, Igor Thiago and Dango Outtara cause in attack.

Because that Spurs win, the comparative ease with which they dealt with their London neighbours and the Bees' ability to both go direct and now play on the floor, really more than they ever have before, tells me Keith Andrews' side can be in the Champions League mix.

They were't far off nabbing a European spot last term, only missing out on the final day. A midfielder who hits double figures would get them there.

‌

Sports.title: Golf news: Rory McIlroy reacts to 'stupid' decision as star clashes with fan
Sports.content:
Golf news: Rory McIlroy reacts to 'stupid' decision as star clashes with fan

The BMW Championship crowned a new winner on Sunday as Rory McIlroy found himself in title contention once again on the PGA Tour

View 4 Images Wyndham Clark won the BMW Championship 2026 at Bellerive Country Club (Image: Getty)

Wyndham Clark almost let an almighty lead slip but held on to win the BMW Championship by three strokes on Sunday. Rory McIlroy had closed the gap on the American heading into the final few holes, but Clark upped his game to seal the £2.6million top prize.

‌



The BMW Championship was held at Missouri's Bellerive Country Club for the 2026 edition, with Scottie Scheffler the defending champion. However, it was his compatriot Clark who got off to a fast start with an opening 64, alongside the likes of McIlroy and Gary Woodland.

‌



The US Open winner then took up the solo lead after round two and didn't look back. Despite entering the last day five shots clear of McIlroy, the Northern Irishman did close the gap. But three birdies on the final three holes from Clark meant McIlroy had to settle for third and Patrick Cantlay finished as runner-up.

‌



However, McIlroy made an error on 17 that he later branded "stupid" as Mirror Sport brings you all the latest news from the world of golf.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rory McIlroy blows chance to pocket £1.64m as he reacts to BMW Championship collapse READ MORE :

'Typical' Rory McIlroy called out as LIV Golf stars divisively invited to Alfred Dunhill READ MORE :

Rory McIlroy's "stupid" decision

Having cut Clark's lead down on the final day, McIlroy entered the par-five 17th just one stroke behind the American. But he found the rough off the tee and went bunker to bunker after a misexecuted lay-up.

‌



View 4 Images McIlroy came up just short (Image: Getty)

McIlroy's tournament hopes were ended with a bogey, and he lamented his decision whilst speaking to CBS Sports. He said: "I tried to get it up a bit too far. I should have been taking that left bunker out of play.

"If you're going to lay it up, lay it up, so just another stupid decision with a lay-up on a par-five that cost me. I can't be too disappointed. I'm probably not playing well enough to be disappointed that I didn't win.

‌



"I had my chances on the back nine and hit a lot of good putts that didn't go in. Wyndham Clark stepped up when he needed to. His birdie on 16 was huge and the way he played the last three holes, he showed a lot of character."

Golfer clashes with a fan

LIV Golf Indianapolis also took place over the weekend, and on Saturday, the iconic Bubba Watson had an altercation with a rather unruly fan.

Watson was playing his round with Lee Westwood and Bryson DeChambeau at Chatham Hills when a fan screamed as Westwood was in his pre-shot routine.

‌



View 4 Images Watson had an interaction with a fan (Image: Getty)

The Englishman had to step back and compose himself once more when his playing partner, Watson, took umbrage at the act. A clip that has surfaced online appears to show Watson exchanging words with the fan in an agitated manner.

"Oh, you don't want to say anything now? Say something, I'm looking at you, say it," Watson said, before staring the person down and walking towards the green.

‌



LIV rookie makes history

Watson, Westwood and DeChambeau were joined at LIV Indianapolis by HyFlyers GC rookie Michael La Sasso. And although many a star name graced the field, La Sasso came out on top.

The American shot an incredible 60 in Round Two to launch him into contention, and although Jon Rahm was on his tail during the final day, he held on, becoming the youngest winner in LIV Golf history.

View 4 Images La Sasso claimed LIV victory for the first time (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

As uncertainty lingered, with Saudi Arabia's PIF no longer funding LIV beyond the season that concluded on Sunday, La Sasso was soaked in champagne by his team-mates.

"I had a bunch of buddies texting me last night asking if they should fly in, and I said I was going to win anyway, but you might as well come for the show," said La Sasso. "It ended up working itself out."

Sports.title: Billionaire bookie boss Denise Coates revealed as owner of £600k Dan Skelton jumper
Sports.content:
Billionaire bookie boss Denise Coates revealed as owner of £600k Dan Skelton jumper

The founder and CEO of Bet365, who is one of Britain’s wealthiest women, is now listed as the owner of the four-year-old Push The Limit who won at Glorious Goodwood when trained by Ralph Beckett

View 3 Images Denise Coates: has become a racehorse owner

Billionaire bookmaker boss Denise Coates has joined the ranks of racehorse owners for the first time.

‌



One of Britain’s most successful business people, she is the founder and chief executive of online brand Bet365 and has a net worth of £9.5 billion. She is the eldest daughter of Peter Coates, chairman of Stoke City FC, gaining experience working in her father’s betting shop before establishing Bet365 as one of the world’s largest online betting operations.

‌



In 2024, with her husband Richard Smith, she registered Coates-Smith Racing lp with Companies House as an ‘owner of horses’ and has now acquired the first racehorse.

‌



Push The Limit won two of his six starts on the Flat when trained by Ralph Beckett, including a valuable handicap at last year’s Glorious Goodwood meeting.

He was then bought at the October Sales by champion trainer Dan Skelton and Ryan Mahon for £609,000. The gelding has now been registered to Coates-Smith Racing and with a Flat rating of 103 could be an exciting prospect over jumps.

Skelton, speaking to the Nick Luck Daily Podcast, said: “We feel very lucky to have the family’s support. We did lots with the horse last year but we just felt that physically he was still to turn a corner and switch on to full jumps mode.

‌



View 3 Images Push The Limit: has joined champion jumps trainer Dan Skelton

“He did jump very, very nicely but we felt like a bit of time, given he was such a young horse, would be no negative whatsoever.

“He is only a four-year-old and I think it’s the best thing we’ve done is give him that time. He is moving particularly well, looks great, he’s quite a flashy character - he’s chestnut with white socks - and we did like everything we saw.

‌



“By the time you get mid-way through the season there was only half of it to go and you’re better off having a full run at novice season. Everybody was quite happy to give him a bit of time. Physically I can only say that has definitely been the right thing to do.”

View 3 Images Dan Skelton: became champion jumps trainer for the first time in April (Image: David Davies/PA Wire for The Jockey Club)

Skelton said Push The Limit could make his debut in October.

Article continues below

“I don’t think he’s a horse that wants really soft ground. I’d like to get him out, once we do get some rain in the country, and I’d imagine he’d be ready to run mid or end of October and take a view from there.

“On the track he looked very good and from what we’ve seen at home we like him as well – pretty exciting stuff.”

Sports.title: Arsenal discover Julian Alvarez price tag as Atletico Madrid perform U-turn on transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal discover Julian Alvarez price tag as Atletico Madrid perform U-turn on transfer

Julian Alvarez endured a frosty reception during Atletico Madrid's opening game of the season as his side refuse to sell to Barcelona, but Arsenal remain in the wings

View 2 Images Arsenal remain interested in Julian Alvarez with Atletico Madrid refusing to sell to a La Liga rival

Atletico Madrid internally believe that the only way Julian Alvarez will leave this summer is if Arsenal sign him - despite previously being adamant he wouldn't be sold.

‌



Alvarez faced a hostile reception as Atletico played at home over the weekend with the Argentine making it clear that he wants to leave the Spanish capital. He's made it known, without naming them, that his "dream" would be to join Barcelona.

‌



Atletico though are adamant they will not sell to a fellow La Liga rival, which leaves Barcelona's hopes of signing the forward extremely unlikely. Real Madrid expressed an interest earlier this summer, but Atletico didn't believe their offer to be genuine.

‌



Arsenal are the only non-Spanish side interested as they look to add star quality in the final third. The Athletic has been told that the only scenario Atletico foresee which ends with Alvarez leaving would be if Arsenal made a €150million (£128m) offer.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It appears unlikely that the Gunners, despite their continued investment in their squad, would table such a bid. Arsenal have Viktor Gyokeres and Gabriel Jesus as genuine No.9s, although the latter is tipped to leave. Kai Havertz is more of a false 9 and is currently the preferred option to lead the attack.

‌



Gary Neville claimed on Sky Sports that adding Alvarez would see the likes of Martin Odegaard go to another level, given the way the Argentine would change the dynamic of the team's attack.

Despite the toxicity that was evident during Atletico's clash at the weekend, Diego Simeone underlined the need for the club to be united if they want to win titles.

View 2 Images Arsenal have been linked with a move for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez. (Image: (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images))

‌



He said: “I’m not here to give advice. What I have to do is concentrate on my work, which is, from a sporting sense, to give my best for Atletico Madrid. The only thing I know is that if Atletico Madrid want to win a title, we need to be together, we need to have forwards, and we need to have important forwards. And for that, we need to work on it as a result, everyone, on what we need.”

Goalkeeper Jan Oblak echoed that as he told DAZN: “Julian is here, he’s with us in the team and while he’s with us, we’re going to support him and we want him in the best way. Unfortunately, it’s a situation that isn’t comfortable for anyone, but hopefully all that is sorted out and at the end of the season we can all be happy.”

Atletico’s refusal to engage in talks with Barcelona has forced their sporting director Deco to eye up other striking options. Last week he maintained that the Catalans would sign a striker, especially after the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

Article continues below

He told local outlet TV3: “We have solutions in the team (for the central striker role), but we will probably make a move before the end of the transfer window." Reports claim Inter Milan’s Lautaro Martinez is on their shortlist, but the Italian side see their captain as an unsellable asset.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid dressing room stance on Julian Alvarez transfer noise as Arsenal chase heats up
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid dressing room stance on Julian Alvarez transfer noise as Arsenal chase heats up

Arsenal transfer target Julian Alvarez was booed on his return to action for Atletico Madrid with Jan Oblak speaking out on his situation

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez has the support of the Atletico Madrid squad after being booed amid his uncertain future (Image: (Photo by Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

Julian Alvarez has the support of the Atletico Madrid squad according to goalkeeper Jan Oblak after he was booed on his return. The Arsenal transfer target has been pushing for a move away but Atletico have no plans to sell to his dream club Barcelona which has opened the door for a return to the Premier League.

‌



The Argentine was absent for their La Liga opener earlier this week but was named in the squad for the visit of Villareal. Diego Simeone brought him on in the second half with Atletico scoring a late equaliser in front of their home supporters.

‌



While the majority of Atletico's players went around the pitch and clapped their fans, Alvarez was instructed to leave the pitch. As he trudged down the tunnel accompanied by club officials, he was heavily booed and jeered.

‌



Oblak has now spoken out on the incident and his future while also confirming he has the support of Atletico players despite the uncomfortable situation.

He told DAZN: "We all need to be united. Julian is here, he's with us in the team and while he's with us, we're going to support him and we want him in the best way.

"Unfortunately, it's a situation that isn't comfortable for anyone, but hopefully all that is sorted out and at the end of the season we can all be happy."

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

When pressed about the whistles directed at Alvarez and what advice he might offer him, Diego Simeone said: "I'm not here to give advice. What I have to do is concentrate on my work, which is, from a sporting sense, to give my best for Atletico Madrid.

"The only thing I know is that if Atletico Madrid want to win a title, we need to be together, we need to have forwards, and we need to have important forwards. And for that, we need to work on it as a result, everyone, on what we need."

‌



View 2 Images Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone has spoken about the Julian Alvarez situation

Simeone also disclosed that the decision to prevent Alvarez from approaching the home supporters came from senior figures at the club.

He added: "People at the club told me that the club decided he shouldn't go near the stands or the fans. It was the club's decision to keep him away and separate him so he could go to the locker room."

Article continues below

Atletico have no intention of selling to Barcelona and would apparently only authorise a transfer to Arsenal for a nine-figure sum.

The Gunners seem unlikely to meet that valuation, but offloading Gabriel Martinelli to Al Hilal for a record fee could provide them with sufficient funds to table a bid that Atletico might accept, given the Alvarez situation is becoming increasingly difficult to manage.

Sports.title: Jarrod Bowen could land Premier League return in £50m transfer despite contract vow
Sports.content:
Jarrod Bowen could land Premier League return in £50m transfer despite contract vow

Jarrod Bowen has pledged his future to West Ham but the winger is still the subject of Premier League interest as Crystal Palace consider a move

View 2 Images Jarrod Bowen only signed a new deal this summer, but could still have offers to leave West Ham (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

West Ham talisman Jarrod Bowen could be handed a route back into the Premier League with Crystal Palace eyeing a £50million bid.

‌



The forward has, so far, chosen to remain with the Hammers despite their relegation to the Championship. Bowen has more than proven himself to be top-flight quality, earning England caps whilst at the London Stadium, and has pledged his future to the club.

‌



The 29-year-old signed a new deal to continue captaining West Ham in the summer, but the Eagles are still ready to test his resolve by tabling an offer. The Hammers still need to toe the line financially and landing a sizeable transfer fee would prove beneficial, but Bowen remains their star man and is a fan favourite.

‌



Palace are ready to test the water and want Bowen to replace Ismalia Sarr, who is keen to leave for Galatasaray, reports The Sun. The Turkish side are looking to secure a £34m switch for a player who scored 21 times last term and is clearly pushing for the exit door.

New Eagles boss Pierre Sage left Sarr out of the squad that lost 2-0 at Everton on the opening weekend of the season and Galatasaray want to wrap up a deal within a week, which would leave Palace seeking a replacement.

Bowen scored 11 times for West Ham last season but the south Londoners have been long-time admirers of the Englishman. Palace were frontrunners to sign Bowen from Hull back in January 2020 before the Hammers ended up winning the race for his signature.

‌



West Ham supporters are already frustrated having seen their team, who were pre-season favourites for promotion, fail to win either of their two games.

View 2 Images Ismaila Sarr is looking to leave Crystal Palace

Charlton secured a 2-1 win at the London Stadium on Saturday. Taty Castellanos missed a stoppage-time penalty to rescue a point for West Ham and supporters were left puzzled as to why Bowen did not take it.

‌



The winger's legacy at the Hammers is secure - he was the man who scored the last-minute winner as the club won the UEFA Conference League back in 2023, which was their first European trophy since 1965.

Bowen has since come out and claimed he didn't want to leave the club off the back of a relegation, which motivated him to sign a new deal at West Ham.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher adamant Liverpool tactic 'cannot work' as issue rears its head
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher adamant Liverpool tactic 'cannot work' as issue rears its head

Jamie Carragher has called out Liverpool's midfield after Newcastle continued to catch them out on the counter attack with the former Red citing it as an issue for some time

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has continue to flag issues with the Liverpool midfield (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Jamie Carragher continued to bemoan the make up of Liverpool's midfield during their draw at Newcastle insisting it "cannot work" given the players they pick.

‌



The Reds needed a last minute penalty to rescue a 2-2 draw, but were behind for the majority of the contest at St James' Park. Both Newcastle goals were scored on the counter attack with pace and direct running cutting through Liverpool on the transition.

‌



Andoni Iraola started with Florian Wirtz as his 10 and Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai sitting in behind. The Reds have lacked a natural defensive midfielder for several years, and their issues with containing quick breaks has been apparent since last season.

‌



Newcastle were able to expose those and Carragher was left frustrated, insisting the problems were clear to see in pre-season and will remain whilst Liverpool continue to play with their current three-man midfield.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

After Anthony Elanga put Newcastle in front after four minutes the Sky Sports pundit said on social media: "LFC midfield all bombing forward happened all pre-season, madness!"

‌



Yoane Wissa was allowed to travel almost half the pitch before laying on Joe Willock to put Newcastle ahead, and Carragher was seemingly repeating himself. He posted: "Again! This midfield cannot work, I said it before a competitive ball was kicked."

Back when Liverpool were winning the Premier League and Champions League under Jurgen Klopp they had a midfield that consisted of Fabinho, Georginio Wijnaldum and Jordan Henderson, which gave the team the balance they were looking for.

View 2 Images Newcastle enjoyed success on the counter attack

‌



They have all departed Anfield and Carragher has been flagging for some time that Liverpool no longer have the profile of midfielder who is more defensive. Instead, he called out the amount of attacking players in their starting XI and claims top teams don't operate with the end-to-end style that is often seen in Liverpool games.

"Liverpool have too many attacking players on the pitch, they just want to bomb forward," he said on the Overlap before the season kicked off. "And it’s the same in pre-season at Liverpool this season - it’s just a basketball game. No top team plays football like that. I don’t believe it."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
