Sports.title: Stroll demanded penalties after Bearman and Bortoleto passed red pit exit light | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lance Stroll urged race control to penalise two of his rivals for leaving the pit lane while a red light was shown during the Dutch Grand Prix.

The incident occured as the field left the pits when the race resumed following the stoppage caused by Max Verstappen’s crash.

The pit lane exit lights were green as the field began to leave the pits. However after Fernando Alonso passed by the signal changed to a flashing red light.

Oliver Bearman and Gabriel Bortoleto both drove past the flashing red light. Neither acknowledged the pit lane exit had been closed and continued to the grid, though Bearman suffered a power unit failure before he got there.

Stroll, who was following the pair, noticed the light had changed and alerted his race engineer Gary Gannon:

Stroll The lights red, huh? Light’s red. Gannon Checking, I’m checking. Stroll I’m not going unless it’s green. Gannon Yeah, understood Lance. Stroll 10 seconds later

Tell me if I can go or not. Gannon Waiting to hear back from the FIA.

The signal changes to green and Stroll leaves the pit exit

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

He repeatedly called for the drivers who had passed the red signal to be penalised. Stroll correctly noted that Formula 1’s penalty guidelines state drivers who pass a red light at the pit lane exit during a race should receive 10-second stop-and-go penalties:

Stroll So everybody that went under a red should get a penalty. Gannon Yep, yep. Stroll Stop and go. Gannon Understood, we’ll report it. So the back of the pack… Stroll It’s the rules. Gannon …the back of the pack is in nine, so you can build temp. Good pushing to build temp

Stroll appeared to be under the impression that many more drivers than just the two immediately in front of him had driven past the red signal:

Stroll It’s clear that everyone went under red, then they all should get a penalty. Gannon We’re checking it now. Stroll Stop and go. Gannon Yeah, we’re checking now. Stroll Everybody. Gannon It started out green and then it went red and we’re checking who went through red and reporting it ASAP. Absolutely Lance.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The Aston Martin driver continued to press his case on the formation lap, even when his race engineer was trying to warn him about Bearman’s stoppage ahead:

Gannon ‘Bearman is slow between 10-11. Yellow ahead for Bearman stopped. Bearman stopped between 10-11. Watch for Bearman… Stroll Those are the rules. Gannon …there, watch for Bearmen. Stroll The rules are: it’s red… Gannon Lance, we’ve reported it, we reported it. Now let’s get focused getting around to the grid, okay? We’ve reported and they will action it.

However the stewards chose instead to only reprimand the pair, pointing out that the incident occured before the race resumption and neither had gained an advantage.

“The pit exit light turned red when the driver was approaching the pit exit to join the track for the re-start of the race after a suspension,” they noted. “Such an infringement happening during the race normally requires a very significant penalty as the drivers are obliged to obey light signals at all times. However, in this case the infringement did not happen during a live race, but rather on the build-up before the re-start, although the race had technically already resumed in accordance with Article B5.15.2g.

“In addition to that, the stewards acknowledge that neither any advantage was gained nor any potentially dangerous or unsafe situation was created. Therefore a reprimand to the driver is deemed appropriate given the mitigating circumstances and the unique scenario.”

Sports.title: Mercedes is “clearly not the fastest car on the grid any more” claims Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes are no longer the team to beat in Formula 1 claimed Andrea Kimi Antonelli after McLaren’s second consecutive victory in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Lando Norris passed Antonelli on his way to victory in yesterday’s race at Zandvoort, as he did in the previous round in Hungary.

“For sure, we’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid,” said Antonelli, who holds a 59-point lead in the drivers’ championship. “We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought.”

However Antonelli has high hopes for Mercedes’ forthcoming upgrade for its W17. “The team has been working super-hard on this next package that is coming up and they just want to make sure that it’s going to work out well once we put it on,” he said.

“So for sure, in this race, it’s going to be more difficult, it’s going to be challenging, but we’re ready to do our best and to maximise every opportunity. And then hopefully it’s going to be our turn to bring the package that’s going to give us a little bit of the upper hand again.”

Antonelli’s team mate George Russell believes McLaren’s strength in the last two races has been partly due to the similarities in the track layouts.

“I don’t think it’s a major surprise for us, seeing how competitive Lando was this weekend, considering he won in Budapest,” he said. “It’s a very similar circuit with the long corners, high tyre degradation, with the two-stop strategy, so there’s a lot of similarities between the two circuits.

“I think this may continue for the coming two or three races until we start to bring more to the car, and fingers crossed our competitors don’t.”

He expects Mercedes will be “slightly more competitive” in the next race at Monza, the fastest circuit on the calendar. “However, I believe Ferrari have an engine upgrade incoming, and the truth is we just don’t know.

“But I do believe that these high-degradation circuits really suit McLaren very well, and especially Lando. He’s always been a bit of a specialist in those conditions. We also saw it last year. Monza may be slightly different, but I think they are the team to beat right now.”

Sports.title: Russell defends “fair” decision to let Antonelli into second place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli ran ahead of Russell until he made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period. When Antonelli closed on Russell afterwards, Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.

Russell complied, though it handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight between the pair of them. That erased the gain Russell made in the previous day’s sprint race.

However Russell said letting his team mate by was the correct thing to do for Mercedes.

“We’ve always said as a team, when we’re on different strategies, we’re never going to fight and we’re always going to invert, and that’s always just been our rules,” he explained.

“The fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.”

Although Russell believes there was a chance he could have successfully defended his position from Antonelli – as he later did with Lewis Hamilton, thanks partly to the timing of another VSC period – he also said trying to defend could have compromised his race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally it could have been a P5 as well. So, in the end, you know, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me.”

Russell fell behind Antonelli at the start of the race, then got stuck behind Oscar Piastri and never managed to get back on terms with his team mate. “It was tough,” he said.

“The first VSC came at a pretty awkward timing for me because I felt really strong on the hard [tyre]. I think Kimi’s and my race was kind of the opposite. I had a tough medium stint, he had a very strong medium stint, then I had a strong hard stint, he was struggling.

“But that VSC gave Lewis a free pit stop and obviously Kimi pitted as well. And from there on in, I knew I was going to be under threat.

“I was managing enough in the high-speed corners to allow me to be fast in sector three and defending into turn one [Tarzan]. So I was pleased with that performance.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says extra pit stop “put George at risk” too | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was not convinced his extra pit stop in the Dutch Grand Prix was the right decision as it risked compromising his race.

The Mercedes driver made an extra pit stop 16 laps from the end of the race, taking advantage of a late Virtual Safety Car period. It dropped him from second place to third behind his team mate George Russell

Antonelli was able to repass his team mate for second place after Mercedes ordered Russell to let him through. However Antonelli was unable to gain on race leader Lando Norris.

Afterwards Antonelli said the strategy call had unnecessarily risked both their races, even though he had been struggling on his previous set of tyres.

“It was a difficult second half for me, especially in the last stint on the hards,” he said. “I was just really struggling. I had little confidence in the car and it was not easy.

“Then obviously we pitted [under the VSC] and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

“But I still think probably we could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set [of tyres] because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.”

Although he led most of the race, Antonelli said he was unlikely to win it. “I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were,” he said. “”I think today [second place] was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong.”

“It was a good ending of a difficult weekend for me where I struggled with the feeling of the car, did a lot of mistakes on my side – sprint quali, quali, also in today’s race with Lando I could have defended a bit better,” he added. “So for sure there were things that I didn’t do well this weekend, and for sure the feeling wasn’t as good.”

Sports.title: Moses Itauma’s Record Chase Cannot Sell Hrgovic PPV
Sports.content:
Mentioning Tyson invites attention that does Itauma no favors. Tyson was already must-see television before defeating Berbick in 1986 because of the way he destroyed opponents. He pressed forward, stayed in the pocket, threw combinations, and kept attacking until the fight was over. Itauma is not that type of heavyweight. He fights on the outside, waiting to launch one shot rather than remaining close and overwhelming opponents with power shots. When opponents pressure him, he tends to retreat to escape. It’s a style that looks like a bigger version of Shakur Stevenson.

That approach may be effective, but it is not guaranteed to turn him into a pay-per-view attraction. Fans watching Tyson knew they would see aggression and violence.

His personality doesn’t make up for what he lacks in the excitement department. Itauma looks half-asleep during interviews and brings low energy to the promotion. He comes across as dull rather than as a young heavyweight eager to take over the division.

Patterson also won a vacant heavyweight championship, defeating Archie Moore after Rocky Marciano retired. Itauma would not be breaking new ground by taking an available title. He would simply be doing it two months younger than Patterson.

The more revealing contrast remains Tyson. Berbick held the WBC belt when Tyson destroyed him in the ring. Itauma received his opportunity after Oleksandr Usyk relinquished the IBF title and Frank Sanchez agreed to step aside.

Winning would make Itauma an IBF champion, but the promotional campaign is using their ages to connect two fighters whose appeal and championship victories bear little resemblance.

Queensberry also waited too long to present Hrgovic as dangerous. A few interviews during fight week cannot transform him into a marquee name. Daniel Dubois would have brought greater attention from fans, punching power, and a real British rivalry.

The age statistic is being asked to create interest that the matchup, undercard, and promotion have failed to produce. Casual fans do not purchase pay-per-views to watch someone move ahead of Patterson on a list. Their money goes toward fighters and rivalries they already care about.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Takes Credit For Zepeda, Teofimo Title Wins
Sports.content:
His loss was not as one-sided as the official scores of 118-110, 118-110, and 119-109 suggested. Stevenson landed 295 of 565 punches, compared with Zepeda’s 272 of 979. Shakur was far more accurate, connecting at approximately 52% against Zepeda’s 28%, but only 23 landed punches separated them across 12 rounds.

A later victory over Lamont Roach Jr. gave Zepeda the WBC lightweight title that Stevenson previously held. It was his first full world championship, but he had already reached interim title status before meeting Shakur.

What was interesting is how Shakur handled it publicly. Before Zepeda fought Lamont Roach Jr, Shakur openly predicted Roach would dish out a beating. Once Zepeda walked away with the full WBC lightweight title, Shakur immediately flipped his tune to build up his own credentials.

By comparison, Lopez had a much stronger championship history. He defeated Vasiliy Lomachenko at lightweight and Josh Taylor at light welterweight before surrendering his WBO 140-pound belt to Stevenson in January. Saturday’s majority-decision victory over Rolando Romero made Teofimo a three-division champion.

Those latest wins add value to Shakur’s record because they confirm that Zepeda and Lopez continued operating at the championship level. Stevenson deserves credit for beating them, especially his dominant performance against Teofimo at Madison Square Garden.

However, the WBC title came to Zepeda through his victory over Roach, while Lopez moved to welterweight and took Romero’s WBA belt.

At most, Shakur can use those wins as proof that he defeated quality opposition. He cannot take partial ownership of championships that Zepeda and Teofimo won through their own performances.

Sports.title: Keith Connolly Says Teofimo Lopez May Delay Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
Allowing Teofimo to take that fight first would only weaken Catterall’s position. Lopez could earn the enormous payday, lose the title in the process, or move toward another opponent, leaving Catterall waiting without any guarantee that his opportunity would retain the same value. His better business decision is to demand the Lopez fight next and pursue the Garcia–Benn winner afterward.

Jack Catterall Blocks Teofimo Lopez’s Three-Unification Plan

Jack Catterall says Teofimo Lopez does not have the freedom to select another opponent after capturing the WBA “Super” welterweight title from Rolando Romero on Saturday night.

When Ring Magazine asked who Teofimo should fight next following his majority-decision win, Catterall responded that the WBA had already provided the answer through its 180-day directive.

“180 days @WBABoxing which means November ✅ I understand the politics of boxing better than most. Rolly had a voluntary; now it’s time for my shot! No ducks, no more swerving. Me v Teo next,” said Catterall on X.

His message also answered Teofimo’s intention to pursue three consecutive unification matches without making a mandatory defense. Such a schedule would leave no room for Catterall and require the WBA to ignore or alter its previous ruling.

Romero was elevated to Super champion before Catterall defeated Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s secondary welterweight title on May 23. The WBA ordered the Super champion to face the winner within a maximum of 180 days, placing the deadline in November.

One voluntary defense has already been granted. Romero used it against Teofimo rather than facing Catterall, and the British southpaw does not believe the new champion should receive another exception.

A fight with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn is Teofimo’s preferred next step, and he has discussed collecting the remaining welterweight belts. Those matches involve more money than a Catterall defense, which explains his preference. Still, taking Romero’s belt also meant inheriting the obligation attached to it.

This is not merely a request for consideration. Catterall holds the secondary belt and has a WBA directive supporting his demand. If the organization enforces its own ruling, three straight unification fights will have to wait.

Teofimo Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory

Teofimo Lopez believes his DAZN contract will take him directly from one welterweight unification to another without stopping for a mandatory defense of his WBA title.

The newly crowned champion is targeting Liam Paro, the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn, and eventually Devin Haney. If Lopez gets his way, every appearance during the rest of his deal will involve another champion.

During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Sports.title: Mannix: Jaron Ennis vs. Josh Kelly Talks Are Advanced
Sports.content:
“Boots is chomping at the bit to get back in the ring, and I’m told there are advanced negotiations for Jaron Ennis to face Josh Kelly in a unification fight sometime in November or December,” Mannix said during DAZN’s Sources Say. “Josh Kelly, coming off a win this past month, had some injury issues after that fight. He had a nose injury, but Matchroom, Boots’ team, believes that injury will be healed. I’m told they are targeting that fight on the East Coast before the end of this year.”

If Kelly were a stronger champion, he might be able to make several defenses and earn money from the IBF title before pursuing a unification. His July 25 showing against Caoimhin Agyarko demonstrated why waiting would carry considerable risk.

Heavy punishment left Kelly with a badly damaged nose as he squeezed out a narrow 12-round unanimous decision in Jeddah. Agyarko is ranked No. 15 by the IBF, yet Kelly struggled to keep him under control.

Higher in the IBF rankings are Brandon Adams, former champion Bakhram Murtazaliev, Nikita Tszyu, Israil Madrimov, Ben Mahoney, Xander Zayas, Milan Prat, Giovani Santillan, Yan Marcos, Pavel Sosulin, Ibrahima Diallo, and Bilal Fawaz. Kelly would have a difficult time holding the belt for long against that group.

His title-winning victory over Murtazaliev in Newcastle was also viewed by many as a hometown gift. Kelly stayed mobile rather than engage for long. Near the end of rounds, he used quick shoeshine combinations to impress the judges. Murtazaliev landed the heavier punches and dropped Kelly in the ninth, yet lost on two cards.

Ennis presents a far more severe test. The WBA and WBO champion has more speed, power, combination punching, and offensive variety. The difference is wide enough that placing the fight in Newcastle probably would not change the outcome.

That nose injury may be the greatest immediate concern. If it breaks down during sparring, the unification may have to be postponed. Assuming Kelly gets through camp, taking the Ennis fight now makes more financial sense than continuing with lower-paying title defenses.

Sports.title: Regis Prograis Calls Rocky Marciano Overrated
Sports.content:
“For me, I think Rocky Marciano was overrated,” Prograis said on social media. “He retired undefeated, right? But in this book, I bought this book about Sonny Liston. It said right here about Rocky Marciano that ‘his good fortune was to rise to prominence at a time when his major competitors were either old, like 37-year-old Joe Louis.’ He was 37 when he fought him. Joe Walcott was 37 years old. A natural light heavyweight like Ezzard Charles was 34 years old, and then Archie Moore was 41 at the time.”

The overall point has some merit, but several ages quoted by Prograis are inaccurate. Louis was 37, but Walcott was 38 when Marciano took his heavyweight title in September 1952. Charles was 32 in their first fight and turned 33 before the rematch, not 34. Moore’s birth year remains disputed, leaving him either 38 or 41 when he challenged Marciano in 1955.

Prograis also accused Marciano of avoiding 6-foot-3 Cuban contender Nino Valdes because of his size.

“They had a Cuban fighter called Nino Valdes, and he didn’t want to fight him,” Prograis said. “He said he was too big. So I know a lot of older guys say that Rocky Marciano was this and undefeated this. But I feel Rocky Marciano was overrated at the time.”

Valdes had a legitimate case after rising to the top of the heavyweight rankings, but saying Marciano simply refused to face him leaves out part of the story.

The Cuban lost a 15-round title eliminator to Moore in May 1955. Marciano then met Moore four months later and stopped him in the ninth round. Valdes also suffered numerous defeats during Marciano’s championship reign, making the claim that he was deliberately avoided difficult to prove.

Marciano’s leading opponents were older, and his era lacked the talent found in later generations. Still, Walcott, Charles, and Moore remained dangerous elite fighters. Those victories do not settle every historical argument, but dismissing his entire career as fortunate goes too far.

Sports.title: Rick Glaser Tattles on Eddie Hearn to Turki
Sports.content:
“Turki Alalshikh, you have a great event in the deep planning stage for November 20 on Netflix at the Mecca of Boxing Madison Square Garden in New York And as you know, Eddie Hearn is attempting to undermine your great event,” said Glaser on X. “Whatever Hearn’s reasons may be, personal gain, or other motives, it’s causing havoc in Boxing circles, & the sporting public, especially with Hearn saying on video’s “I don’t care who this upsets” as he mouths off. “Turki Alalshikh, you deserve much better than you are receiving from Hearn in his lack of respect. Best regards from Sonya & I.”

The sign-off completes the effect. Having reported Hearn’s alleged misconduct and lavished Turki with praise, Glaser closes the message as though he were sending a polite letter to a school principal.

Nothing in the post proves that Hearn is trying to damage the event for “personal gain” or any other hidden motive. He represents Anthony Joshua, who signed for the fight to take place at a UK stadium. Joshua prefers Wembley, while Turki and Tyson Fury favor New York.

As Joshua’s promoter, Hearn is supposed to argue his position, even when it clashes with Turki’s plans. That does not automatically make him disloyal or disrespectful.

The message presents the dispute as something more serious. In Glaser’s version, Hearn is creating chaos, sabotaging Turki’s work, and failing to show proper gratitude toward the man financing the event. It is an extraordinary display of public loyalty. Glaser did everything except ask Turki to send Hearn to the headmaster’s office.

Sports.title: Julio Cesar Chavez Broke Edwin Rosario Piece By Piece
Sports.content:
Rosario presented the kind of danger Chavez had not encountered. The WBA champion had knocked out Livingstone Bramble in two rounds the previous year and possessed genuine power in both hands. He also attacked Chavez’s opposition before the bout, dismissing many of his previous opponents as “guys right out of the bar.”

Rosario Could Not Keep Chavez Away

Any doubts about Chavez at lightweight disappeared quickly. Rather than feeling his way into the contest, the 25-year-old Mexican closed the distance and began digging hooks into Rosario’s body.

Rosario had success during the third and fourth rounds. He landed several hard punches and briefly forced Chavez onto the ropes, but nothing discouraged the advancing challenger. Chavez absorbed Rosario’s best shots, turned him, and reclaimed control with short combinations. Once the bout moved into close range, the difference became brutal. Chavez did not simply walk forward and throw punches. He slipped Rosario’s right hand, blocked shots with his elbows and gloves, then answered before the Puerto Rican champion could reset.

The body attack gradually robbed Rosario of his movement and power. Chavez mixed hooks downstairs with uppercuts and straight rights to the head, rarely wasting a punch. HBO’s PunchStat count credited him with landing 450 of 743 punches, an extraordinary 61 percent. Rosario connected with 263 of 731.

A Beating That Lasted Too Long

By the later rounds, Rosario’s left eye was swollen shut, his face was cut, and blood covered his nose and mouth. Still, he refused to go down. His courage allowed the punishment to continue far longer than it should have.

Chavez looked almost untouched as he drove Rosario into a corner during the 11th. With the champion taking another sustained attack, his corner threw in the towel. Referee Richard Steele stopped it at 2:38. All three judges had Chavez far in front: 98-92, 99-91, and 100-92.

The performance made Chavez a two-division champion and erased every question surrounding his move to lightweight. He had taken one of boxing’s most feared punchers, neutralized his power, and broken him down without ever needing a knockdown. Rosario brought danger into the ring that night, but Chavez made it disappear.

Sports.title: Teofimo Defeats Rolly, Now He Has His Eyes Set On Undisputed
Sports.content:
During the first three rounds of the world title bout, Lopez was in control as he used his jab and touched the body of Romero. Late in the fourth round, Romero landed a check left hook that knocked Lopez off balance.

In the fifth round, Rolly got more aggressive, and as a result, he landed a big left hook that produced a cut over Teofimo’s right eye.

Seconds later, Romero connected with a vicious overhand right that buckled Lopez’s knees.

Romero followed the big right hand with a flurry of shots, but Lopez was able to survive the round. Lopez bounced back in the sixth as he returned to his game plan of working off the jab and attacking the body.

Lopez continued to apply intelligent pressure in the seventh as he landed a solid right hand. As round seven was coming to a close, Romero caught Lopez with a powerful check left hook.

For the remainder of the WBA welterweight title bout, Teofimo Lopez fought a smart and very disciplined fight. Despite the low punch output, Rolly had the more eye-catching shots, but Teofimo outworked him and won by majority decision.

With the victory, Teofimo “The Takeover” Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) became a three-division world champion. As soon as Lopez was announced as the winner, the boxing community was seeking the answer to the proverbial question: What’s next?

During the post-fight press conference, Teofimo Lopez spoke about his future and the path he plans to travel in his boxing journey.

“I think I’m here, this is the road to undisputed, you know what I’m saying? I’m here to reclaim and collect all of the next world titles, and whoever the next champion is, that’s what it’s all about.”

Teofimo Lopez went on to say, “Honestly, I got four fights with, well now three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title.”

Currently, the world champions in the welterweight division are Teofimo Lopez (WBA), Devin Haney (WBO), Ryan Garcia (WBC), and Liam Paro (IBF). In his quest to become undisputed, the first step for Lopez is to become a unified world champion.

If Lopez wants what looks like the softer touch, a unification bout with IBF champion Liam Paro may be next. If Lopez wants a fight that is going to be a big event, then he may want to pursue a bout with the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner.

Ghana News.title: Ghana invites Petrobras for direct talks on oil exploration in Keta Basin
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has invited Brazilian state-owned oil company Petrobras to enter into direct talks on oil exploration in the Keta Basin, as the country intensifies efforts to attract fresh investment into its upstream petroleum sector.

The Chief Executive of the Petroleum Commission, Emeafa Hardcastle, disclosed this at the launch of the 2025 Annual Investment Report. She revealed that several major exploration and production (E&P) companies have expressed interest in securing petroleum agreements in Ghana.

“We already have a few major exploration and production companies knocking at our doors for petroleum agreements. While some of these discussions remain confidential, I can confirm today that we have extended a formal invitation to Petrobras to engage in direct negotiations with Ghana over the Keta Basin,” she said.

Ms. Hardcastle added that the Petroleum Commission would continue collaborating with relevant government agencies to enhance the regulatory environment and facilitate responsible petroleum development.

She stressed that Ghana must look beyond the immediate financial returns from petroleum investments and consider the broader economic opportunities the sector can generate.

“The value of petroleum investment should not be measured solely by the capital that enters the country. We must also consider the jobs created, technology transferred, businesses developed, infrastructure established, and industrial capabilities built,” she said.

According to her, the upstream petroleum industry has significant linkages with other sectors of the economy, including engineering, fabrication, logistics, finance, insurance, information technology, manufacturing, and professional services. These linkages, she noted, could help position the petroleum sector as a driver of Ghana’s industrialisation.

“If properly harnessed, investments in petroleum can become an important catalyst for broader industrialisation,” she said.

Ms. Hardcastle further stated that the Petroleum Commission remained committed to ensuring that local content participation is commercially sustainable and contributes meaningfully to Ghana’s economic transformation.

“We remain optimistic about the prospects for Ghana’s upstream industry,” she said.

She assured investors that the Commission would continue to work with other state institutions to improve regulatory efficiency and create an environment that supports long-term investment in Ghana’s petroleum sector.

Ghana News.title: 24-Hour Economy secures $5.5bn project commitments – Advisor
Ghana News.content:
The 24-Hour Economy programme has mobilised about $5.5 billion in project commitments, largely from the private sector rather than government capital funding, a year after its launch.

The 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme was launched in July 2025 and aims to shift the country from an import-dependent, raw material-exporting economy towards a self-reliant, round-the-clock productive economy.

Speaking at an engagement with the media in Accra last Wednesday, the Presidential Advisor on the 24-Hour Economy, Augustus Goosie Tanoh, said the programme would rely on the private sector to implement the projects while the government would facilitate the environment for the investments to thrive.

Despite its young age, he said the programme had attracted significant investment interest because of the credibility of its economic framework.

“It is a young programme, but because of the credibility of the economics around it, we are able to mobilise commitments of $5.5 billion,” he said.

Mr Tanoh explained that the programme’s responsibility was to develop viable projects and demonstrate their bankability to attract private capital.

“We have to show that Project ‘A’ and Project ‘B’ are bankable. Then you put your money in it,” he said.

The presidential advisor added that the government support was mainly limited to administrative and project-preparation costs, including hiring consultants and providing basic equipment such as computers and vehicles.

“The only support government gives us is our administrative costs. It takes government support to hire consultants, buy a computer, and buy a vehicle,” he said.

Major projects underway

Mr Tanoh disclosed that WAPCo’s solar project alone was valued at $1.45 billion, while renewable energy and renewable natural gas projects accounted for an additional $2 billion to $3 billion.

He pointed out that project developers must demonstrate sufficient equity before agreements would be signed, particularly for large-scale projects.

“If you are doing a project like WAPCo Solar, which is $1.45 billion, you want to make sure the person doing it has more than $1.45 billion as equity,” he noted.

The Buipe solar and battery project, which is part of the programme’s pipeline, is expected to generate 1,500 megawatts (MW) of electricity and create 13,000 jobs.

The 24-hour programme also targets the creation of 1.7 million jobs by the end of 2028.

Mr Tanoh explained that despite public expectations, the 24-Hour Economy is being conceived as a “systematic reconstruction” of Ghana’s productive system, with interventions spanning agriculture, manufacturing, logistics, infrastructure, and access to finance.

“We all want the economy to move to a level of capacity utilisation that allows factories to operate at 90 per cent, 100 percent, and to invest in new production lines,” he said. “But you can’t leap from 10 percent capacity utilisation to 100 percent capacity utilisation in one year.”

24-Hour markets clarified

Mr Tanoh also clarified that the 24-Hour Economy Secretariat had no jurisdiction or oversight responsibility over the 24-hour markets being developed across the country.

He said the markets were being financed by district assemblies and implemented by the Ministry of Local Government and the district assemblies.

“Although they use a 24-hour logo, we have no control over the markets.

We are not part of deciding where it goes and so on and so forth,” Mr Tanoh stated.

He disclosed that the secretariat had been sued four or five times over market projects despite having no responsibility for them.

Ghana News.title: Divorce, smartphones and control – BBC sees how Taliban run Afghanistan
Ghana News.content:
Governor Abdullah Sarhadi gives money to treat a boy's broken arm and hands out funds for a local mosque - then, in his office in northern Afghanistan, an astonishing exchange unfolds.

A young woman tells the grey-bearded former Taliban commander that she wants to divorce her husband, who she accuses of months of abuse and beatings.

She will not take no for an answer.

In a country where girls are banned from secondary education, the 18-year-old argues her case calmly and confidently, her face completely hidden behind a full-face veil and sunglasses.

"If there was any chance to live together, I wouldn't be here… I have taken my decision," she says.

After trying to persuade her to avoid divorce, the governor later comments that women are "mindless" and "deficient in intellect", to laughter from the male officials, bodyguards and elders around him.

The moment gives a rare glimpse into the day-to-day realities of the Taliban's rule, five years after they swept aside the US-backed government in 2021.

In that time, women have been excluded from most workplaces, banned from universities and may not travel alone or visit parks and leisure centres.

In encounters spread over two years, the BBC gained unusual access to influential figures in the extreme Islamist movement, spending time with men who once planned suicide attacks or spent years in underground hideouts, but are now officials and soldiers.

The Taliban came into power saying they had changed, but many of their policies are similar to the hard-line interpretation of Sharia - Islamic religious law - they imposed in the 1990s.

The men we met seemed to want to present themselves as reasonable, yet were not keen to discuss their past violence. And we saw moments of unease between the rulers and those they rule.

Governor Sarhadi says Tuba – not her real name – should stay in the marriage.

"Ask yourself: 'Who would marry me after I get my divorce?'" says Sarhadi. "You'll have to compromise a lot or you'll lose your dignity and honour."

"Mr Governor, my honour and dignity have already been ruined," she responds.

Her husband listens, awaiting his turn to speak.

Under Sharia, a woman requesting that her husband agrees to a divorce may have to return some or all of the money given to her by him when they married. A financial settlement is often agreed. But this woman's husband says he wants four times the amount, which her family refuses to pay.

The governor says the woman should be given her own room. He adds that officials will warn him not to beat her - "otherwise he'd be jailed".

Unsatisfied, Tuba's father later tells the BBC the family will pursue divorce through the courts, even though, under the Taliban's court system, it is very difficult for a woman to get a divorce without the husband's consent.

Sarhadi was a military commander during the Taliban's first stint in power in the 1990s. He was among thousands of insurgents who surrendered in late 2001 as a US-led coalition ousted the group.

He was held for several years in US detention in Guantanamo Bay, but eventually released.

When the Taliban regained power, he became a governor - first in the province of Bamiyan, then when we met him in late June, in Sheberghan city in Jawzjan province. He has recently become deputy commander of a military corps in the northern province of Kunduz.

Tapping on an old-style mobile with a tiny screen, he says a recent ban on smartphones for officials has slowed things down. "Before, you could send a quick message… sending documents and getting an answer fast." If he says any more about the ban, "it will cause trouble", he adds.

But in other ways his worldview seems largely unchanged from the Taliban's position 25 years ago. Then, he was a military commander in Bamiyan, where the Taliban blew up ancient giant Buddha statues, triggering international shock and condemnation.

He initially tries to avoid our questions about the archaeological site, but eventually, he says: "I destroyed it with my own hands.

"Whatever we did and we do is in accordance with the guidance and God's law… We smash idols rather than sell them. Why should I regret? It was God's will."

In the capital Kabul, we meet another senior Taliban figure who swapped a violent past for a role with the ruling administration.

Habibullah Badr drives us through the streets in an armoured car.

He says he was previously "responsible for the operations of suicide attackers" in Kabul.

"I know all the roads and streets very well… we had all the information we needed about Kabul and its alleys," he says. "There were areas that needed a long time to plan."

Taliban suicide attacks killed thousands of people in Afghanistan, including many civilians.

Badr is cautious about discussing his past though, fearing it will "make people upset" and could "reopen wounds".

Asked about civilian deaths, he says the Taliban targeted US convoys and that civilians were urged to stay away from foreign bases.

Whenever I try to ask him about specific attacks that took place in civilian areas, he evades the question.

He is currently taking time out from official roles for medical treatment, but was previously deputy head of prisons for the whole country – and ran the very jail where he was held on death row under the previous government.

Badr invites us to join him at a tribal gathering, where the head of a charitable foundation is to honour him with a medal. But things take an unexpected turn.

"Mr Badr is a pride for Afghanistan and a great fighter," says Sultan Mohammad Talaee. "But I also have a complaint. If the schools and education were open to all it would be a great work for Afghanistan. I hope this doesn't offend you."

An awkward silence follows, his audience unsure how to react. Talaee's microphone is swiftly removed.

Afterwards, he tells the BBC: "I requested for the girls' schools to reopen… seeking knowledge is an obligation for both men and women in Islam."

He adds: "There were other things I wanted to say but they didn't let me talk more."

Often those who speak out face much more severe consequences.

Women told us of the deep despair they felt over dreams thwarted by restrictions on education, and of friends jailed for protesting.

Most journalists we spoke to said they had been summoned or questioned by the Taliban's intelligence organisation, Estikhbaraat.

The BBC put some of these concerns to the Taliban government's spokesman, known as Zabihullah Mujahid.

He has been a public face for the Taliban government since 2021. He still uses the pseudonym he went by for years during the insurgency, but he told us his real name is Tahir Shah Seddiqi - revealing it publicly for the first time.

In a lavish press centre funded by the Americans for the previous government, we ask him about the first press conference he gave there, two days after the Taliban took control of the country.

Then, he told the world the Taliban government would allow women to work and study "within our frameworks" and they would "be very active" in society. Why did they fail to keep their word?

"We are committed to women's rights, freedom of speech and other things within Sharia," he replies. "We should see everything through the Sharia lens."

Allowing women to work in offices such as his own "would lead to immoralities" and "their dignity would be undermined", he adds.

He says the issue of education for women is "under discussions… we need a Sharia-based solution for it".

When questioned about the Taliban's crackdown on media freedom, he says: "In a society like Afghanistan we have our restrictions. We can't let media do whatever propaganda they want… they can't broadcast against Islamic laws and rites."

The Taliban government sits in Kabul, but Mujahid spends a lot of time in the southern city of Kandahar, the Taliban's heartland, which some now consider the de facto capital.

We ask to meet the Taliban's supreme leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada, who is based there. He rarely appears in public and has never given a media interview - we are told it will not be possible at the moment.

Restrictions have been tightened in Kandahar since I last visited two years ago. Now men must have beards. Radio stations are not allowed to play music or broadcast women's voices, and we were not allowed to film in the city.

Two hours' drive away, along dusty roads, some of the group's most devoted former fighters showed the BBC the insurgents' old secret cave network.

Abid Lalai, a former fighter who now mans a checkpoint as part of a security force under the interior ministry, shows us the holes he fired from and the places he used to put his Quran and hang AK-47s.

His superior, Abdul Samad, shows us an unmarked graveyard, saying his father is buried here, killed fighting for the Taliban.

The area is one of the most deprived in a country where the UN says three in four people cannot provide for their basic needs. Samad says the local population desperately need water, roads and clinics.

"Emirate [Taliban] officials have not forgotten us," says Samad. He says the leaders may be busy with other priorities. "We are hopeful, they will look after us sometime."

Five years since the Taliban began their second stint in power, poverty, unemployment and economic instability remain pressing concerns.

Taliban figures we spoke to said they were working to tackle them, but we met other people who believe the group itself is the country's main problem.

"I'm speechless about how a group that has no understanding about life is suddenly in power," says Hoda - not her real name - a woman who protested on the streets when the Taliban first returned to power.

"Women can't accept this situation," she tells the BBC. "They might advance restrictions but it won't stay like this forever."

"I think the Taliban are scared of educated women," she adds. "That's why they restrict women. They want uneducated women so they can't raise wise men. Because that would end the Taliban."

Ghana News.title: UCC launches Africa Ocean Institute to strengthen coastal resilience
Ghana News.content:
The University of Cape Coast (UCC) has officially launched the Africa Ocean Institute (AOI), a multidisciplinary platform aimed at advancing ocean knowledge, developing innovative solutions, and promoting the sustainable management of Africa’s coastal and marine resources.

The launch, held at the Academic Board Chamber on the UCC campus, was presided over by the vice-chancellor, Professor Denis Worlanyo Aheto.

The Registrar of the School, Gideon Abbeyquaye, Esq., said African coastal and marine ecosystems were facing several interconnected challenges.

“African coastal and marine ecosystems are confronted by the combined challenges of climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution alongside illegal fishing, maritime insecurity, and the unsustainable exploitation of marine resources.”

The launch marks the culmination of decades of work and vision in coastal management at UCC, dating back to the 1990s.

In 1996, the university was identified as a forerunner of institutional advancement in integrated coastal management. This led to the establishment of a dedicated team to build awareness and capacity around coastal areas.

Although the initial effort was later interrupted, the idea continued to develop and has now culminated in the establishment of the Africa Ocean Institute.

Bringing together expertise

Professor Denis Worlanyo Aheto said the idea for the institute had its roots in discussions held years ago.

“The idea of this AOI, the discussion actually started in the corridors of Dakar…”he said.

The AOI has been established as a multidisciplinary, science-based institutional platform that brings together the complementary expertise UCC has developed over the years.

The institute has been designated as a graduate training hub and will operate alongside other prominent institutes within the university, including the Institute of Education Planning and Administration and the Institute for Development Studies.

The strength of the AOI lies in bringing together three distinct but interconnected university entities.

They are the Centre for Coastal Management, a World Bank Africa Centre of Excellence in Coastal Resilience; the Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture Science, which serves as an African Union Centre of Excellence for Training in Marine Fisheries and Coastal Zone Management; and the newly established Centre for Marine Affairs.

The Centre for Coastal Management provides specialised knowledge in climate change, biological and coastal development and related areas.

The Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture Science provides the academic foundation through its expertise in fisheries, aquatic sciences, aquaculture and related fields.

The Centre for Marine Affairs contributes expertise in policy, governance, law and outreach, with a focus on the blue economy, ocean law, ocean governance and the relationship between marine resources, society and development.

Together, the three entities are expected to provide a holistic approach to ocean studies.

Focus on Africa’s blue economy

The establishment of the institute is driven by the need to harness the opportunities presented by Africa’s oceans while addressing the challenges facing coastal and marine resources.

Its mission is to “advance ocean knowledge, inspire solutions, and transform Africa’s Blue Future.”

The blue economy represents a significant economic opportunity for the continent, with activities estimated to generate between US$296 billion and US$300 billion annually and support approximately 50 million jobs.

Fisheries alone contribute an estimated 10 million tonnes of catch annually. If the catch were processed locally, it could potentially increase Africa’s gross domestic product by US$50 billion each year.

The potential of the blue economy is particularly important given Africa’s geography. Of the continent’s 54 countries, 32 are coastal states, with many national capitals strategically located along the coast.

The blue economy has consequently become an increasingly prominent part of Africa’s development agenda.

Research and training

The AOI is expected to provide an international platform for innovative, demand-driven and interdisciplinary research.

It will also focus on training scientists, professionals, and practitioners to address the continent’s coastal and marine challenges.

Ultimately, the institute is dedicated to promoting the sustainable management of physical coastal and marine resources.

Through this approach, the Africa Ocean Institute seeks to help Africa harness the wealth of its oceans while preserving those resources for generations to come.

Ghana News.title: Work begins to reclaim Lafa basin to reduce flooding in Mallam, Weija and surrounding areas
Ghana News.content:
Work has begun to reclaim the Lafa water retention basin at Mallam as part of the government’s efforts to reduce the risk of flooding in Mallam, Weija, Dansoman and surrounding communities.

The operation, being led by the 48 Engineer Regiment of the Ghana Armed Forces, is aimed at restoring the basin’s capacity after years of accumulated solid waste, siltation and illegal encroachment.

The exercise involves dredging the basin, removing accumulated waste for disposal at a designated landfill site, demolishing illegal structures within the water reserve and constructing protective embankments to strengthen flood control measures.

The operation is being coordinated by the Post-Flood Mitigation Task Force as part of a broader national effort to restore waterways and drainage channels across Accra following the devastating floods of June 29.

The government has provided the resources and equipment required for the exercise, with similar flood mitigation works also underway at Oyarifa, East Legon and around the Kpeshie Lagoon.

Authorities are urging residents and other members of the public to cooperate with the taskforce and refrain from activities that obstruct waterways or undermine efforts to manage flood risks.

The reclamation of the Lafa basin is expected to improve its capacity to retain excess stormwater and help reduce the impact of flooding on communities downstream.

Ghana News.title: No minimum salary required for Republic Bank mortgage – Head of Mortgage Banking
Ghana News.content:
The Head of Mortgage Banking at Republic Bank, Dan Adjetey Morhenu, has assured prospective homeowners that the bank does not have a minimum salary requirement for customers seeking mortgage financing.

According to him, Republic Bank’s mortgage solutions are designed to accommodate customers across different income levels, with the financing arrangement depending largely on an applicant’s income and the type of property they intend to acquire.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, August 24, Mr Morhenu said the bank could support customers at different stages of their homeownership journey, including those who may need to acquire land before gradually developing their properties.

His comments followed the conclusion of the 2026 JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair at the Achimota Retail Centre, where prospective homeowners engaged financial institutions, property developers and other players in the housing sector.

The three-day mini-fair, held from Friday, August 21 to Sunday, August 23, provided patrons with an opportunity to seek information on mortgages, property acquisition, construction financing and other housing solutions.

‘We don’t have a minimum salary’

Mr Morhenu said one of the most frequently asked questions at the fair was the minimum salary required to qualify for a mortgage.

He explained that Republic Bank does not impose a fixed salary threshold, stressing that people with different income levels could explore mortgage options.

“One of the key questions that came up was what is the minimum salary to qualify for a mortgage, and we kept hammering that we don’t have a minimum salary. No matter the amount you earn as income, there is a mortgage for you,” he said.

He explained, however, that an applicant’s income would determine the type of mortgage arrangement and homeownership path that would be most suitable.

Customers with lower incomes, he said, could begin by acquiring land and gradually progress to construction, while those with higher incomes could potentially purchase completed properties.

“Based on the quantum of income, some people may have to start from the land and we walk them through the building. Some also, because they earn so much, are able to acquire properties immediately,” he explained.

Mr Morhenu said Republic Bank’s approach was not simply to provide loans but to structure mortgage solutions around customers’ individual financial circumstances.

He also highlighted the bank’s fixed mortgage rates, saying they provide borrowers with greater certainty and help them manage their finances throughout the repayment period.

“At Republic Bank, our rates are fixed. We fix it because we want you to manage your cash flow, so it is not just about purchasing a house; we are also managing your cash flow for you,” he said.

‘There was a long queue before we set up’

Mr Morhenu also described the turnout at the Habitat Fair as unexpectedly high, saying a queue had already formed at the Achimota Retail Centre before exhibitors had completed setting up on the opening day.

“It was exciting. I was quite surprised that even before we set up on Friday, there was a long queue at the mall waiting to have a conversation with not just Republic Bank, but the other exhibitors,” he said.

He said the strong interest continued throughout the three-day event, with Republic Bank’s booth remaining busy until late on Friday.

According to him, the bank’s mortgage team stayed until about 8:30pm on the opening day to attend to the last customer.

The interest continued on Saturday, when more members of the public visited the fair and sought information on mortgage financing.

“We had our fellow bankers who came around to ask questions, we had government workers, expatriates who came around and we had to take our time because mortgages are not just a one-time decision that you take,” he said.

Mr Morhenu stressed that purchasing a home was a major financial commitment and required careful discussions between prospective borrowers and mortgage specialists.

He said the bank was prepared to spend sufficient time with customers to understand their financial circumstances and guide them towards suitable mortgage options.

Republic Bank offers refinancing for dollar mortgages

The Republic Bank executive also addressed challenges faced by some borrowers who had taken US dollar-denominated mortgages from other financial institutions.

He disclosed that the bank undertook several refinancing arrangements in 2022 for customers who were servicing dollar loans but were struggling with the financial burden.

“In 2022, we had to refinance a lot of these loans. They had US dollar loans with other banks. They approached us to refinance them in cedis, so most of them are okay now,” he said.

He urged customers who may still be struggling with foreign currency-denominated mortgage obligations not to abandon their properties but to approach Republic Bank to explore possible refinancing options.

“If there are some of them who are still struggling, don’t walk away from your property. They should come and speak to us so that we can refinance them into cedis,” Mr Morhenu said.

He assured such customers that the bank could consider flexible repayment arrangements depending on their circumstances.

‘We were really overwhelmed with the numbers’

Also speaking about the Habitat Fair, Mortgage Specialist at Republic Bank (Ghana) PLC, Elizabeth Abena Anokware Amedeka, expressed appreciation to members of the public for their strong participation.

She said the turnout reflected growing interest among Ghanaians in understanding how mortgages work and the steps involved in securing a home.

“We want to thank the public for the massive turnout. It was great; people asked the right questions about mortgages and how to start. We were really overwhelmed with the numbers,” she said.

Ms Amedeka encouraged members of the public to participate in future editions of the fair, assuring them that Republic Bank was ready to guide prospective homeowners throughout the homeownership process.

She said the bank’s support went beyond providing financing, with mortgage specialists available to guide customers from the initial stages through to acquiring their homes.

“Republic Bank is ready to walk you through this journey and we are ready to assist you from the beginning of the process to you picking up your keys,” she said.

Ghana News.title: ‘It was exciting’ – Republic Bank executive recounts huge turnout at Habitat Fair
Ghana News.content:
Head of Mortgage Banking at Republic Bank, Dan Adjetey Morhenu, has described the strong public turnout at the 2026 JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair as “exciting”, saying interest in the event was evident even before exhibitors had opened their stands.

According to him, a long queue had already formed at the Achimota Retail Centre on Friday, August 21, with patrons eager to engage Republic Bank and other exhibitors on homeownership, mortgage financing and housing solutions.

“It was exciting. I was quite surprised that even before we set up on Friday, there was a long queue at the mall waiting to have a conversation with not just Republic Bank, but the other exhibitors,” Mr Morhenu said.

He was speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, August 24, while reflecting on the three-day Habitat Fair, which ended at the Achimota Retail Centre on Sunday, August 23.

The event brought together prospective homeowners and players in Ghana’s housing and construction sector, giving patrons the opportunity to explore options for building, buying, financing or improving their homes.

Mr Morhenu said the level of interest was so high that Republic Bank’s mortgage team had to extend its operations beyond the scheduled closing time on the opening day.

“On Friday, we didn’t close early. We had to wait for the last person to leave our booth before we closed. That was around 8:30pm,” he said.

‘Mortgages are not just a one-time decision’

The strong turnout continued into Saturday, with more patrons visiting the fair to engage exhibitors and seek information on mortgage financing.

Mr Morhenu said the bank interacted with people from diverse backgrounds, including fellow bankers, government workers and expatriates.

“Then it followed through on Saturday. As for Saturday, people are home and so a lot of people came around. We had our fellow bankers who came around to ask, we had government workers, expatriates who came around and we had to take our time,” he said.

He said the bank could not rush its engagements with prospective customers because taking a mortgage was a significant long-term financial commitment.

“Mortgages are not just a one-time decision that you take, so we had to take our time for everybody and then we closed off on Sunday,” he added.

One of the most frequently asked questions during the fair, he said, was the minimum salary required to qualify for a mortgage.

Mr Morhenu explained that Republic Bank does not have a fixed minimum salary threshold, allowing people with different income levels to explore mortgage options.

“One of the key questions that came up was what is the minimum salary to qualify for a mortgage, and we kept hammering that we don’t have a minimum salary. No matter the amount you earn as income, there is a mortgage for you,” he said.

He explained, however, that a customer’s income would determine the type of mortgage arrangement and homeownership option that would be most suitable.

Customers with lower incomes, he said, could begin their homeownership journey by acquiring land and gradually progressing to construction, while those with higher incomes could potentially purchase completed properties.

“It’s just that based on the quantum of income, some people may have to start from the land and we walk them through the building. Some also, because they earn so much, are able to acquire properties immediately,” he explained.

Republic Bank highlights fixed mortgage rates

Mr Morhenu also highlighted Republic Bank’s fixed mortgage rates, saying the arrangement gives customers greater certainty in managing their finances throughout the repayment period.

He said the bank’s mortgage offering went beyond simply financing the purchase of a property to helping customers manage their cash flow.

“At Republic Bank, our rates are fixed. We fix it because we want you to manage your cash flow. So it is not just about purchasing a house; we are also managing your cash flow for you,” he said.

According to him, the approach enables prospective homeowners to better understand their financial obligations and plan their finances around their mortgage repayments.

Mr Morhenu also spoke about challenges faced by some customers who had taken US dollar-denominated mortgage loans from other banks.

He disclosed that Republic Bank, in 2022, assisted some of these customers by refinancing their dollar-denominated loans into cedi facilities.

“In 2022, we had to refinance a lot of these loans. They had US dollar loans with other banks. They approached us to refinance them in cedis, so most of them are okay now,” he said.

He urged customers who were still struggling with such loans not to abandon their properties but to approach Republic Bank to explore possible refinancing arrangements.

“If there are some of them who are still struggling, don’t walk away from your property. They should come and speak to us so that we can refinance them into cedis,” Mr Morhenu said.

He added that the bank would be willing to consider flexible terms for eligible customers to help them manage their mortgage obligations.

‘We were really overwhelmed with numbers’

Mortgage Specialist at Republic Bank (Ghana) PLC, Elizabeth Abena Anokware Amedeka, also expressed gratitude to the public for the strong turnout at the Habitat Fair.

She said the event provided an important opportunity for prospective homeowners to ask practical questions and gain a better understanding of how to begin their homeownership journey.

“We want to thank the public for the massive turnout. It was great. People asked the right questions about mortgage and how to start. We were really overwhelmed with numbers,” she said.

Ms Amedeka encouraged members of the public to participate in subsequent editions of the fair, assuring them that Republic Bank was prepared to support customers throughout the mortgage process.

“We want to say don’t miss the next session because Republic Bank is ready to walk you through this journey and we are ready to assist you from the beginning of the process to you picking up your keys,” she said.

She stressed that the bank’s role went beyond providing loans, saying it was committed to guiding customers through the various stages of securing a home.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod losses remain key on Minority agenda as Parliament reconvenes – Afenyo-Markin
Ghana News.content:
Alexander Afenyo-Markin

Minority Leader in Parliament, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, has reaffirmed the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Caucus’ commitment to investigating the reported loss of more than US$1.7 billion linked to the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme and the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod).

Mr Afenyo-Markin made the statement after meeting NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia at his private residence in Accra on Monday morning.

According to the Minority Leader, the meeting focused on party matters and key issues confronting the Minority ahead of Parliament’s emergency sitting.

He said Dr Bawumia commended the Minority Caucus for its work and encouraged members to continue holding the government accountable.

“He commended the Minority for its efforts so far.”

Mr Afenyo-Markin said the reported loss, which he described as equivalent to about 1.5% of Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), would remain a key issue for the Minority as Parliament reconvenes.

“I further informed him that this colossal loss, under the watch of GoldBod and the Bank of Ghana, is firmly on the Minority’s agenda as Parliament reconvenes today.”

He said the Minority would pursue the matter in the interest of the Ghanaian public and seek answers over the circumstances surrounding the reported loss.

“We remain resolute in this commitment, and we will not relent until the Ghanaian people receive the answers they deserve.”

The Minority has been pushing for parliamentary scrutiny of the reported losses associated with the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, with the NPP Caucus expected to pursue its motion for an inquiry when the House resumes.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
