World.title: Iraq foreign reserves decline 11.6% to $86.17B in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official financial statements from the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) show that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves declined to $86.175 billion at the end of June 2026, marking a decrease of $11.257 billion (-11.6%) compared to the $97.432 billion recorded at the close of 2025.

According to reserve records published on Monday, August 24, 2026, the contraction followed an early-year peak above $102 billion before downward momentum set in through the second quarter.

Monthly Reserve Trajectory (H1 2026)

End of 2025 Baseline: $97.432 billion

January 2026: $101.082 billion

February 2026 (Peak): $102.131 billion

March 2026: $100.341 billion

April 2026: $97.809 billion

May 2026: $93.673 billion

June 2026:$86.175 billion(Month-over-month drop of $7.498 billion)

The overall drop reduced the local currency value of the total portfolio from 126.661 trillion IQD at the end of 2025 to 112.027 trillion IQD by June 30, 2026—a net decline of 14.634 trillion IQD (-11.6%).

Reserve Component End of 2025 (IQD) End of June 2026 (IQD) Net Change Change (%) Investments & Securities 93.266 Trillion 81.998 Trillion -11.268 Trillion -12.1% Monetary Gold Reserves 31.488 Trillion 29.415 Trillion -2.073 Trillion -6.6% Cash Vault Holdings 1.907 Trillion 0.614 Trillion -1.293 Trillion -67.8% Total Equivalent Value 126.661 Trillion 112.027 Trillion -14.634 Trillion -11.6%

The reserve reduction aligns with broader fiscal pressures in the first half of 2026, during which lower oil revenues widened the state budget deficit and prompted the central bank to meet elevated domestic foreign currency demand.

While liquid investment instruments fell by 11.268 trillion IQD to absorb trade financing and foreign wire settlements, cash assets held in central bank vaults rebounded moderately in June (up to 614 billion IQD from 366 billion IQD in May), even as overall foreign exchange reserves adjusted downward to $86.175 billion.

World.title: National Security Adviser Al Aboudi meets U.S. Envoy on arms control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi met on Monday, August 24, 2026, with the Chargé d’Affaires of the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Joshua Harris, to discuss bilateral security cooperation, regional de-escalation, and Baghdad’s ongoing measures to restrict weapons exclusively to state control.

According to an official statement issued by the National Security Advisory, Al-Aboudi reaffirmed that the Iraqi government remains committed to maintaining national stability, mitigating broader regional tensions, and regulating the state monopoly over arms.

Key Discussion Pillars & Security Priorities

State Monopoly Over Arms: Al-Aboudi emphasized the government’s systematic implementation of regulatory frameworks designed to consolidate all weapons under official state security command.

Institutional Governance & Sovereign Decision-Making: Underlined Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s administrative vision focused on strengthening national defense and security institutions to support independent sovereign policymaking and economic recovery.

Counter-Terrorism & Intelligence Sharing: Reviewed shared security mechanisms between Baghdad and Washington, focusing on counter-terror operations, joint training, and strategic intelligence exchange.

Regional De-escalation: Discussed ongoing diplomatic and security initiatives to defuse regional friction and reinforce stability across the Middle East.

U.S. Diplomatic Backing: Harris affirmed Washington’s support for the Iraqi government’s security roadmap, institutional sovereignty, and regional stabilization initiatives.

The meeting between Al-Aboudi and Harris underscores consistent coordination between Baghdad and Washington on key security priorities, coming shortly after high-level diplomatic discussions on the U.S.–Iraq Strategic Framework Agreement.

By synchronizing counter-terrorism efforts with domestic initiatives to restrict unregulated weapons, Iraqi authorities aim to reinforce sovereign command structures, improve internal stability, and foster a secure environment for long-term economic investment.

World.title: Samarra Drug Company starts first domestic Moxifloxacin Antibiotic output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra (SDI), an affiliate of the Iraqi Ministry of Industry and Minerals, announced on Monday, August 24, 2026, the successful domestic production of Moxifloxacin, a broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic targeting five distinct bacterial infections, marking its first addition to the company’s manufacturing portfolio.

In an official statement received by IraqiNews.com, SDI Director General, Chemist Mohammed Abdul Qader Al-Nuaimi, confirmed that the formulation marks a key step in expanding state pharmaceutical production lines and bolstering domestic medical security.

Clinical Scope & Key Indications

Moxifloxacin is a fourth-generation synthetic fluoroquinolone antibiotic designed to treat severe and complex bacterial infections in adult patients, including:

Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Lower respiratory tract bacterial infections.

Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Bacterial flair-ups affecting chronic obstructive airway passages.

Acute Bacterial Sinusitis: Severe sinus and nasal inflammation.

Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: Complicated and uncomplicated bacterial dermatological and subcutaneous infections.

Other Complex Bacterial Invasions: Broad-spectrum systemic coverage against susceptible Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens.

Strategic Importance for National Drug Security

Import Substitution: Domestic manufacturing directly reduces the Ministry of Health’s reliance on foreign imported antibiotics, conserving foreign exchange reserves.

National Pharmaceutical Localization: Aligns with Iraq’s industrial localization roadmap aimed at strengthening the domestic supply chain for critical medications.

Supply Chain Reliability: Ensures stable, high-quality, and cost-effective medical supplies for state healthcare facilities and the local private retail market.

The launch of Moxifloxacin comes as part of the Samarra facility’s broader modernization drive to introduce advanced active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and expand local formulation capacities.

By localizing the manufacture of advanced broad-spectrum antibiotics, SDI continues to scale production lines to meet the clinical procurement requirements of Iraqi hospitals and healthcare centers.

World.title: Iraq to launch portal for 1M residential plots project in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi government will officially launch the dedicated digital registration platform for its flagship “One Million Residential Plots” initiative on September 1, 2026, targeting citizens who have never previously benefited from state land allocations, government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi announced on Monday, August 24, 2026.

Al-Aboudi confirmed that the first batch of serviced land parcels—exceeding 250,000 plots developed in coordination with the private sector—is fully prepared across various governorates. The government is also evaluating structured bank lending programs to assist eligible citizens with residential construction financing.

Key Program Milestones & Eligibility Framework

Digital Application Launch: The official online registration platform will open on September 1, 2026, featuring integrated identity verification and automated auditing to cross-check eligibility.

Strict Eligibility Criteria: The initiative is restricted exclusively to Iraqi citizens who have not received prior land grants, housing allocations, or state residential real estate.

First Batch Scale: More than 250,000 fully serviced residential plots (equipped with water, electricity, sewage, and road networks) have been prepared nationwide under public-private development partnerships.

Construction Loan Mechanisms: The federal government, in coordination with state and private commercial banks, is assessing low-interest housing loan packages to support plot recipients in constructing single-family housing units.

The digital launch follows executive directives issued on August 9, 2026, by Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi, instructing ministries and provincial municipal directorates to initiate executive procedures in governorates where land zoning and site demarcation have been completed.

Municipalities have accelerated land surveying and partitioning over recent weeks. On August 18, the Karbala Municipality Directorate finalized all technical sorting and zoning requirements for its local allocation quota, preparing parcels for distribution as part of the broader national strategy to alleviate urban housing shortages and curb informal settlements.

World.title: Iraq tests return of Basrah crude sales through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is resuming efforts to transfer more oil straight from its southern export ports, with state marketer SOMO seeking customers for September shipments as restricted tanker access via the Strait of Hormuz reopens.

The offering includes Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy, with purchasers likely to pick up the petroleum from Iraq’s Gulf export facilities rather than using alternate transfer arrangements devised during the recent shipping interruption.

The decision follows a significant breakthrough over the weekend, when Iran granted transit through Hormuz for several tankers carrying Iraqi oil in response to persistent diplomatic pleas from Baghdad.

For Iraq, even a partial reopening is crucial.

The majority of the country’s petroleum typically departs via its southern Gulf ports, rendering the economy especially susceptible when tanker traffic through Hormuz is halted.

Baghdad has spent recent weeks looking for methods to keep exports and government revenues coming. International merchants have utilized smaller boats and ship-to-ship swaps to transport some Iraqi barrels beyond the Gulf, while the government has stepped up attempts to enhance export capacity via Turkey and explore future routes via Syria and Jordan.

SOMO’s recent offering may give an early indicator of whether oil merchants are willing to return to loading straight from Basrah, despite ongoing security and transportation hazards.

QatarEnergy is also testing the market with oil available for collection within Hormuz, indicating that regional producers are progressively investigating whether traditional Gulf shipments may restart.

However, tanker movements remain far lower than usual, indicating that Iraq cannot count on Hormuz recovering to its pre-conflict role.

This uncertainty has fueled Baghdad’s desire to diversify its oil infrastructure. Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration seeks to increase exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan port and create new routes to the Mediterranean and Red Sea.

For now, the top objective is to send as many Iraqi barrels to foreign consumers as securely as possible while also restoring the oil revenue on which the government budget is largely dependent.

The SOMO tender is therefore more than just a crude sale. It is an early test of whether Iraq’s key southern oil-export infrastructure can resume regular operations after the Hormuz crisis, which revealed one of the country’s most serious economic weaknesses.

World.title: Oman’s SalamAir adds Erbil as second destination in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — SalamAir, Oman’s low-cost airline, will commence direct flights between Muscat and Erbil on October 25, 2026, strengthening its footprint in Iraq after its debut into the Baghdad market.

The airline has launched ticket sales for the new flight, which will run twice a week between the Omani capital and Erbil.

One-way Lite fares will start at approximately $143 (187,000 Iraqi dinars).

SalamAir adds Erbil as its second Iraqi destination, capitalizing on the success of its current Muscat-Baghdad route.

The new link is designed to facilitate business, tourist, commerce, and family travel between Oman and Iraq, as well as provide travelers from Erbil with additional connections via Muscat to destinations in India and other regions of Asia.

SalamAir Chief Commercial Officer Steven Allen characterized Iraq as an important market for the airline, with Erbil providing an additional potential to meet expanding regional demand and improve Muscat’s position as a connecting hub.

The extension also offers another international link to Erbil International Airport, and it comes as Iraq welcomes more regional airline services as business and tourism flourish.

World.title: Ukraine backers gather as war escalates, air defence runs low
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukraine hosts a meeting of its key European backers on Monday to press for critical air-defence supplies and more pressure on Moscow, with Russian attacks killing more civilians than at any time since the first months of the invasion.

The meeting of the Coalition of the Willing will be jointly chaired by the leaders of Britain, France and Germany.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be in Kyiv for his first international trip since taking office, and several other leaders are expected to join remotely.

EU Council President Antonio Costa is also due in Kyiv for the talks, which come amid the latest, deadly escalation of the war.

Russia has been pounding Kyiv with ballistic missiles in recent weeks, ripping open apartment blocks and killing dozens of citizens in the capital.

The escalating Russian strikes have pushed civilian deaths to their highest levels since the first months of Russia’s 2022 invasion.

After almost every attack — which sees tens of thousands hunker in the Kyiv metro system and many more in basements and other shelters across the city — Zelensky has issued public pleas for more air-defence support.

Ahead of the meeting, Ukraine has forged ahead with its campaign against Russia’s logistics sites, hitting multiple warehouses belonging to e-commerce giant Ozon.

Ozon reported fires early Monday at its warehouses in Krasnodar and Makhachkala, both in southern Russia, adding that sites in Adygeysk and Nevinnomyssk were evacuated due to threats of drone attack.

Russian authorities also said debris from a Ukrainian drone attack killed two children and wounded nine others.

– UK, French support –

Ukraine celebrates independence day on Monday, which also marks exactly four-and-a-half years since Russia invaded on February 24, 2022.

“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve,” Burnham said in a statement before his arrival in Kyiv.

“We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”

Diplomacy on ending the conflict — Europe’s largest since World War II — is effectively frozen.

Russia is demanding hardline territorial and political concessions that Kyiv has rejected as a capitulation that would only enable another Russian attack.

Burnham is set to announce that the British government is authorising defence firm MBDA to release classified information needed to help Ukraine and France set up local production of the long-range SCALP missile.

And on Saturday, French President Emmanuel Macron pledged Paris would deliver new interceptor missiles.

“It is crucial to provide Ukraine with all the necessary means to defend its skies and thwart this aggression,” Macron wrote on X.

The ballistic missiles Russia has been firing in their dozens are incredibly fast and travel with a high-arching trajectory, making them difficult to stop.

Kyiv’s homegrown weapons cannot shoot them down, meaning Ukraine is reliant on advanced systems — chiefly, US Patriot interceptors — to protect its skies.

But due to shortfalls globally since the US launched its war on Iran, Ukraine has been left exposed.

– Ukraine’s missiles shortfall –

Ahead of the meeting, Zelensky revealed the extent of the deficit, releasing usually closely guarded numbers.

He said deliveries of crucial Patriot interceptors had halved since 2023.

“Over the entire of 2023, Ukraine received 675 missiles, and over all of 2025 — 364, even though Russian missile strikes have increased,” Zelensky said.

“For 2026, as currently projected, it is 264,” he added, saying Ukraine was seeking a package of at least 300 for the upcoming winter.

The United States faces its own shortfall of the missiles during its war on Iran and has resisted releasing large numbers to Ukraine.

Zelensky said Russia could produce around 100 ballistic missiles a month.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has accelerated its own campaign of long-range strikes on Russian energy and logistics sites — including oil refineries and retail warehouses.

The Coalition of the Willing is a Franco-British initiative to deliver support to Ukraine and ramp up pressure on Russia.

Originally designed as a group of countries that would be willing to deploy peacekeeping troops to Ukraine in the event a ceasefire was reached, it has become a parallel forum for marshalling support to Ukraine as uncertainty persists over US commitments under Donald Trump.

World.title: New Zealand moves to ban social media for under-16s
World.content:
Wellington – New Zealand’s government will introduce legislation on Monday banning under 16s from using social media, joining a number of countries seeking to keep youngsters off sites such as Instagram and TikTok.

New Zealand has been investigating a social media ban for over a year, after neighbouring Australia implemented its world-first legislation in December.

Under the Online Safety Bill, firms like Meta could be fined up to 10 percent of their global revenue if they fail to comply.

“We simply cannot accept the harm being done to a generation of New Zealand children,” Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said.

In announcing the Online Safety Bill, Luxon said “one in three children aged between 13 and 17 are now spending at least five hours on social media a day”.

“Social media is exposing them to harmful content, addictive technology and pressures they are not equipped to deal with, and it’s affecting their family life, mental health, sleep, and education,” he said.

Luxon specifically called out platforms Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and Facebook, saying they would be required to take “reasonable steps to check users are over the age of 16”.

They would have to use “existing account information, facial age estimation, digital ID services and formal ID” to verify age.

Platforms would also be required to assess the risks they pose as well as report on how those dangers are being reduced, and penalties would be introduced for companies that fail to comply.

Education Minister Erica Stanford said the Bill “places legal obligations on platforms”.

“No penalties are proposed for children, their parents or caregivers,” Stanford said.

It’s unclear whether the bill will pass, as both National Party’s coalition partners — the libertarian ACT party and NZ First — have said they oppose it.

In a statement, the populist NZ First said they could not support the law given the “colossal failure” of the legislation in Australia, while ACT said they believed the law “won’t work”, and teenagers would easily get around the ban.

Australia last year banned under 16s from the likes of Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, in a crackdown designed to protect children from online bullying and “predatory algorithms”.

A team of Australia-based researchers in a peer-reviewed study published in June found little evidence to suggest teenagers have turned away from social media as a consequence, however.

World.title: 'Monstrous, mindless': Chidambaram criticises 'One Nation, One Election' plan at House panel meet
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former union minister

has opposed the proposed âOne Nation, One Electionâ framework before a joint parliamentary committee, calling the initiative âunconstitutionalâ, âmonstrousâ and âmindlessâ.

Chidambaram, who appeared before the panel examining the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, argued that synchronising Lok Sabha and state assembly elections could violate the constitutional framework governing elected legislatures.

Sources, quoted by news agency PTI, said the former home and finance minister told the panel that since legislatures are elected for five-year terms, curtailing their tenure would amount to a violation of the basic structure of the Constitution.

Chidambaram also said his conscience did not allow him to support the proposed legislation and argued that the government does not have the required two-thirds majority to pass the bills, sources told PTI.

The Congress leader described the proposal to hold nationwide elections simultaneously as a âmindlessâ exercise and strongly opposed the governmentâs push for simultaneous polls.

Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Sagarika Ghosh, who is also a member of the committee, separately opposed the bills.





Ghosh said the proposal could give âunbridledâ power to the Election Commission, sources said.

The joint committee, headed by BJP MP PP Chaudhary, also heard representations from around 10 Padma awardees, including Tarlochan Singh, Navin Khanna, Meenakshi Jain and Niru Kumar. While some supported simultaneous elections, others opposed the proposal, warning that it could lead to âchaosâ in the country.

The two bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024 and subsequently referred to the joint committee for detailed examination.

The proposal followed recommendations from a high-level committee headed by former president Ram Nath Kovind, which suggested holding Lok Sabha, state assembly and local body elections simultaneously in a phased manner. Union Home Minister Amit Shah was also a member of the panel.

India had earlier held Lok Sabha and state assembly elections together from 1951-52 through 1967. The cycle was disrupted after premature dissolutions of some state assemblies in 1968 and 1969, followed by the early dissolution of the Fourth Lok Sabha in 1970 and fresh general elections in 1971.

Since then, staggered election cycles have become the norm, with several Lok Sabha and state assembly terms ending before their full five-year tenure.

World.title: Why Vijay scrapped Chennai’s second airport plan at Parandur
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday announced that his government would abandon the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur, saying the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents.

The announcement was made in the assembly as Vijay said Chennai still needed a new airport to meet rising passenger demand, industrial growth and increasing cargo movement. However, he said the new airport should be located at a site where agricultural and residential areas would face minimal disruption.

"To fulfill the promise I made to the people that day... the steps taken to establish a new airport in Parandur will be abandoned by this government," Vijay said.

The government is now considering alternative locations and plans to conduct technical feasibility studies before finalising a new site.

Why Vijay rejected Parandur

Vijay said he had visited Eganapuram and other villages on January 20, 2025, and heard the grievances of residents protesting against the proposed airport in Parandur and 12 surrounding villages.

"I stand firmly with the people protesting against the airport to be established in Chennai's Parandur and 12 surrounding villages," he said.





The chief minister said farmers were the backbone of the country and backed those protesting to protect their agricultural land.

Vijay said he had also opposed the Parandur project at a public meeting in Vikravandi in October 2024, while making clear that he supported industrial development and the role of airports in it.

"However, this project should not be located in Parandur. The government must reconsider this project," he said.

He added that an alternative site should be identified where the impact on agricultural land and people's livelihoods would be minimal.

Chennai airport to be expanded

While dropping Parandur, the government said Chennai's existing airport would be expanded.

Vijay said the Meenambakkam airport, operated by the Airports Authority of India, currently has the capacity to handle around 30 million passengers annually. With the under-construction Terminal 3 becoming operational, capacity is expected to rise to 34 million passengers a year.

The government plans to expand the airport on its north-western side by constructing a fifth terminal, which is expected to handle another 20 million passengers annually.

The government is also considering alternative sites for a new airport, with technical feasibility studies to be conducted by expert teams.

Why Parandur was chosen

The Parandur project had received in-principle approval from the Civil Aviation Ministry in April 2025 for an International Greenfield Airport in Kancheepuram district.

The proposed project had faced opposition from residents of villages that were expected to be affected by land acquisition and construction.

However, the DMK has criticised the decision to abandon the project, arguing that it could hurt Tamil Nadu's industrial growth and investment prospects.

Former chief minister and DMK president MK Stalin said dropping the project would set the state's development back by several years.

"The announcement made today by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu to drop the Parandur International Airport project will set the state's development back by several years. Tamil Nadu's interests cannot be mortgaged for petty political considerations," Stalin said.

He also called the decision a setback to employment opportunities for Tamil Nadu's youth.

DMK warns of economic fallout

Former Tamil Nadu minister and DMK MLA Thangam Thennarasu also criticised the decision, saying the Parandur site was selected after studying options for establishing two runways.

"Possibilities for setting up two runways were all studied and only then Parandur was selected," he said.

Thennarasu argued that scrapping the project for political reasons could hurt the state's economy and push industries towards neighbouring Andhra Pradesh.

"It would be best to have the airport at Parandur. Dropping the Parandur Airport project for political reasons will cause economic damage," he said.

"Many industries will move towards Andhra Pradesh.

We have already lost the Hosur Airport," he added.

Thennarasu also said compensation had already been provided to people whose land was acquired for the project and cited the Land Acquisition Act while arguing that the acquired land should be used for its intended purpose.

DMK stages assembly walkout

The announcement triggered an immediate confrontation in the Tamil Nadu Assembly, with DMK MLAs staging a walkout after Speaker JCD Prabhakar denied DMK leader KN Nehru permission to respond to the statement, citing Assembly rules.

The opposition accused the government of making a policy U-turn that could affect Tamil Nadu's industrial momentum and prospects of attracting investment.

Vijay, however, maintained that the government supports airport-led industrial development but believes the proposed airport should not come at the cost of agricultural land and people's livelihoods.

World.title: Kashmiri Pandits under PM Package flag fresh threats; seek security
World.content:
A fresh threat letter was allegedly circulated on social media targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees serving in the Kashmir Valley, prompting the All PM Package Employees Forum Kashmir to seek enhanced security from the Jammu and Kashmir administration.

In a letter to chief secretary of Jammu and Kashmir on Monday, the forum said the purported threat poster, allegedly issued by an outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC) and dated August 23, contains the names, addresses and vehicle numbers of some employees.

The forum said the authenticity of the poster has not yet been verified by police or security agencies but warned that its repeated circulation was a matter of âgrave concernâ.

In its letter, the forum said, "The authenticity of the poster is yet to be verified by the Police and security agencies. However, the repeated circulation of such threat letters and posters, particularly those containing sensitive personal information, is a matter of grave concern.

World.title: Parul University marks 80th Independence Day with former CJI Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai as chief guest
World.content:
Vadodara based Parul University (PU) marked the spirit of Indiaâs 80th

with Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai, the Former Chief Justice of India, as the chief guest, bringing together university leaders, faculty members, students and staff for a gathering centered on the nationâs path of freedom, solidarity and advancement.

The celebrations commenced with the hoisting of the National Flag at PU Circle followed by the National Anthem, creating a solemn and patriotic beginning of the event. The gathering reflected the collective involvement from the university community in commemorating the nationâs Independence.

During the special session, Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai shared his views on the significance of Independence Day, the values that live inside the Constitution, and the responsibility of citizens in contributing towards the nationâs continued progress.

Addressing the audience he said, âLet justice guide your choices. Let equality shape your understanding of society. Let liberty inform your defense of rights.

And let fraternity deepen your concerns for others.â Further while communicating with the young aspiring lawyers in the audience he said, âLawyers are equally important custodians of the constitutional order. Your career will ultimately be measured not only by the positions that you occupy or the cases that you win but also by the values you uphold.â

Â âI am honoured to participate in the celebrations at Parul University", said Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai

Expressing his gratitude and congratulating everyone on India's 79 years of Independence and 80th Independence day he further added, âI am honoured to participate in the celebrations at Parul University." He said, "Independence Day is not only an occasion to commemorate Indiaâs freedom from colonial rule, but also an opportunity to reflect on the constitutional promises of liberty, equality, justice and fraternity.

â He connected the freedom struggle with the Constitution, explaining that the struggle was also against inequality, discrimination, exploitation and the erosion of human dignity.

The celebrations included a march past by NCC cadets, highlighting themes of unity, integrity and discipline. The programme also featured cultural performances, including patriotic songs, dances and thematic presentations. Students brought Indiaâs cultural diversity to life through acts that carried messages of national unity, selfless service and social harmony along with engaging theatrical performances.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Parul Patel, Vice President (Student Affairs and General Administration) and Chairperson (Admissions Committee), Parul University said, âIndependence Day is an opportunity to help our youth understand the value of freedom, that the freedom we celebrate comes with a responsibility to contribute to the nationâs progress. At Parul University, we believe that education must go beyond classrooms to nurture young individuals who are conscious of their responsibilities, respect the values of our Constitution, and have the confidence and conviction to contribute meaningfully to society and the nation.

World.title: JPSC 'irregularities': Supreme Court issues notice to Centre, state after CBI probe plea

World.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy returns to Hyderabad, likely to address controversy over denied US visit
World.content:
Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy returned to Hyderabad on Monday (August 24, 2026) morning, cutting short his overseas visit, originally scheduled to cover London, United Kingdom, and the United States.

Mr. Reddy spent three days in London but could not proceed to the United States after the Centre denied permission for the second leg of his tour. The Chief Minister and the Congress party have attributed the decision to political considerations.

Soon after landing in Hyderabad, Mr. Reddy got down to official work and convened a meeting with all government Secretaries.

CM Revanth likely to address US visit controversy

Mr. Reddy is expected to speak on the controversy surrounding the denial of permission for his US visit, either on Monday or Tuesday. The Chief Minister is likely to question the Centre’s decision and maintain that his proposed U.S. tour was focused on engaging with leading educational institutions and attracting them to establish partnerships in Telangana.

Mr. Reddy had earlier thanked All India Congress Committee (AICC) president Mallikarjun Kharge for his support on the issue. Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge and Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka had also publicly backed the Chief Minister and criticised the Centre’s decision to deny permission for the U.S. leg of his tour

Political controversy

Meanwhile, several Congress leaders, including Ministers, MLAs and MLCs, are also expected to meet the Chief Minister and press for disciplinary action against Endowments Minister Konda Surekha. She has been at the centre of a controversy following remarks made by her daughter, Konda Susmitha, against the Chief Minister at an event in Warangal. The Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) subsequently issued a show cause notice to Ms. Surekha, seeking her explanation.

In her response, Ms. Surekha urged the party to withdraw the notice, arguing that she should not be held responsible for the actions of her daughter. However, she did not condemn her daughter’s remarks against the Chief Minister.

The issue escalated while Mr. Reddy was in the UK, with more than 20 Congress MLAs and MLCs holding a press conference in Hyderabad to demand action against Ms Surekha. SC Welfare Minister Adluri Lakshman went a step further and sought her removal from the Cabinet.

Konda Surekha meets AICC president

A day before the Chief Minister’s return, Ms. Surekha reportedly met All India Congress Committee (AICC) president Mallikarjun Kharge. Details of the meeting, however, were not made public.

Silence of senior Ministers

The controversy has also highlighted the unusual silence of several senior Ministers, who have refrained from publicly commenting on the episode. Instead, it was largely younger legislators, including first-time MLAs, who rallied behind the Chief Minister and spoke out against Ms. Surekha. The TPCC president Mahesh Kumar Goud made it clear that those crossing the limits would not be spared irrespective of their position, sending a strong warning to leaders targeting the government.

World.title: Centre’s denial of US visit clearance an insult to Telangana;  proposed meetings were clearly mentioned: CM Revanth Reddy
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy termed the Centre’s refusal to grant political clearance for his proposed visit to the United States an insult to Telangana and alleged that the decision reflected discrimination against the Telugu State.

Mr. Reddy said the State government had provided detailed information to the Centre about the purpose and objectives of his proposed foreign visit, which was part of the TelanganaRising 2047 initiative. “Information was provided to the Centre. The purpose of the visit and the proposed meetings were clearly mentioned. If the proposal of a Chief Minister is rejected without properly reviewing the information and collecting the necessary details, can such a decision be taken without the knowledge of the Prime Minister?” he asked, addressing a press conference held in Hyderabad on Monday (August 24, 2026).

Explaining the arrangements normally made for official foreign visits, Mr. Reddy said Indian missions abroad facilitate meetings for Chief Ministers and Union Ministers travelling officially. He rejected the argument that he planned to meet some critics of India in the USA, and said it is the Indian missions that facilitate meeting.

The Chief Minister also questioned the Centre’s approach by citing the foreign visits of Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. He said Mr. Patel had recently undertaken an eight-day visit to the U.S. and Canada to promote the Vibrant Gujarat 2047 initiative and attract investments to the State.

“If the Gujarat Chief Minister can travel to the US and Canada to promote Vibrant Gujarat 2047 and meet investors, why was the U.S. visit of the Telangana Chief Minister denied when it was proposed for similar purposes under TelanganaRising 2047?” Mr. Reddy asked.

Questioning the Centre’s approach, Mr. Reddy said Telangana should not be treated as a lesser State. “Is Telangana being looked down upon? Is there discrimination against Telangana?” he asked. He alleged that attempts were being made to obstruct Telangana’s development initiatives, particularly its efforts to attract investments and establish partnerships with leading global educational and sports institutions.

He appealed to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders criticising him to condemn the Centre’s decision, as they were elected from the State, and the State’s interests should be paramount. He also urged the media to bring the issue to the attention of the people. “This is not an insult to Revanth Reddy personally. It is an insult to the people of Telangana and the Telangana State government,” he said.

Mr. Reddy said the government would continue with its TelanganaRising 2047 programme despite the denial of permission for his U.S. visit. He announced that the State government had decided to organise the TelanganaRising 2047 programme on December 7, 8 and 9, including an investment summit aimed at attracting investments and showcasing the State’s opportunities to global investors.

World.title: Mandya: Over ₹8 lakh cash found in beggar’s house after her death
World.content:
More than ₹8 lakh in cash has been found in the rented house of an elderly woman who survived by begging in Guthalu locality of Mandya, following her death on Sunday (August 23, 2026).

The deceased has been identified as Hoor-Un-Nisa, who had been living alone since the death of her unmarried sister two years ago. The two sisters had reportedly lived together for several decades and depended largely on alms for their livelihood.

After Hoor-Un-Nisa died of age-related ailments, local residents and community leaders entered the house to make arrangements for her funeral. During a search of the premises, they reportedly discovered more than 30 bags containing cash and other valuables.

Community volunteers and leaders initially opened some of the bags and counted around ₹8 lakh in cash. Nearly 20 bags are yet to be opened and counted, raising the possibility that the total cash could be considerably higher.

The recovered money has been kept at a local mosque in Guthalu for safekeeping. Community leaders have also contacted the deceased woman’s surviving relatives.

The remaining bags are expected to be opened and the cash officially counted in the presence of the relatives, officials and community representatives. A decision on the lawful handover of the money will be taken after the rightful claimant to the funds is established.

World.title: Heavy rain lashed several parts of Delhi; portion of building under construction collapses
World.content:
A portion of a dilapidated building collapsed in the Chandni Mahal area here, amid heavy rainfall in the national Capital on Monday (August 24, 2026), damaging three to four two-wheelers, police said.

After the Chandni Mahal police station received a PCR call about the collapse at 1569, Pahari Bhojla dispatched a police team, which reached the spot and secured the area.

Police said they shifted people present at the site to a safe location and removed vehicles lying under or near the debris. No injuries were reported, they said, adding that the building was in a dilapidated condition.

According to police, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) had already issued a notice regarding the building’s condition, and repair work was underway when the collapse happened.

Police said necessary action is being taken in coordination with the MCD authorities.

Heavy rain lashed several parts of Delhi, leading to waterlogging and traffic disruptions at multiple locations.

World.title: Karnataka: Tiger sighted in forest area in Kishkindha hills of Koppal after nearly five decades
World.content:
A tiger has been camera-trapped in the Kishkindha hills of Koppal district, nearly five decades after the big cat was last reported in the forest area of the region, prompting the Forest Department to step up vigilance and alert local communities.

Wildlife experts said the tiger may have been frequenting the hill forests for several months and could have entered the area through a wildlife corridor connecting it to the Srisailam landscape in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh.

The Forest Department began monitoring the area after receiving repeated reports from residents over the past three months of a tiger moving around the Yelugudda region. Camera traps were installed at strategic locations in the hills. One of the cameras, placed at Temba, captured the tiger moving through the area on Sunday (August 23, 2026), confirming its presence.

Alert sounded

Following the sighting, the Forest Department has sounded an alert in Hampi and surrounding areas. Sirens have been sounded in Sanapur, Basapur, Jabbalagudda, Benakal, Agoli, Venkatagi, Hanumanahalli and Junglirangapur, warning residents, shepherds and cattle grazers against entering the Yelugudda forest area.

People have also been advised not to venture into the forest alone or sleep outdoors at night. The department has asked residents to immediately report any fresh sighting or information about the tiger.

Additional forest personnel have been deployed in the Yelugudda area over the past three days, while more camera traps are being installed to track the animal’s movements and ascertain when and from where it entered the landscape.

World.title: No shortage of sugar in India, retail prices to come down: industry body ISMA
World.content:
Sugar industry's apex body ISMA on Monday (August 24, 2026) asserted that there is no shortage of sugar in the country and prices in the retail market are expected to come down.

Addressing a press conference, Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) President Niraj Shirgaokar said the prices have risen due to various factors, including speculative buying by traders and bulk consumers as well as lower production because of the bad weather conditions.

The ISMA president also categorically said that mills were not involved in creating artificial scarcity and jacking up the ex-mill prices.

Mr. Shirgaokar said the prices have started to ease following the government's decision to allow duty-free imports of 1 million tonnes of raw sugar.

"India does not have a sugar shortage," Mr. Shirgaokar told reporters in New Delhi.

He said the closing stock of sugar at the end of September would be 35 lakh tonnes.

Moreover, the ISMA president said that the mills would start operations by around October 15 and produce around 10-12 lakh tonnes in the month of October.

The demand for the month of October would be 24-25 lakh tonnes, he added.

World.title: Delhi airport sees 15 flight diversions due to bad weather
World.content:
At least 15 flights were diverted at the Delhi airport on Monday (August 24, 2026) due to inclement weather conditions, according to an official.

Scores of flights were delayed, and some were cancelled at the Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA) in the national capital due to the bad weather.

Rains lashed the national capital and thunderstorms, lightning and winds of 30-40 kmph are also expected in parts of the city.

The official said 12 flights were diverted to Jaipur, two to Chandigarh and one to Lucknow.

IndiGo, in a post on X, said bad weather in the national capital has impacted flight schedules and that the airline was closely monitoring the weather.

Travel Advisory



Bad weather over #Delhi has impacted flight schedules. We are closely monitoring the weather and doing our best to get you where you need to be, safely and smoothly.



If you're travelling today, we recommend checking your flight status on our website via… — IndiGo (@IndiGo6E) August 24, 2026

"Adverse weather conditions may impact flight operations to and from Delhi today," Air India said in a post on X.

#TravelAdvisory



Adverse weather conditions may impact flight operations to and from Delhi today.



To ensure a smooth travel experience, we encourage our passengers to check the latest flight status at the following link before heading to the airport: https://t.co/5vemTROi62… — Air India (@airindia) August 24, 2026

Data from flight tracking website Flightradar24.com showed that over 280 services were delayed and more than 20 flights were cancelled at the airport.

IGIA handles more than 1,300 flight movements daily.

World.title: Iran’s rial currency hits new record low as U.S. prepares to announce more sanctions
World.content:
Iran's currency hit a record low Monday (August 24, 2026) as Washington prepared to announce new sanctions it said would add further pressure on an economy already battered by previous sanctions and a U.S. naval blockade.

The rial dropped to 2.02 million to the U.S. dollar as trading opened on currency markets. Iran's official Central Bank rate stood at around 1.5 million rial to the dollar, but the market rate is what most Iranians pay.

The currency had already been under pressure before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, as Iran faced double-digit inflation and negative growth, but has repeatedly hit new lows as nearly six months of war have taken an even greater toll.

Iranians find daily staples increasingly unaffordable. Since the war began, rice is up some 60%, and prices of beef are more than 150% higher. The International Monetary Fund forecasts that GDP will contract more than 5%.

Still, economic pressure has not yet translated into political pressure. Iran retains a key strategic advantage: Its attacks and threats on ships in the Strait of Hormuz have brought traffic in the vital waterway to a near halt, damaging the world economy and heaping pressure on U.S. President Donald Trump ahead of congressional elections.

The war, as a result, has devolved into a fight over who controls the strait, through which a fifth of the world's traded oil transited before the conflict. Iran is now refusing to fully reopen it unless it can charge ships.

Iran and Oman, which are on opposite sides of the strait, are reportedly in the final stages of agreeing upon a plan for joint management of the waterway. Oman's Foreign Minister is set to visit Iran on Tuesday (August 25).

In an attempt to break the impasse, Trump's administration promised that even stronger sanctions than those already in place would be announced Monday (August 25), including secondary sanctions on countries that continue to do business with Iran.

“President Trump decimated Iran's economy to a point where the rial has never been weaker, and inflation has rarely been higher,” U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote Sunday (August 23) in an opinion piece in the Financial Times.

“The regime's final refuge now lies in the self-deception of fearful nations that still believe accommodating aggression can secure a durable peace.” Already last week, the United Arab Emirates announced that it was suspending all trade with Iran. The UAE has long been one of Iran's largest trading partners and its biggest source of imports.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei told reporters in Tehran on Monday (August 24) that “any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences." “Our hands are not tied,” he added.

Pakistan, which played a key role in brokering a 60-day ceasefire in June, sent a high-level delegation to Iran on Monday (August 25) to discuss ending the war, the military said.

In downtown Tehran, 73-year-old Sadegh Mahmoudi did not hold out hope for a resolution. He joined a line of about a dozen people to purchase U.S. dollars with his remaining savings to hedge against further declines.

“There is no hope for a deal and peace,” he said.

World.title: CDF Munir, Naqvi in Iran as part of Pakistan's efforts for regional peace
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi reached Tehran on Monday, Iranian media reported after Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) described the visit “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”.

State media in Pakistan, meanwhile, reported that CDF Munir and Naqvi had held a meeting with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni.

Earlier, ISPR said CDF Munir will “focus on promoting efforts towards peaceful, lasting and comprehensive resolution of the conflict in the Middle East” during the visit.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei on Sunday said CDF Munir was expected to travel to Tehran to continue efforts to bring peace and security to the region.

He said CDF Munir would lead an official delegation and the “visit aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Iran and Pakistan and to continue Pakis­tan’s good offices in support of peace and security in the region”.

During the visit, CDF Munir would meet and hold talks with senior officials Iran, Baqaei added.

The United States and Israel triggered the Middle East war with a massive wave of strikes against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region.

An April 8 ceasefire ended nearly 40 days of intense bombardment, but control over the Strait of Hormuz soon emerged as a key flashpoint in the conflict.

Iran has controlled the vital energy conduit since the war began. Reopening the strait, vital for global oil and gas supplies, has become a US priority, but Tehran insists the waterway will remain closed until Washington lifts its naval blockade on Iranian ports, removes oil sanctions and unfreezes Iranian assets abroad.

Pakistan has played a key role in efforts to halt war between Iran and the United States, brokering a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in June, but peace negotiations currently appear stalled.

Last week, US President Donald Trump announced that Washington would ramp up economic pressure on Iran “on an unprecedented scale”.

Washington has urged other governments, including Beijing, to join efforts to further isolate Iran’s economy.

The US is expected to announce details related to the planned sanctions on Mondau, which ​US officials have ​said would be “ the ⁠toughest sanctions in history ” on Iran.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Moody's lifts Pakistan sovereign rating to B3 from Caa1, cites governance improvement and easing of external risk
World.content:
Global ratings agency Moody’s lifted Pakistan’s sovereign rating to ‘B3’ from ‘Caa1’ on Monday, citing improvements in governance and easing external vulnerability risks.

The agency maintained the country’s outlook at ‘stable’.

“We expect the recent improvement in Pakistan’s debt affordability to be durable, underpinned by sustained macroeconomic stability,” the agency said in a statement.

Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad also shared the development in a post on X.

“After S&P, Moody’s also upgrades Pakistan Sovereign Ratings to B3 from Caa1,” he wrote.

The development comes only a month after S&P Global Ratings upgraded Pakistan’s long-term sovereign credit rating to ‘B’ from ‘B-’, citing an improving external position and gradual macroeconomic stabilisation, while also assigning a stable outlook.

A country’s sovereign credit rating serves as an indicator of its financial health for foreign investors. It assesses creditworthiness — the risk involved in lending money to the country, evaluated by its ability to repay its debts. Upgrading this rating gives global lenders greater confidence in the economy, helping the country attract foreign investment and borrow funds on better terms.

More to follow.

World.title: Mir Raza murder case: Victim's family moves SHC against judicial commission formation, seeks JIT for probe
World.content:
KARACHI: The family of Mir Raza Ali — a 25-year-old Karachi-based businessman who was found dead with a gunshot wound last month — moved the Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday against the provincial government’s decision to form a judicial commission for a review of the probe into his murder case.

The development took place as the Sindh government implemented its decision announced on Sunday, despite objections by Ali’s family and lawyer.

Judicial correspondence to this effect, dated August 24 and seen Dawn, said the SHC chief justice had appointed Justice Omar Sial to head the commission.

Meanwhile, Ali’s family filed a petition in the SHC through their lawyer, Jibran Nasir, requesting it to set aside the decision to form the commission and constitute a joint investigation team (JIT) instead.

The petition, a copy of which is available with Dawn, named 19 respondents, including the Sindh government, Sindh Home Department, the provincial inspector general of police, Karachi additional inspector general of police, the Federation of Pakistan and the defence ministry.

The petitioners requested the court to set aside the Sindh government’s decision to form a judicial commission, including “any subsequent proceedings arising from it”.

Instead, they sought the court’s directives for the formation of an “independent, impartial and multi-agency JIT, including members from Sindh police, Rangers, Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), and military intelligence, with a senior officer of unimpeachable integrity who has had no previous involvement” in the case appointed as its head.

The plea contended that the head must conduct a “fresh and comprehensive investigation into the abduction, torture and murder” of Ali.

It further sought the court’s directives for the yet-to-be-formed JIT to “independently investigate the possibility of extortion, ransom, organised criminal activity, business/financial dispute or any other motive, and shall determine on the basis of evidence whether the facts attract any provision of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, including the applicability of Section 19 thereof”,

The court may also direct the JIT to investigate the conduct of two police officials — East Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Farrukh Ali Lanjar and Sharea Faisal Deputy Superintendent of Police Arshad Afridi, both of whom have been named as respondents in the plea — as well as of “any other police officer involved in the investigation to determine if their conducts constitutes offence under Section 166(2), 201 and 218 PPC”, the petition said.

The petitioners further requested the court to instruct the Sindh government to initiate an independent departmental fact-finding inquiry against members of a previous investigation team in the case and “all other officers whose responsibility emerges, on the terms of reference (TORs) proposed by the petitioners and/or such modified TORs as this honourable court may deem appropriate”.

They asked the court to “direct that the departmental inquiry and criminal investigation into the conduct of the concerned police officials shall proceed independently and simultaneously in accordance with law”.

The petitioners also requested the immediate suspension of DIG Lanjar, Crime Investigation Agency Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Samiullah, East SSP Zubair Nazir Shaikh, East Superintendent of Police Usman Sadozai and Ferozabad and the Ferozabad SIO, as well as their removal from their postings pending the murder case probe.

They also sought a departmental inquiry into their conduct to “preserve the integrity of the investigation and inquiry”.

Moreover, the petitioners asked the court to restrain the Rapid Response Force and the Crime Investigation branch DIG from “submitting the final challan/chargesheet” in the case during the pendency of their plea.

They further requested the court to restrain the learned judicial magistrate XXI Karachi East from treating any report filed by the two as the final challan/ chargesheet under Section 173 CrPC during the pendency of this petition”.

The petitioners contended that the judicial commission was “neither empowered to conduct a criminal investigation nor submit a charge sheet” and could not be presented as an alternative to already available effective alternatives such as JIT.

The petition stated that the formation of a judicial commission without disclosing the TORs and the mandate seemed like an “attempt to scapegoat the honourable judiciary by burdening it with failures of the previous and instant investigation team while also forcing upon it the responsibility to solve the case”.

The petition stated that the circumstances surrounding the investigation had shown that an “ordinary investigative mechanism has failed to satisfactorily establish even the fundamental circumstances surrounding the abduction, torture and murder of Mir Raza Ali Khan, while serious allegations have simultaneously emerged concerning the manner in which the earlier investigation was conducted”.

It said that the previous investigation team had “prematurely adopted and propagated a theory of sucide, failed to record statements of the seven immediate family, failed to presever and properly handle material physical and digital evidence, failed to secure relevant CCTV footage, mishandled the deceased’s smart watch, and failed to appropriately respond to material medico-legal concerns which ultimately resulted in the final medical opinion expressly excluding suicide”.

The petitioners said the prevailing circumstances surrounding the case had brought into question the investigation process.

Petitioners sought the constitution of an independent JIT “comprising officers who have had no previous involvement in the case and possessing appropriate forensic, digital, financial, telecommunications and field-investigation expertise”.

The hearing

Later in the day, a two-judge bench, comprising Justice Adnan-ul-Karim Memon, heard the petition and issued notices to the respondents as well as Sindh advocate general for August 31.

During the hearing, the petitioner’s counsel contended that police investigation had not yet reached any conclusion.

“We learned from the media that the Sindh government was forming a judicial commission,” Nasir informed the court. He held that formation of a judicial commission at this stage of the investigation could adversely impact the case.

Speaking to the media after the hearing, Nasir said that the court had barred the police from submitting its final report until a decision is made on the plea.

He added that the court has also sought the terms and conditions of the judicial commission and a report from the police over the “negligence and carelessness” on the part of the police officials in the case.

The case

Ali, a 25-year-old businessman and a graduate of the Institute of Business Administration, was found dead with a gunshot wound on July 29 in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar a day after he was reported missing.

While his family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police were initially building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

A murder charge was eventually added to the first information report (FIR) after the exhumation and a second post-mortem of Ali’s body revealed that he had suffered multiple injuries and was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide.

The second autopsy was conducted after a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination.

On August 6, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Sumaiyya Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8.

A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered.

The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team.

On Aug 19, Ali’s parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam Hussain, wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, seeking his “direct supervision of the murder investigation” into the slain business owner’s death.

They also urged the chief minister to order an investigation and departmental inquiry into the previous investigation team and immediately suspend the officers involved.

On Sunday, the provincial government acknowledged the letter and announced decision to form a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and in accordance with the law.

However, soon after the announcement, the counsel for Ali’s family raised objections and said they would approach the SHC in the matter.

The family’s counsel held that the family was not informed of the commission, its TORs were not disclosed and that the police were yet to submit an investigation report before the magistrate.

In a video message, Ali’s sister said the family came to know about the Sindh government’s decision through the media.

Raising similar objections and questions as those by Nasir, she said: “On August 24, the police are to submit their report. But if there is no report yet, on what basis are they making this decision?”

“We, as a family, are not standing for this decision. We have been saying this since the beginning that we do not trust how the proceedings are going on.”

World.title: In meeting with IMO chief, Dar calls for 'urgent intervention' for return of Pakistani sailors held by Somali pirates
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met the International Maritime Organisation’s head and called for “urgent and effective institutional intervention” for the return of 10 Pakistani sailors held captive by Somali pirates, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO).

Dar met IMO Secretary General Arsenio Dominguez in London, where he is on a four-day visit.

He also thanked Dominguez for his support for the ongoing efforts to secure the safe release of the 10 Pakistani seafarers, the FO statement said.

The seafarers were among the crew of MT Honour 25 — a Palau-flagged oil tanker — that was hijacked by armed pirates off the coast of Puntland, Somalia on April 21, 2026.

Four months later, there has been no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages, despite concerns abounding about their declining health.

Since the hijacking, the crew has made several emotional videos and audio appeals , while reporting that they have run out of clean water, food and medicine.

The hostages are victims of an “ ownership crisis ”, as it is not clearly established who owns the ship, and the man previously thought to be the owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them.

Besides 10 Pakistanis, the crew members also include seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan.

Dar reaffirms Pakistan commitment to IMO

In his meeting with Dominguez, Dar also reaffirmed Pakistan’s “longstanding commitment” to IMO and appreciated its role as the principal international regulatory body for safe, secure and efficient international shipping, the FO statement said.

He highlighted Pakistan’s continued efforts to strengthen maritime governance, implement international maritime standards, and further develop its blue economy, the statement added.

The two sides also discussed further strengthening Pakistan-IMO cooperation in maritime safety, security, regulatory reforms, and the development of Pakistan’s maritime sector, according to FO.

World.title: Newly elected members of AJK Legislative Assembly take oath of office
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Newly elected members of the AJK Legislative Assembly were administered the oath of office by outgoing Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar on Monday.

Assembly Secretary Amjed Latif Abbasi read out the notifications of the 38 members elected from the territorial and refugee constituencies in the phased elections, as well as those of the eight members elected by them on reserved seats.

Shortly after the announcement of the results, all newly elected members took the oath at the hands of the outgoing speaker, who failed to retain his seat in the elections. The members then signed the oath register in the order of their constituencies.

PML-N’s Ahmed Raza Qadri moved a motion seeking the suspension of the rules that prescribed a bar on certain times for elections to the offices of speaker, deputy speaker and leader of the house.

On a point of order, PPP’s Abdul Majid Khan noted that although the PML-N had a majority and could suspend the rules, it should avoid holding the session on the 12th of Rabi-ul-Awwal — Eid-i-Miladun Nabi, widely commemorated as the birthday of Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him) — out of respect for the sanctity of the day.

The chair, however, said there was no harm in holding the session and conducting the election process on that day.

“The transition of power should take place as early as possible, and it is good that on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, members will pay tributes to the Holy Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) from the floor of the house,” he said, amid desk-thumping by PML-N legislators.

PML-N wins 5, PPP wins 2 reserved seats

The PML-N bagged five while the PPP won two of the seven reserved seats that were up for grabs in the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly on Monday.

Under Article 22(1) of the AJK Constitution, the Legislative Assembly consists of 53 members, including 45 members elected directly through adult franchise and eight members chosen by directly elected representatives.

The reserved seats include five seats for women and one each for Ulema-i-Din or Mashaikh well-versed in the teachings of Islam, Jammu and Kashmir State subjects residing abroad, and technocrats and other professionals.

PML-N’s Chaudhry Abdul Rehman Arain was the only candidate to have submitted his nomination papers for the seat reserved for state subjects residing abroad. He was consequently declared elected unopposed.

After polling for the remaining seats on Monday, PML-N’s Sehrish Qamar, Maryam Idrees and Maryam Zaman, also known as Maryam Kashmiri, secured one seat each reserved for women. Seven votes were polled for each of them, as were for PPP’s Farzana Yaqoob, who claimed the fourth reserved seat for women.

There were just two more contenders — PML-N’s Riffat Abid and PPP’s Zobia Khurshid Raja — vying for the seats for women whose votes were tied at five. Eventually, Raja was declared the winner for the last seat left, with the result being decided by drawing lots.

For the seat reserved for Ulema and Mashaikh, PML-N’s Mohammad Mazhar Saeed won against his sole contender, PPP’s Hafiz Tariq Mahmood, after garnering 26 votes — almost double than Mahmood’s 12.

Similarly, PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Gillani also bagged 26 votes to claim the seat reserved for technocrats and professionals, beating PPP’s Sahibzada Zulfiqar Ali by 14 votes.

Shortly after their election, the Election Commission notified the successful candidates.

In days preceding Monday’s polls, elections to seven of the 45 directly elected seats — five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district — could not be held due to the law and order situation in the region. As a result, the 38 members elected so far, representing 84.4 per cent of the directly elected membership, participated in the reserved seat elections.

AJK polls

The elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were divided into phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10.

The third phase was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.

So far, in the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N has secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party has also joined hands with the PML-N.

The PPP has alleged widespread rigging in the polls, with the party also ramping up its criticism of the ruling PML-N in recent days.

Last week, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said that a genuine alliance with the PML-N was not possible until their grievances regarding the AJK polls were addressed as he established formal contact with the PTI and offered to cooperate with the party in Parliament.

Speaking to the media, the PPP chairman alleged that the AJK election process had been made controversial for political interests. He alleged that the federal government’s political and administrative machinery had remained active in AJK throughout the six-phase election process, raising serious questions over its transparency.

The PPP, he said, had raised its objections before the Election Commission, parliament and other constitutional forums, but the PML-N had failed to address its concerns or engage in meaningful dialogue after the polls.

Moreover, he said the commitments and political understandings reached with the PML-N before the prime minister’s election had not been honoured. The PPP had cooperated in the wider national interest, he said, but there could be no genuine alliance with the PML-N unless the party’s concerns over the AJK elections were addressed and political commitments fulfilled.

He pointed out that the government needed PPP’s votes for several important laws, constitutional amendments and difficult bills. He said legislation could not be forced through on the basis of a majority or through coercion.

The discord between the PPP and PML-N was also apparent in the National Assembly on Aug 18, when the former managed to compel the government to virtually suspend the heavy legislative agenda for the day, which included 21 bills.

On Aug 20, when the lower house of Parliament passed two bills pertaining to the military and nuclear command structure, the PPP also objected to the manner in which the legislation was presented. While the party ultimately voted in favour of the bills, Bilawal lashed out at the government for not taking ruling allies on board.

World.title: 'Imran would not have spent 3 years in jail if he wanted to make a deal,' says PTI's Gohar
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday brushed aside speculation regarding a deal with the government, saying party founder Imran Khan would not have spent three years in jail if he wanted to make a deal.

He made the remarks while speaking outside the Supreme Court (SC) alongside PTI leader Sardar Latif Khosa after the two met with the court’s registrar.

“Khan sahib does not make deals. He will not stay in the hospital a minute more than is necessary for his tests and treatment. If he had to make a deal, he would not have spent three years in jail,” Gohar said.

“All we have to say is that there should be no politics on his health,” he said.

During the press talk, Gohar said that he and Khosa had arrived at the SC to meet with Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi in connection with the party’s contempt petition against the government’s alleged violation of its Aug 18 order for shifting Imran to Shifa International Hospital.

“I asked to meet the chief justice. He was busy so it could not happen. Myself and Khosa sahib met the SC registrar and requested that a number be allotted to this case and it be fixed for hearing,” he said.

He said that the registrar had assured that a case number would be allotted to the contempt plea. Gohar said that they were also assured of the early fixation of the case before the SC.

“This [Aug 18 order] cannot be ignored. The whole world is looking at the SC and whether it is able to implement its order,” he said.

“We only wanted PTI founder’s medical tests to be conducted at a private hospital, with both his sister Uzma and his personal physician Dr Faisal Sultan included in the medical board examining him,” he said.

Meanwhile, Khosa said that a case number was being allotted to the was in Lahore.

Last week, Imran’s sister Uzma Khan had filed contempt petition before the SC against officials for flouting its Aug 18 order. The petition, filed by Advocate Uzair Karamat Bhandari on behalf of Dr Uzma, also requested the apex court to depute an officer or appoint a local commission to ensure that Imran was immediately shifted to the private hospital in accordance with its earlier directions.

Imran’s hospital transfer saga

Last week, the SC had ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board.

A three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibr­ahim issued the interim contempt petition, and quoted the registrar as saying that one of the judges directions on petitions seeking Imran’s hospitalisation, access to personal physicians and family members and provision of his medical record to his family.

The court had also ordered that Dr Uzma and Dr Sultan — Imran’s personal physician — be present during the medical check-up by a medical board.

At the same time, Imran’s family members, PTI members and lawyers associated with him were barred from disclosing his health condition or medical reports to the media or public until the next hearing.

The next day, the government had filed a review plea against the court’s order to shift Imran to the private hospital, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice.

However, the SC had returned the plea on Thursday with the objection that the contents of the affidavit and facts, along with the review petition filed under Article 188 of the Constitution, had not been properly drawn up and that one of the paper books was not in order.

The same night, elaborate arrangements were put in place in and around Shifa International Hospital, and all signs pointed to the PTI founder being brought there, in compliance with the SC order.

But, it became clear on Friday morning that Imran had been taken to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside Al Shifa Hospital” for the diversion.

In a post on X, he said, “In the light of the SC’s order, the prisoner was taken to the hospital under appropriate security arrangements during the night between August 20 and 21.

“A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist, and a physician, conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit,” he said.

Later, the Pims administration said that two specialists from Shifa Inter­national Hospital participated in Imran’s eye assessment, while other examinations were carried out by the concerned Pims specialists.

Imran has been taken to Pims multiple times after his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January.

“The clinical input arising from the ophthalmological assessment was taken into account alongside findings of the investigations conducted at Pims,” the statement said.

Meanwhile, the government on Thursday filed a fresh review petition against the SC’s Aug 18 order. The Islamabad chief commissioner again filed the plea, saying that his office had a direct, substantial and legally protected interest in the matter and that the Aug 18 order adversely affected its constitutional authority.

World.title: PM Shehbaz and Sindh CM 'agree to maintain political tolerance, consultation' amid rift in ruling coalition
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Monday, and both agreed to “maintain political tolerance and consultation”, the premier’s party, PML-N, posted on X.

The meeting comes amid an emerging rift between the PML-N and Murad’s PPP, allies in the Centre.

State broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported that the meeting took place in Islamabad while the PML-N said matters of mutual interest and political affairs were also discussed on the occasion.

The talks also covered Sindh-related matters and ongoing development projects, the PML-N’s X post stated.

Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema and Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik also attended the meeting.

The meeting takes place against the backdrop of the PPP expressing its grievances, particularly those related to recent elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The PML-N has come out as the winner in the polls that the PPP alleges were marred by rigging and irregularities.

Last week, the PPP also established formal contact with the opposition, with party Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari saying a genuine alliance with the ruling PML-N was not possible until their grievances regarding the AJK elections were addressed.

While the immediate focus during the meeting was parliamentary cooperation — from restoring the opposition’s participation in committees to pursuing electoral reforms — the meeting also carried a broader political undertone.
